kural.Translation: 'A' leads letters; the Ancient Lord Leads and lords the entire world
kural.explanation: As the letter A is the first of all letters, so the eternal God is first in the world
kural.couplet: A, as its first of letters, every speech maintains;The "Primal Deity" is first through all the world's domains

kural.Translation: That lore is vain which does not fall  At His good feet who knoweth all
kural.explanation: What Profit have those derived from learning, who worship not the good feet of Him who is possessed of pure knowledge ?
kural.couplet: No fruit have men of all their studied lore,Save they the 'Purely Wise One's' feet adore

kural.Translation: Long they live on earth who gain The feet of God in florid brain
kural.explanation: They who are united to the glorious feet of Him who passes swiftly over the flower of the mind, shall flourish long above all worlds
kural.couplet: His feet, 'Who o'er the full-blown flower hath past,' who gainIn bliss long time shall dwell above this earthly plain

kural.Translation: Who hold His feet who likes nor loathes Are free from woes of human births
kural.explanation: To those who meditate the feet of Him who is void of desire or aversion, evil shall never come
kural.couplet: His foot, 'Whom want affects not, irks not grief,' who gainShall not, through every time, of any woes complain

kural.Translation: God's praise who tell, are free from right  And wrong, the twins of dreaming night
kural.explanation: The two-fold deeds that spring from darkness shall not adhere to those who delight in the true praise of God
kural.couplet: The men, who on the 'King's' true praised delight to dwell,Affects not them the fruit of deeds done ill or well

kural.Translation: They prosper long who walk His way Who has the senses signed away
kural.explanation: Those shall long proposer who abide in the faultless way of Him who has destroyed the five desires of the senses
kural.couplet: Long live they blest, who 've stood in path from falsehood freed;His, 'Who quenched lusts that from the sense-gates five proceed'

kural.Translation: His feet, whose likeness none can find, Alone can ease the anxious mind
kural.explanation: Anxiety of mind cannot be removed, except from those who are united to the feet of Him who is incomparable
kural.couplet: Unless His foot, 'to Whom none can compare,' men gain,'Tis hard for mind to find relief from anxious pain

kural.Translation: Who swims the sea of vice is he Who clasps the feet of Virtue's sea
kural.explanation: None can swim the sea of vice, but those who are united to the feet of that gracious Being who is a sea of virtue
kural.couplet: Unless His feet 'the Sea of Good, the Fair and Bountiful,' men gain,'Tis hard the further bank of being's changeful sea to attain

kural.Translation: Like senses stale that head is vain Which bows not to Eight-Virtued Divine
kural.explanation: The head that worships not the feet of Him who is possessed of eight attributes, is as useless as a sense without the power of sensation
kural.couplet: Before His foot, 'the Eight-fold Excellence,' with unbent head,Who stands, like palsied sense, is to all living functions dead

kural.Translation: The sea of births they alone swim Who clench His feet and cleave to Him
kural.explanation: None can swim the great sea of births but those who are united to the feet of God
kural.couplet: They swim the sea of births, the 'Monarch's' foot who gain;None others reach the shore of being's mighty main

kural.Translation: The genial rain ambrosia call: The world but lasts while rain shall fall
kural.explanation: By the continuance of rain the world is preserved in existence; it is therefore worthy to be called ambrosia
kural.couplet: The world its course maintains through life that rain unfailing gives;Thus rain is known the true ambrosial food of all that lives

kural.Translation: The rain begets the food we eat
kural.explanation: Rain produces good food, and is itself food
kural.couplet: The rain makes pleasant food for eaters rise;As food itself, thirst-quenching draught supplies

kural.Translation: Let clouds their visits stay, and dearth Distresses all the sea-girt earth
kural.explanation: If the cloud, withholding rain, deceive (our hopes) hunger will long distress the sea-girt spacious world
kural.couplet: If clouds, that promised rain, deceive, and in the sky remain,Famine, sore torment, stalks o'er earth's vast ocean-girdled plain

kural.Translation: Unless the fruitful shower descend, The ploughman's sacred toil must end
kural.explanation: If the abundance of wealth imparting rain diminish, the labour of the plough must cease
kural.couplet: If clouds their wealth of waters fail on earth to pour,The ploughers plough with oxen's sturdy team no more

kural.Translation: Destruction it may sometimes pour But only rain can life restore
kural.explanation: Rain by its absence ruins men; and by its existence restores them to fortune
kural.couplet: 'Tis rain works all: it ruin spreads, then timely aid supplies;As, in the happy days before, it bids the ruined rise

kural.Translation: No grassy blade its head will rear, If from the cloud no drop appear
kural.explanation: If no drop falls from the clouds, not even the green blade of grass will be seen
kural.couplet: If from the clouds no drops of rain are shed'Tis rare to see green herb lift up its head

kural.Translation: The ocean's wealth will waste away, Except the cloud its stores repay
kural.explanation: Even the wealth of the wide sea will be diminished, if the cloud that has drawn (its waters) up gives them not back again (in rain)
kural.couplet: If clouds restrain their gifts and grant no rain,The treasures fail in ocean's wide domain

kural.Translation: The earth, beneath a barren sky, Would offerings for the gods deny
kural.explanation: If the heaven dry up, neither yearly festivals, nor daily worship will be offered in this world, to the celestials
kural.couplet: If heaven grow dry, with feast and offering never more,Will men on earth the heavenly ones adore

kural.Translation: Were heaven above to fail below Nor alms nor penance earth would show
kural.explanation: If rain fall not, penance and alms-deeds will not dwell within this spacious world
kural.couplet: If heaven its watery treasures ceases to dispense,Through the wide world cease gifts, and deeds of 'penitence'

kural.Translation: Water is life that comes from rain Sans rain our duties go in vain
kural.explanation: If it be said that the duties of life cannot be discharged by any person without water, so without rain there cannot be the flowing of water
kural.couplet: When water fails, functions of nature cease, you say;Thus when rain fails, no men can walk in 'duty's ordered way'

kural.Translation: No merit can be held so high As theirs who sense and self deny
kural.explanation: The end and aim of all treatise is to extol beyond all other excellence, the greatness of those who, while abiding in the rule of conduct peculiar to their state, have abandoned all desire
kural.couplet: The settled rule of every code requires, as highest good,Their greatness who, renouncing all, true to their rule have stood

kural.Translation: To con ascetic glory here Is to count the dead upon the sphere
kural.explanation: To describe the measure of the greatness of those who have forsaken the two-fold desires, is like counting the dead
kural.couplet: As counting those that from the earth have passed away,'Tis vain attempt the might of holy men to say

kural.Translation: No lustre can with theirs compare Who know the right and virtue wear
kural.explanation: The greatness of those who have discovered the properties of both states of being, and renounced the world, shines forth on earth (beyond all others)
kural.couplet: Their greatness earth transcends, who, way of both worlds weighed,In this world take their stand, in virtue's robe arrayed

kural.Translation: With hook of firmness to restrain The senses five, is heaven to gain
kural.explanation: He who guides his five senses by the hook of wisdom will be a seed in the world of heaven
kural.couplet: He, who with firmness, curb the five restrains,Is seed for soil of yonder happy plains

kural.Translation: Indra himself has cause to say How great the power ascetics' sway
kural.explanation: Indra, the king of the inhabitants of the spacious heaven, is himself, a sufficient proof of the strength of him who has subdued his five senses
kural.couplet: Their might who have destroyed 'the five', shall soothly tellIndra, the lord of those in heaven's wide realms that dwell

kural.Translation: The small the paths of ease pursue The great achieve things rare to do
kural.explanation: The great will do those things which is difficult to be done; but the mean cannot do them
kural.couplet: Things hard in the doing will great men do;Things hard in the doing the mean eschew

kural.Translation: They gain the world, who grasp and tell Of taste, sight, hearing, touch and smell
kural.explanation: The world is within the knowledge of him who knows the properties of taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell
kural.couplet: Taste, light, touch, sound, and smell: who knows the wayOf all the five,- the world submissive owns his sway

kural.Translation: Full-worded men by what they say, Their greatness to the world display
kural.explanation: The hidden words of the men whose words are full of effect, will shew their greatness to the world
kural.couplet: The might of men whose word is never vain,The 'secret word' shall to the earth proclaim

kural.Translation: Their wrath, who've climb'd the mount of good, Though transient, cannot be withstood
kural.explanation: The anger of those who have ascended the mountain of goodness, though it continue but for a moment, cannot be resisted
kural.couplet: The wrath 'tis hard e'en for an instant to endure,Of those who virtue's hill have scaled, and stand secure

kural.Translation: With gentle mercy towards all, The sage fulfils the vitue's call
kural.explanation: The virtuous are truly called Anthanar; because in their conduct towards all creatures they are clothed in kindness
kural.couplet: Towards all that breathe, with seemly graciousness adorned they live;And thus to virtue's sons the name of 'Anthanar' men give

kural.Translation: From virtue weal and wealth outflow; What greater good can mankind know?
kural.explanation: Virtue will confer heaven and wealth; what greater source of happiness can man possess ?
kural.couplet: It yields distinction, yields prosperity; what gainGreater than virtue can a living man obtain

kural.Translation: Virtue enhances joy and gain; Forsaking it is fall and pain
kural.explanation: There can be no greater source of good than (the practice of) virtue; there can be no greater source of evil than the forgetfulness of it
kural.couplet: No greater gain than virtue aught can cause;No greater loss than life oblivious of her laws

kural.Translation: Perform good deeds as much you can Always and everywhere, o man!
kural.explanation: As much as possible, in every way, incessantly practise virtue
kural.couplet: To finish virtue's work with ceaseless effort strive,What way thou may'st, where'er thou see'st the work may thrive

kural.Translation: In spotless mind virtue is found And not in show and swelling sound
kural.explanation: Let him who does virtuous deeds be of spotless mind; to that extent is virtue; all else is vain show
kural.couplet: Spotless be thou in mind! This only merits virtue's name;All else, mere pomp of idle sound, no real worth can claim

kural.Translation: Four ills eschew and virtue reach, Lust, anger, envy, evil-speech
kural.explanation: That conduct is virtue which is free from these four things, viz, malice, desire, anger and bitter speech
kural.couplet: 'Tis virtue when, his footsteps sliding not through envy, wrath,Lust, evil speech-these four, man onwards moves in ordered path

kural.Translation: Do good enow; defer it not A deathless aid in death if sought
kural.explanation: Defer not virtue to another day; receive her now; and at the dying hour she will be your undying friend
kural.couplet: Do deeds of virtue now Say not, 'To-morrow we'll be wise';Thus, when thou diest, shalt thou find a help that never dies

kural.Translation: Litter-bearer and rider say  Without a word, the fortune's way
kural.explanation: The fruit of virtue need not be described in books; it may be inferred from seeing the bearer of a palanquin and the rider therein
kural.couplet: Needs not in words to dwell on virtue's fruits: compareThe man in litter borne with them that toiling bear

kural.Translation: Like stones that block rebirth and pain Are doing good and good again
kural.explanation: If one allows no day to pass without some good being done, his conduct will be a stone to block up the passage to other births
kural.couplet: If no day passing idly, good to do each day you toil,A stone it will be to block the way of future days of moil

kural.Translation: Weal flows only from virtue done The rest is rue and renown gone
kural.explanation: Only that pleasure which flows from domestic virtue is pleasure; all else is not pleasure, and it is without praise
kural.couplet: What from virtue floweth, yieldeth dear delight;All else extern, is void of glory's light

kural.Translation: Worthy act is virtue done Vice is what we ought to shun
kural.explanation: That is virtue which each ought to do, and that is vice which each should shun
kural.couplet: 'Virtue' sums the things that should be done;'Vice' sums the things that man should shun

kural.Translation: The ideal householder is he Who aids the natural orders there
kural.explanation: He will be called a (true) householder, who is a firm support to the virtuous of the three orders in
kural.couplet: The men of household virtue, firm in way of good, sustainThe other orders three that rule professed maintain

kural.Translation: His help the monk and retired share, And celibate students are his care
kural.explanation: He will be said to flourish in domestic virtue who aids the forsaken, the poor, and the dead
kural.couplet: To anchorites, to indigent, to those who've passed away,The man for household virtue famed is needful held and stay

kural.Translation: By dutiful householder's aid God, manes, kin, self and guests are served
kural.explanation: The chief (duty of the householder) is to preserve the five-fold rule (of conduct) towards the manes, the Gods, his guests, his relations and himself
kural.couplet: The manes, God, guests kindred, self, in due degree,These five to cherish well is chiefest charity

kural.Translation: Sin he shuns and food he shares His home is bright and brighter fares
kural.explanation: His descendants shall never fail who, living in the domestic state, fears vice (in the acquisition of property) and shares his food (with others)
kural.couplet: Who shares his meal with other, while all guilt he shuns,His virtuous line unbroken though the ages runs

kural.Translation: In grace and gain the home excels, Where love with virtue sweetly dwells
kural.explanation: If the married life possess love and virtue, these will be both its duty and reward
kural.couplet: If love and virtue in the household reign,This is of life the perfect grace and gain

kural.Translation: Who turns from righteous family To be a monk, what profits he?
kural.explanation: What will he who lives virtuously in the domestic state gain by going into the other, (ascetic) state ?
kural.couplet: If man in active household life a virtuous soul retain,What fruit from other modes of virtue can he gain

kural.Translation: Of all who strive for bliss, the great Is he who leads the married state
kural.explanation: Among all those who labour (for future happiness) he is greatest who lives well in the household state
kural.couplet: In nature's way who spends his calm domestic days,'Mid all that strive for virtue's crown hath foremost place

kural.Translation: Straight in virtue, right in living Make men brighter than monks praying
kural.explanation: The householder who, not swerving from virtue, helps the ascetic in his way, endures more than those who endure penance
kural.couplet: Others it sets upon their way, itself from virtue ne'er declines;Than stern ascetics' pains such life domestic brighter shines

kural.Translation: Home-life and virtue, are the same; Which spotless monkhood too can claim
kural.explanation: The marriage state is truly called virtue The other state is also good, if others do not reproach it
kural.couplet: The life domestic rightly bears true virtue's name;That other too, if blameless found, due praise may claim

kural.Translation: He is a man of divine worth Who lives in ideal home on earth
kural.explanation: He who on earth has lived in the conjugal state as he should live, will be placed among the Gods who dwell in heaven
kural.couplet: Who shares domestic life, by household virtues graced,Shall, mid the Gods, in heaven who dwell, be placed

kural.Translation: A good housewife befits the house, Spending with thrift the mate's resource
kural.explanation: She who has the excellence of home virtues, and can expend within the means of her husband, is a help in the domestic state
kural.couplet: As doth the house beseem, she shows her wifely dignity;As doth her husband's wealth befit, she spends: help - meet is she

kural.Translation: Bright is home when wife is chaste If not all greatness is but waste
kural.explanation: If the wife be devoid of domestic excellence, whatever (other) greatness be possessed, the conjugal state, is nothing
kural.couplet: If household excellence be wanting in the wife,Howe'er with splendour lived, all worthless is the life

kural.Translation: What is rare when wife is good What can be there when she is bad?
kural.explanation: If his wife be eminent (in virtue), what does (that man) not possess ? If she be without excellence, what does (he) possess ?
kural.couplet: There is no lack within the house, where wife in worth excels,There is no luck within the house, where wife dishonoured dwells

kural.Translation: What greater fortune is for men Than a constant chaste woman?
kural.explanation: What is more excellent than a wife, if she possess the stability of chastity ?
kural.couplet: If woman might of chastity retain,What choicer treasure doth the world contain

kural.Translation: Her spouse before God who adores, Is like rain that at request pours
kural.explanation: If she, who does not worship God, but who rising worships her husband, say, "let it rain," it will rain
kural.couplet: No God adoring, low she bends before her lord;Then rising, serves: the rain falls instant at her word

kural.Translation: The good wife guards herself from blame, She tends her spouse and brings him fame
kural.explanation: She is a wife who unweariedly guards herself, takes care of her husband, and preserves an unsullied fame
kural.couplet: Who guards herself, for husband's comfort cares, her household's fame,In perfect wise with sleepless soul preserves, -give her a woman's name

kural.Translation: Of what avail are watch and ward? Their purity is women's guard
kural.explanation: What avails the guard of a prison ? The chief guard of a woman is her chastity
kural.couplet: Of what avail is watch and ward?Honour's woman's safest guard

kural.Translation: Women who win their husbands' heart Shall flourish where the gods resort
kural.explanation: If women shew reverence to their husbands, they will obtain great excellence in the world where the gods flourish
kural.couplet: If wife be wholly true to him who gained her as his bride,Great glory gains she in the world where gods bliss abide

kural.Translation: A cuckold has not the lion-like gait Before his detractors aright
kural.explanation: The man whose wife seeks not the praise (of chastity) cannot walk with lion-like stately step, before those who revile them
kural.couplet: Who have not spouses that in virtue's praise delight,They lion-like can never walk in scorner's sight

kural.Translation: An honest wife is home's delight And children good are jewels abright
kural.explanation: The excellence of a wife is the good of her husband; and good children are the jewels of that goodness
kural.couplet: The house's 'blessing', men pronounce the house-wife excellent;The gain of blessed children is its goodly ornament

kural.Translation: The world no higher bliss bestows Than children virtuous and wise
kural.explanation: Among all the benefits that may be acquired, we know no greater benefit than the acquisition of intelligent children
kural.couplet: Of all that men acquire, we know not any greater gain,Than that which by the birth of learned children men obtain

kural.Translation: No evil comes and no blemish; Noble sons bring all we wish
kural.explanation: The evils of the seven births shall not touch those who abtain children of a good disposition, free from vice
kural.couplet: Who children gain, that none reproach, of virtuous worth,No evils touch them, through the sev'n-fold maze of birth

kural.Translation: Children are one's wealth indeed Their wealth is measured by their deed
kural.explanation: Men will call their sons their wealth, because it flows to them through the deeds which they (sons) perform on their behalf
kural.couplet: 'Man's children are his fortune,' say the wise;From each one's deeds his varied fortunes rise

kural.Translation: The food is more than nectar sweet In which one's children hands insert
kural.explanation: The rice in which the little hand of their children has dabbled will be far sweeter (to the parent) than ambrosia
kural.couplet: Than God's ambrosia sweeter far the food before men laid,In which the little hands of children of their own have play'd

kural.Translation: Children's touch delights the body Sweet to ears are their words lovely
kural.explanation: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and the hearing of their words, pleasure to the ear
kural.couplet: To patent sweet the touch of children dear;Their voice is sweetest music to his ear

kural.Translation: The flute and lute are sweet they say Deaf to baby's babble's lay!
kural.explanation: "The pipe is sweet, the lute is sweet," say those who have not heard the prattle of their own children
kural.couplet: 'The pipe is sweet,' 'the lute is sweet,' by them't will be averred,Who music of their infants' lisping lips have never heard

kural.Translation: A father's duty to his son is  To seat him in front of the wise
kural.explanation: The benefit which a father should confer on his son is to give him precedence in the assembly of the learned
kural.couplet: Sire greatest boon on son confers, who makes him meet,In councils of the wise to fill the highest seat

kural.Translation: With joy the hearts of parents swell  To see their children themselves excel
kural.explanation: That their children should possess knowledge is more pleasing to all men of this great earth than to themselves
kural.couplet: Their children's wisdom greater than their own confessed,Through the wide world is sweet to every human breast

kural.Translation: The mother, hearing her son's merit  Delights more than when she begot
kural.explanation: The mother who hears her son called "a wise man" will rejoice more than she did at his birth
kural.couplet: When mother hears him named 'fulfill'd of wisdom's lore,'Far greater joy she feels, than when her son she bore

kural.Translation: The son to sire this word is debt  \"What penance such a son begot!\"
kural.explanation: (So to act) that it may be said "by what great penance did his father beget him," is the benefit which a son should render to his father
kural.couplet: To sire, what best requital can by grateful child be done?To make men say, 'What merit gained the father such a son?'

kural.Translation: What bolt can bar true love in fact  The tricking tears reveal the heart
kural.explanation: Is there any fastening that can shut in love ? Tears of the affectionate will publish the love that is within
kural.couplet: And is there bar that can even love restrain?The tiny tear shall make the lover's secret plain

kural.Translation: To selves belong the loveless ones;  To oth'rs the loving e'en to bones
kural.explanation: Those who are destitute of love appropriate all they have to themselves; but those who possess love consider even their bones to belong to others
kural.couplet: The loveless to themselves belong alone;The loving men are others' to the very bone

kural.Translation: Soul is encased in frame of bone  To taste the life of love alone
kural.explanation: They say that the union of soul and body in man is the fruit of the union of love and virtue (in a former birth)
kural.couplet: Of precious soul with body's flesh and bone,The union yields one fruit, the life of love alone

kural.Translation: Love yields aspiration and thence  Friendship springs up in excellence
kural.explanation: Love begets desire: and that (desire) begets the immeasureable excellence of friendship
kural.couplet: From love fond yearning springs for union sweet of minds;And that the bond of rare excelling friendship binds

kural.Translation: The crowning joy of home life flows  From peaceful psychic love always
kural.explanation: These are the fruits of tranquil life of love
kural.couplet: Sweetness on earth and rarest bliss above,These are the fruits of tranquil life of love

kural.Translation: \"Love is virtue's friend\" say know-nots  It helps us against evil plots
kural.explanation: The ignorant say that love is an ally to virtue only, but it is also a help to get out of vice
kural.couplet: The unwise deem love virtue only can sustain,It also helps the man who evil would restrain

kural.Translation: Justice burns the loveless form  Like solar blaze the boneless worm
kural.explanation: Virtue will burn up the soul which is without love, even as the sun burns up the creature which is without bone, ie worms
kural.couplet: As sun's fierce ray dries up the boneless things,So loveless beings virtue's power to nothing brings

kural.Translation: Life bereft of love is gloom  Can sapless tree in desert bloom?
kural.explanation: The domestic state of that man whose mind is without love is like the flourishing of a withered tree upon the parched desert
kural.couplet: The loveless soul, the very joys of life may know,When flowers, in barren soil, on sapless trees, shall blow

kural.Translation: Love is the heart which limbs must move,  Or vain the outer parts will prove
kural.explanation: Of what avail are all the external members (of the body) to those who are destitute of love, the internal member
kural.couplet: Though every outward part complete, the body's fitly framed;What good, when soul within, of love devoid, lies halt and maimed

kural.Translation: The seat of life is love alone;  Or beings are but skin and bone!
kural.explanation: That body alone which is inspired with love contains a living soul: if void of it, (the body) is bone overlaid with skin
kural.couplet: Bodies of loveless men are bony framework clad with skin;Then is the body seat of life, when love resides within

kural.Translation: Men set up home, toil and earn  To tend the guests and do good turn
kural.explanation: The whole design of living in the domestic state and laying up (property) is (to be able) to exercise the benevolence of hospitality
kural.couplet: All household cares and course of daily life have this in viewGuests to receive with courtesy, and kindly acts to do

kural.Translation: To keep out guests cannot be good  Albeit you eat nector-like food
kural.explanation: It is not fit that one should wish his guests to be outside (his house) even though he were eating the food of immortality
kural.couplet: Though food of immortality should crown the board,Feasting alone, the guests without unfed, is thing abhorred

kural.Translation: Who tends his guests day in and out  His life in want never wears out
kural.explanation: The domestic life of the man that daily entertains the guests who come to him shall not be laid waste by poverty
kural.couplet: Each day he tends the coming guest with kindly care;Painless, unfailing plenty shall his household share

kural.Translation: The goddess of wealth will gladly rest  Where smiles welcome the worthy guest
kural.explanation: Lakshmi with joyous mind shall dwell in the house of that man who, with cheerful countenance, entertains the good as guests
kural.couplet: With smiling face he entertains each virtuous guest,'Fortune' with gladsome mind shall in his dwelling rest

kural.Translation: Should his field be sown who first  Feeds the guests and eats the rest?
kural.explanation: Is it necessary to sow the field of the man who, having feasted his guests, eats what may remain ?
kural.couplet: Who first regales his guest, and then himself supplies,O'er all his fields, unsown, shall plenteous harvests rise

kural.Translation: Who tends a guest and looks for next  Is a welcome guest in heaven's feast
kural.explanation: He who, having entertained the guests that have come, looks out for others who may yet come, will be a welcome guest to the inhabitants of heaven
kural.couplet: The guest arrived he tends, the coming guest expects to see;To those in heavenly homes that dwell a welcome guest is he

kural.Translation: Worth of the guest of quality  Is worth of hospitality
kural.explanation: The advantages of benevolence cannot be measured; the measure (of the virtue) of the guests (entertained) is the only measure
kural.couplet: To reckon up the fruit of kindly deeds were all in vain;Their worth is as the worth of guests you entertain

kural.Translation: Who loathe guest-service one day cry:  \"We toil and store; but life is dry\"
kural.explanation: Those who have taken no part in the benevolence of hospitality shall (at length lament) saying, "we have laboured and laid up wealth and are now without support."
kural.couplet: With pain they guard their stores, yet 'All forlorn are we,' they'll cry,Who cherish not their guests, nor kindly help supply

kural.Translation: The man of wealth is poor indeed  Whose folly fails the guest to feed
kural.explanation: That stupidity which excercises no hospitality is poverty in the midst of wealth It is the property of the stupid
kural.couplet: To turn from guests is penury, though worldly goods abound;'Tis senseless folly, only with the senseless found

kural.Translation: Anicham smelt withers: like that  A wry-faced look withers the guest
kural.explanation: As the Anicham flower fades in smelling, so fades the guest when the face is turned away
kural.couplet: The flower of 'Anicha' withers away, If you do but its fragrance inhale;If the face of the host cold welcome convey, The guest's heart within him will fail

kural.Translation: The words of Seers are lovely sweet  Merciful and free from deceit
kural.explanation: Sweet words are those which imbued with love and free from deceit flow from the mouth of the virtuous
kural.couplet: Pleasant words are words with all pervading love that burn;Words from his guileless mouth who can the very truth discern

kural.Translation: Sweet words from smiling lips dispense  More joys than heart's beneficence
kural.explanation: Sweet speech, with a cheerful countenance is better than a gift made with a joyous mind
kural.couplet: A pleasant word with beaming smile's preferred,Even to gifts with liberal heart conferred

kural.Translation: Calm face, sweet look, kind words from heart  Such is the gracious virtue's part
kural.explanation: Sweet speech, flowing from the heart (uttered) with a cheerful countenance and a sweet look, is true virtue
kural.couplet: With brightly beaming smile, and kindly light of loving eye,And heart sincere, to utter pleasant words is charity

kural.Translation: Whose loving words delight each one  The woe of want from them is gone
kural.explanation: Sorrow-increasing poverty shall not come upon those who use towards all, pleasure-increasing sweetness of speech
kural.couplet: The men of pleasant speech that gladness breathe around,Through indigence shall never sorrow's prey be found

kural.Translation: To be humble and sweet words speak  No other jewel do wise men seek
kural.explanation: Humility and sweetness of speech are the ornaments of man; all others are not (ornaments)
kural.couplet: Humility with pleasant speech to man on earth,Is choice adornment; all besides is nothing worth

kural.Translation: His sins vanish, his virtues grow  Whose fruitful words with sweetness flow
kural.explanation: If a man, while seeking to speak usefully, speaks also sweetly, his sins will diminish and his virtue increase
kural.couplet: Who seeks out good, words from his lips of sweetness flow;In him the power of vice declines, and virtues grow

kural.Translation: The fruitful courteous kindly words  Lead to goodness and graceful deeds
kural.explanation: That speech which, while imparting benefits ceases not to please, will yield righteousness (for this world) and merit (for the next world)
kural.couplet: The words of sterling sense, to rule of right that strict adhere,To virtuous action prompting, blessings yield in every sphere

kural.Translation: Kind words free from meanness delight  This life on earth and life the next
kural.explanation: Sweet speech, free from harm to others, will give pleasure both in this world and in the next
kural.couplet: Sweet kindly words, from meanness free, delight of heart,In world to come and in this world impart

kural.Translation: Who sees the sweets of sweetness here  To use harsh words how can he dare?
kural.explanation: Why does he use harsh words, who sees the pleasure which sweet speech yields ?
kural.couplet: Who sees the pleasure kindly speech affords,Why makes he use of harsh, repellant words

kural.Translation: Leaving ripe fruits the raw he eats  Who speaks harsh words when sweet word suits
kural.explanation: To say disagreeable things when agreeable are at hand is like eating unripe fruit when there is ripe
kural.couplet: When pleasant words are easy, bitter words to use,Is, leaving sweet ripe fruit, the sour unripe to choose

kural.Translation: Unhelped in turn good help given  Exceeds in worth earth and heaven
kural.explanation: (The gift of) heaven and earth is not an equivalent for a benefit which is conferred where none had been received
kural.couplet: Assistance given by those who ne'er received our aid,Is debt by gift of heaven and earth but poorly paid

kural.Translation: A help rendered in hour of need  Though small is greater than the world
kural.explanation: A favour conferred in the time of need, though it be small (in itself), is (in value) much larger than the world
kural.couplet: A timely benefit, -though thing of little worth,The gift itself, -in excellence transcends the earth

kural.Translation: Help rendered without weighing fruits  Outweighs the sea in grand effects
kural.explanation: If we weigh the excellence of a benefit which is conferred without weighing the return, it is larger than the sea
kural.couplet: Kindness shown by those who weigh not what the return may be:When you ponder right its merit, 'Tis vaster than the sea

kural.Translation: Help given though millet-small  Knowers count its good palm-tree tall
kural.explanation: Though the benefit conferred be as small as a millet seed, those who know its advantage will consider it as large as a palmyra fruit
kural.couplet: Each benefit to those of actions' fruit who rightly deem,Though small as millet-seed, as palm-tree vast will seem

kural.Translation: A help is not the help's measure  It is gainer's worth and pleasure
kural.explanation: The benefit itself is not the measure of the benefit; the worth of those who have received it is its measure
kural.couplet: The kindly aid's extent is of its worth no measure true;Its worth is as the worth of him to whom the act you do

kural.Translation: Forget not friendship of the pure  Forsake not timely helpers sure
kural.explanation: Forsake not the friendship of those who have been your staff in adversity Forget not be benevolence of the blameless
kural.couplet: Kindness of men of stainless soul remember evermoreForsake thou never friends who were thy stay in sorrow sore

kural.Translation: Through sevenfold births, in memory fares  The willing friend who wiped one's tears
kural.explanation: (The wise) will remember throughout their seven-fold births the love of those who have wiped away their affliction
kural.couplet: Through all seven worlds, in seven-fold birth, Remains in mem'ry of the wiseFriendship of those who wiped on earth, The tears of sorrow from their eyes

kural.Translation: To forget good turns is not good  Good it is over wrong not to brood
kural.explanation: It is not good to forget a benefit; it is good to forget an injury even in the very moment (in which it is inflicted)
kural.couplet: 'Tis never good to let the thought of good things done thee pass away;Of things not good, 'tis good to rid thy memory that very day

kural.Translation: Let deadly harms be forgotten  While remembering one good-turn
kural.explanation: Though one inflict an injury great as murder, it will perish before the thought of one benefit (formerly) conferred
kural.couplet: Effaced straightway is deadliest injury,By thought of one kind act in days gone by

kural.Translation: The virtue-killer may be saved  Not benefit-killer who is damned
kural.explanation: He who has killed every virtue may yet escape; there is no escape for him who has killed a benefit
kural.couplet: Who every good have killed, may yet destruction flee;Who 'benefit' has killed, that man shall ne'er 'scape free

kural.Translation: Equity is supreme virtue  It is to give each man his due
kural.explanation: That equity which consists in acting with equal regard to each of (the three) divisions of men [enemies, strangers and friends] is a pre-eminent virtue
kural.couplet: If justice, failing not, its quality maintain,Giving to each his due, -'tis man's one highest gain

kural.Translation: Wealth of the man of equity  Grows and lasts to posterity
kural.explanation: The wealth of the man of rectitude will not perish, but will bring happiness also to his posterity
kural.couplet: The just man's wealth unwasting shall endure,And to his race a lasting joy ensure

kural.Translation: Though profitable, turn away  From unjust gains without delay
kural.explanation: Forsake in the very moment (of acquisition) that gain which, though it should bring advantage, is without equity
kural.couplet: Though only good it seem to give, yet gainBy wrong acquired, not e'en one day retain

kural.Translation: The worthy and the unworthy  Are seen in their posterity
kural.explanation: The worthy and unworthy may be known by the existence or otherwise of good offsprings
kural.couplet: Who just or unjust lived shall soon appear:By each one's offspring shall the truth be clear

kural.Translation: Loss and gain by cause arise;  Equal mind adorns the wise
kural.explanation: Loss and gain come not without cause; it is the ornament of the wise to preserve evenness of mind (under both)
kural.couplet: The gain and loss in life are not mere accident;Just mind inflexible is sages' ornament

kural.Translation: Of perdition let him be sure  Who leaves justice to sinful lure
kural.explanation: Let him whose mind departing from equity commits sin well consider thus within himself, "I shall perish."
kural.couplet: If, right deserting, heart to evil turn,Let man impending ruin's sign discern

kural.Translation: The just reduced to poverty  Is not held down by equity
kural.explanation: The great will not regard as poverty the low estate of that man who dwells in the virtue of equity
kural.couplet: The man who justly lives, tenacious of the right,In low estate is never low to wise man's sight

kural.Translation: Like balance holding equal scales  A well poised mind is jewel of the wise
kural.explanation: To incline to neither side, but to rest impartial as the even-fixed scale is the ornament of the wise
kural.couplet: To stand, like balance-rod that level hangs and rightly weighs,With calm unbiassed equity of soul, is sages' praise

kural.Translation: Justice is upright, unbending  And free from crooked word-twisting
kural.explanation: Freedom from obliquity of speech is rectitude, if there be (corresponding) freedom from bias of mind
kural.couplet: Inflexibility in word is righteousness,If men inflexibility of soul possess

kural.Translation: A trader's trade prospers fairly  When his dealings are neighbourly
kural.explanation: The true merchandize of merchants is to guard and do by the things of others as they do by their own
kural.couplet: As thriving trader is the trader known,Who guards another's interests as his own

kural.Translation: Self-rule leads to realms of gods  Indulgence leads to gloomy hades
kural.explanation: Self-control will place (a man) among the Gods; the want of it will drive (him) into the thickest darkness (of hell)
kural.couplet: Control of self does man conduct to bliss th' immortals share;Indulgence leads to deepest night, and leaves him there

kural.Translation: No gains with self-control measure  Guard with care this great treasure
kural.explanation: Let self-control be guarded as a treasure; there is no greater source of good for man than that
kural.couplet: Guard thou as wealth the power of self-control;Than this no greater gain to living soul

kural.Translation: Knowing wisdom who lives controlled  Name and fame seek him untold
kural.explanation: Knowing that self-control is knowledge, if a man should control himself, in the prescribed course, such self-control will bring him distinction among the wise
kural.couplet: If versed in wisdom's lore by virtue's law you self restrainYour self-repression known will yield you glory's gain

kural.Translation: Firmly fixed in self serene  The sage looks grander than mountain
kural.explanation: More lofty than a mountain will be the greatness of that man who without swerving from his domestic state, controls himself
kural.couplet: In his station, all unswerving, if man self subdue,Greater he than mountain proudly rising to the view

kural.Translation: Humility is good for all  To the rich it adds a wealth special
kural.explanation: Humility is good in all; but especially in the rich it is (the excellence of) higher riches
kural.couplet: To all humility is goodly grace; but chief to themWith fortune blessed, -'tis fortune's diadem

kural.Translation: Who senses five like tortoise hold  Their joy prolongs to births sevenfold
kural.explanation: Should one throughout a single birth, like a tortoise keep in his five senses, the fruit of it will prove a safe-guard to him throughout the seven-fold births.
kural.couplet: Like tortoise, who the five restrainsIn one, through seven world bliss obtains

kural.Translation: Rein the tongue if nothing else  Or slips of tongue bring all the woes
kural.explanation: Whatever besides you leave unguarded, guard your tongue; otherwise errors of speech and the consequent misery will ensue
kural.couplet: Whate'er they fail to guard, o'er lips men guard should keep;If not, through fault of tongue, they bitter tears shall weep

kural.Translation: Even a single evil word  Will turn all good results to bad
kural.explanation: If a man's speech be productive of a single evil, all the good by him will be turned into evil
kural.couplet: Though some small gain of good it seem to bring,The evil word is parent still of evil thing

kural.Translation: The fire-burnt wounds do find a cure  Tongue-burnt wound rests a running sore
kural.explanation: The wound which has been burnt in by fire may heal, but a wound burnt in by the tongue will never heal
kural.couplet: In flesh by fire inflamed, nature may thoroughly heal the sore;In soul by tongue inflamed, the ulcer healeth never more

kural.Translation: Virtue seeks and peeps to see  Self-controlled savant anger free
kural.explanation: Virtue, seeking for an opportunity, will come into the path of that man who, possessed of learning and self-control, guards himself against anger
kural.couplet: Who learns restraint, and guards his soul from wrath,Virtue, a timely aid, attends his path

kural.Translation: Decorum does one dignity  More than life guard its purity
kural.explanation: Propriety of conduct leads to eminence, it should therefore be preserved more carefully than life
kural.couplet: 'Decorum' gives especial excellence; with greater care'Decorum' should men guard than life, which all men share

kural.Translation: Virtues of conduct all excel;  The soul aid should be guarded well
kural.explanation: Let propriety of conduct be laboriously preserved and guarded; though one know and practise and excel in many virtues, that will be an eminent aid
kural.couplet: Searching, duly watching, learning, 'decorum' still we find;Man's only aid; toiling, guard thou this with watchful mind

kural.Translation: Good conduct shows good family  Low manners mark anomaly
kural.explanation: Propriety of conduct is true greatness of birth, and impropriety will sink into a mean birth
kural.couplet: 'Decorum's' true nobility on earth;'Indecorum's' issue is ignoble birth

kural.Translation: Readers recall forgotten lore,  But conduct lost returns no more
kural.explanation: A Brahman though he should forget the Vedas may recover it by reading; but, if he fail in propriety of conduct even his high birth will be destroyed
kural.couplet: Though he forget, the Brahman may regain his Vedic lore;Failing in 'decorum due,' birthright's gone for evermore

kural.Translation: The envious prosper but ill  The ill-behaved sinks lower still
kural.explanation: Just as the envious man will be without wealth, so will the man of destitute of propriety of conduct be without greatness
kural.couplet: The envious soul in life no rich increase of blessing gains,So man of 'due decorum' void no dignity obtains

kural.Translation: The firm from virtue falter not  They know the ills of evil thought
kural.explanation: Those firm in mind will not slacken in their observance of the proprieties of life, knowing, as they do, the misery that flows from the transgression from them
kural.couplet: The strong of soul no jot abate of 'strict decorum's' laws,Knowing that 'due decorum's' breach foulest disgrace will cause

kural.Translation: Conduct good ennobles man,  Bad conduct entails disgrace mean
kural.explanation: From propriety of conduct men obtain greatness; from impropriety comes insufferable disgrace
kural.couplet: 'Tis source of dignity when 'true decorum' is preserved;Who break 'decorum's' rules endure e'en censures undeserved

kural.Translation: Good conduct sows seeds of blessings  Bad conduct endless evil brings
kural.explanation: Propriety of conduct is the seed of virtue; impropriety will ever cause sorrow
kural.couplet: 'Decorum true' observed a seed of good will be;'Decorum's breach' will sorrow yield eternally

kural.Translation: Foul words will never fall from lips  Of righteous men even by slips
kural.explanation: Those who study propriety of conduct will not speak evil, even forgetfully
kural.couplet: It cannot be that they who 'strict decorum's' law fulfil,E'en in forgetful mood, should utter words of ill

kural.Translation: Though read much they are ignorant  Whose life is not world-accordant
kural.explanation: Those who know not how to act agreeably to the world, though they have learnt many things, are still ignorant
kural.couplet: Who know not with the world in harmony to dwell,May many things have learned, but nothing well

kural.Translation: Who know the wealth and virtue's way  After other's wife do not stray
kural.explanation: The folly of desiring her who is the property of another will not be found in those who know (the attributes of) virtue and (the rights of) property
kural.couplet: Who laws of virtue and possession's rights have known,Indulge no foolish love of her by right another's own

kural.Translation: He is the worst law breaking boor  Who haunts around his neighbour's door
kural.explanation: Among all those who stand on the outside of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand outside their neighbour's door
kural.couplet: No fools, of all that stand from virtue's pale shut out,Like those who longing lurk their neighbour's gate without

kural.Translation: The vile are dead who evil aim  And put faithful friends' wives to shame
kural.explanation: Certainly they are no better than dead men who desire evil towards the wife of those who
kural.couplet: They're numbered with the dead, e'en while they live, -how otherwise?With wife of sure confiding friend who evil things devise

kural.Translation: Their boasted greatness means nothing  When to another's wife they cling
kural.explanation: However great one may be, what does it avail if, without at all considering his guilt, he goes unto the wife of another ?
kural.couplet: How great soe'er they be, what gain have they of life,Who, not a whit reflecting, seek a neighbour's wife

kural.Translation: Who trifles with another's wife  His guilty stain will last for life
kural.explanation: He who thinks lightly of going into the wife of another acquires guilt that will abide with him imperishably and for ever
kural.couplet: 'Mere triflel' saying thus, invades the home, so he ensuresA gain of guilt that deathless aye endures

kural.Translation: Hatred, sin, fear, and shame-these four  Stain adulterers ever more
kural.explanation: Hatred, sin, fear, disgrace; these four will never leave him who goes in to his neighbour's wife
kural.couplet: Who home ivades, from him pass nevermore,Hatred and sin, fear, foul disgrace; these four

kural.Translation: He is the righteous householder  His neighbour's wife who covets never
kural.explanation: He who desires not the womanhood of her who should walk according to the will of another will be praised as a virtuous house-holder
kural.couplet: Who sees the wife, another's own, with no desiring eyeIn sure domestic bliss he dwelleth ever virtuously

kural.Translation: They lead a high-souled manly life  The pure who eye not another's wife
kural.explanation: That noble manliness which looks not at the wife of another is the virtue and dignity of the great
kural.couplet: Manly excellence, that looks not on another's wife,Is not virtue merely, 'tis full 'propriety' of life

kural.Translation: Good in storm bound earth is with those  Who clasp not arms of another's spouse
kural.explanation: Is it asked, "who are those who shall obtain good in this world surrounded by the terror-producing sea ?" Those who touch not the shoulder of her who belongs to another
kural.couplet: Who 're good indeed, on earth begirt by ocean's gruesome tide?The men who touch not her that is another's bride

kural.Translation: Sinners breaking virtue's behest  Lust not for another's wife at least
kural.explanation: Though a man perform no virtuous deeds and commit (every) vice, it will be well if he desire not the womanhood of her who is within the limit (of the house) of another
kural.couplet: Though virtue's bounds he pass, and evil deeds hath wrought;At least, 'tis good if neighbour's wife he covet not

kural.Translation: As earth bears up with diggers too  To bear revilers is prime virtue
kural.explanation: To bear with those who revile us, just as the earth bears up those who dig it, is the first of virtues
kural.couplet: As earth bears up the men who delve into her breast,To bear with scornful men of virtues is the best

kural.Translation: Forgive insults is a good habit  Better it is to forget it
kural.explanation: Bear with reproach even when you can retaliate; but to forget it will be still better than that
kural.couplet: Forgiving trespasses is good always;Forgetting them hath even higher praise;

kural.Translation: Neglect the guest is dearth of dearth  To bear with fools is strength of strength
kural.explanation: To neglect hospitality is poverty of poverty To bear with the ignorant is might of might
kural.couplet: The sorest poverty is bidding guest unfed depart;The mightiest might to bear with men of foolish heart

kural.Translation: Practice of patient quality  Retains intact itegrity
kural.explanation: If you desire that greatness should never leave, you preserve in your conduct the exercise of patience
kural.couplet: Seek'st thou honour never tarnished to retain;So must thou patience, guarding evermore, maintain

kural.Translation: Vengeance is not in esteem held  Patience is praised as hidden gold
kural.explanation: (The wise) will not at all esteem the resentful They will esteem the patient just as the gold which they lay up with care
kural.couplet: Who wreak their wrath as worthless are despised;Who patiently forbear as gold are prized

kural.Translation: Revenge accords but one day's joy  Patience carries its praise for aye
kural.explanation: The pleasure of the resentful continues for a day The praise of the patient will continue until (the final destruction of) the world
kural.couplet: Who wreak their wrath have pleasure for a day;Who bear have praise till earth shall pass away

kural.Translation: Though others cause you wanton pain  Grieve not; from unjust harm refrain
kural.explanation: Though others inflict injuries on you, yet compassionating the evil (that will come upon them) it will be well not to do them anything contrary to virtue
kural.couplet: Though others work thee ill, thus shalt thou blessing reap;Grieve for their sin, thyself from vicious action keep

kural.Translation: By noble forbearance vanquish  The proud that have caused you anguish
kural.explanation: Let a man by patience overcome those who through pride commit excesses
kural.couplet: With overweening pride when men with injuries assail,By thine own righteous dealing shalt thou mightily prevail

kural.Translation: More than ascetics they are pure  Who bitter tongues meekly endure
kural.explanation: Those who bear with the uncourteous speech of the insolent are as pure as the ascetics
kural.couplet: They who transgressors' evil words endureWith patience, are as stern ascetics pure

kural.Translation: Who fast are great to do penance  Greater are they who bear offence
kural.explanation: Those who endure abstinence from food are great, next to those who endure the uncourteous speech of others
kural.couplet: Though 'great' we deem the men that fast and suffer pain,Who others' bitter words endure, the foremost place obtain

kural.Translation: Deem your heart as virtuous  When your nature is not jealous
kural.explanation: Let a man esteem that disposition which is free from envy in the same manner as propriety of conduct
kural.couplet: As 'strict decorum's' laws, that all men bind,Let each regard unenvying grace of mind

kural.Translation: No excellence excels the one  That by nature envies none
kural.explanation: Amongst all attainable excellences there is none equal to that of being free from envy towords others
kural.couplet: If man can learn to envy none on earth,'Tis richest gift, -beyond compare its worth

kural.Translation: Who envies others' good fortune  Can't prosper in virtue of his own
kural.explanation: Of him who instead of rejoicing in the wealth of others, envies it, it will be said "he neither desires virtue not wealth."
kural.couplet: Nor wealth nor virtue does that man desire 'tis plain,Whom others' wealth delights not, feeling envious pain

kural.Translation: The wise through envy don't others wrong  Knowing that woes from evils throng
kural.explanation: (The wise) knowing the misery that comes from transgression will not through envy commit unrighteous deeds
kural.couplet: The wise through envy break not virtue's laws,Knowing ill-deeds of foul disgrace the cause

kural.Translation: Man shall be wrecked by envy's whim  Even if enemies spare him
kural.explanation: To those who cherish envy that is enough Though free from enemies that (envy) will bring destruction
kural.couplet: Envy they have within! Enough to seat their fate!Though foemen fail, envy can ruin consummate

kural.Translation: Who envies gifts shall suffer ruin  Without food and clothes with his kin
kural.explanation: He who is envious at a gift (made to another) will with his relations utterly perish destitute of food and rainment
kural.couplet: Who scans good gifts to others given with envious eye,His kin, with none to clothe or feed them, surely die

kural.Translation: Fortune deserts the envious  Leaving misfortune omnious
kural.explanation: Lakshmi envying (the prosperity) of the envious man will depart and introduce him to her sister
kural.couplet: From envious man good fortune's goddess turns away,Grudging him good, and points him out misfortune's prey

kural.Translation: Caitiff envy despoils wealth  And drags one into evil path
kural.explanation: Envy will destroy (a man's) wealth (in his world) and drive him into the pit of fire (in the world to come.)
kural.couplet: Envy, embodied ill, incomparable bane,Good fortune slays, and soul consigns to fiery pain

kural.Translation: Why is envy rich, goodmen poor  People with surprise think over
kural.explanation: The wealth of a man of envious mind and the poverty of the righteous will be pondered
kural.couplet: To men of envious heart, when comes increase of joy,Or loss to blameless men, the 'why' will thoughtful hearts employ

kural.Translation: The envious prosper never  The envyless prosper ever
kural.explanation: Never have the envious become great; never have those who are free from envy been without greatness
kural.couplet: No envious men to large and full felicity attain;No men from envy free have failed a sure increase to gain

kural.Translation: Who covets others' honest wealth  That greed ruins his house forthwith
kural.explanation: If a man departing from equity covet the property (of others), at that very time will his family be destroyed and guilt be incurred
kural.couplet: With soul unjust to covet others' well-earned store,Brings ruin to the home, to evil opes the door

kural.Translation: Who shrink with shame from sin, refrain  From coveting which brings ruin
kural.explanation: Those who blush at the want of equity will not commit disgraceful acts through desire of the profit that may be gained
kural.couplet: Through lust of gain, no deeds that retribution bring,Do they, who shrink with shame from every unjust thing

kural.Translation: For spiritual bliss who long  For fleeting joy commit no wrong
kural.explanation: Those who desire the higher pleasures (of heaven) will not act unjustly through desire of the trifling joy. (in this life.)
kural.couplet: No deeds of ill, misled by base desire,Do they, whose souls to other joys aspire

kural.Translation: The truth-knowers of sense-control  Though in want covet not at all
kural.explanation: The wise who have conquered their senses and are free from crime, will not covet (the things of others), with the thought "we are destitute."
kural.couplet: Men who have conquered sense, with sight from sordid vision freed,Desire not other's goods, e'en in the hour of sorest need

kural.Translation: What is one's subtle wisdom worth  If it deals ill with all on earth
kural.explanation: What is the advantage of extensive and accurate knowledge if a man through covetousness act senselessly towards all ?
kural.couplet: What gain, though lore refined of amplest reach he learn,His acts towards all mankind if covetous desire to folly turn

kural.Translation: Who seeks for grace on righteous path  Suffers by evil covetous wealth
kural.explanation: If he, who through desire of the virtue of kindness abides in the domestic state ie, the path in which it may be obtained, covet (the property of others) and think of evil methods (to obtain it), he will perish
kural.couplet: Though, grace desiring, he in virtue's way stand strong,He's lost who wealth desires, and ponders deeds of wrong

kural.Translation: Shun the fruit of covetousness  All its yield is inglorious
kural.explanation: Desire not the gain of covetousness In the enjoyment of its fruits there is no glory
kural.couplet: Seek not increase by greed of gain acquired;That fruit matured yields never good desired

kural.Translation: The mark of lasting wealth is shown  By not coveting others' own
kural.explanation: If it is weighed, "what is the indestructibility of wealth," it is freedom from covetousness
kural.couplet: What saves prosperity from swift decline?Absence of lust to make another's cherished riches thine

kural.Translation: Fortune seeks the just and wise  Who are free from coveting vice
kural.explanation: Lakshmi, knowing the manner (in which she may approach) will immediately come to those wise men who, knowing that it is virtue, covet not the property of others
kural.couplet: Good fortune draws anigh in helpful time of need,To him who, schooled in virtue, guards his soul from greed

kural.Translation: Desireless, greatness conquers all;  Coveting misers ruined fall
kural.explanation: To covet (the wealth of another) regardless of consequences will bring destruction That greatness (of mind) which covets not will give victory
kural.couplet: From thoughtless lust of other's goods springs fatal ill,Greatness of soul that covets not shall triumph still

kural.Translation: Though a man from virtue strays,  To keep from slander brings him praise
kural.explanation: Though one do not even speak of virtue and live in sin, it will be well if it be said of him "he does not backbite."
kural.couplet: Though virtuous words his lips speak not, and all his deeds are illIf neighbour he defame not, there's good within him still

kural.Translation: Who bite behind, and before smile  Are worse than open traitors vile
kural.explanation: To smile deceitfully (in another's presence) after having reviled him to his destruction (behind his back) is a greater evil than the commission of (every other) sin and the destruction of (every) virtue
kural.couplet: Than he who virtue scorns, and evil deeds performs, more vile,Is he that slanders friend, then meets him with false smile

kural.Translation: Virtue thinks it better to die,  Than live to backbite and to lie
kural.explanation: Death rather than life will confer upon the deceitful backbiter the profit which (the treatises on) virtue point out
kural.couplet: 'Tis greater gain of virtuous good for man to die,Than live to slander absent friend, and falsely praise when nigh

kural.Translation: Though harsh you speak in one's presence  Abuse is worse in his absence
kural.explanation: Though you speak without kindness before another's face speak not in his absence words which regard not the evil subsequently resulting from it
kural.couplet: In presence though unkindly words you speak, say notIn absence words whose ill result exceeds your thought

kural.Translation: Who turns to slander makes it plain  His praise of virtue is in vain
kural.explanation: The emptiness of that man's mind who (merely) praises virtue will be seen from the meanness of reviling another behind his back
kural.couplet: The slanderous meanness that an absent friend defames,'This man in words owns virtue, not in heart,' proclaims

kural.Translation: His failings will be found and shown,  Who makes another's failings known
kural.explanation: The character of the faults of that man who publishes abroad the faults of others will be sought out and published
kural.couplet: Who on his neighbours' sins delights to dwell,The story of his sins, culled out with care, the world will tell

kural.Translation: By pleasing words who make not friends  Sever their hearts by hostile trends
kural.explanation: Those who know not to live in friendship with amusing conversation will by back-biting estrange even their relatives
kural.couplet: With friendly art who know not pleasant words to say,Speak words that sever hearts, and drive choice friends away

kural.Translation: What will they not to strangers do  Who bring their friends' defects to view?
kural.explanation: What will those not do to strangers whose nature leads them to publish abroad the faults of their intimate friends ?
kural.couplet: Whose nature bids them faults of closest friends proclaimWhat mercy will they show to other men's good name

kural.Translation: The world in mercy bears his load  Who rants behind words untoward
kural.explanation: The world through charity supports the weight of those who reproach others observing their absence
kural.couplet: 'Tis charity, I ween, that makes the earth sustain their loadWho, neighbours' absence watching, tales or slander tell abroad

kural.Translation: No harm would fall to any man  If each his own defect could scan
kural.explanation: If they observed their own faults as they observe the faults of others, would any evil happen to men ?
kural.couplet: If each his own, as neighbours' faults would scan,Could any evil hap to living man

kural.Translation: With silly words who insults all  Is held in contempt as banal
kural.explanation: He who to the disgust of many speaks useless things will be despised by all
kural.couplet: Words without sense, while chafe the wise,Who babbles, him will all despise

kural.Translation: Vain talk before many is worse  Than doing to friends deeds adverse
kural.explanation: To speak useless things in the presence of many is a greater evil than to do unkind things towards friends
kural.couplet: Words without sense, where many wise men hear, to pourThan deeds to friends ungracious done offendeth more

kural.Translation: The babbler's hasty lips proclaim  That \"good-for-nothing\" is his name
kural.explanation: That conversation in which a man utters forth useless things will say of him "he is without virtue."
kural.couplet: Diffusive speech of useless words proclaimsA man who never righteous wisdom gains

kural.Translation: Vain words before an assembly  Will make all gains and goodness flee
kural.explanation: The words devoid of profit or pleasure which a man speaks will, being inconsistent with virtue,
kural.couplet: Unmeaning, worthless words, said to the multitude,To none delight afford, and sever men from good

kural.Translation: Glory and grace will go away  When savants silly nonsense say
kural.explanation: If the good speak vain words their eminence and excellence will leave them
kural.couplet: Gone are both fame and boasted excellence,When men of worth speak of words devoid of sense

kural.Translation: Call him a human chaff who prides  Himself in weightless idle words
kural.explanation: Call not him a man who parades forth his empty words Call him the chaff of men
kural.couplet: Who makes display of idle words' inanity,Call him not man, -chaff of humanity

kural.Translation: Let not men of worth vainly quack  Even if they would roughly speak
kural.explanation: Let the wise if they will, speak things without excellence; it will be well for them not to speak useless things
kural.couplet: Let those who list speak things that no delight afford,'Tis good for men of worth to speak no idle word

kural.Translation: The wise who weigh the worth refrain  From words that have no grain and brain
kural.explanation: The wise who seek after rare pleasures will not speak words that have not much weight in them
kural.couplet: The wise who weigh the worth of every utterance,Speak none but words of deep significance

kural.Translation: The wise of spotless self-vision  Slip not to silly words-mention
kural.explanation: Those wise men who are without faults and are freed from ignorance will not even forgetfully speak things that profit not
kural.couplet: The men of vision pure, from wildering folly free,Not e'en in thoughtless hour, speak words of vanity

kural.Translation: To purpose speak the fruitful word  And never indulge in useless load
kural.explanation: Speak what is useful, and speak not useless words
kural.couplet: If speak you will, speak words that fruit afford,If speak you will, speak never fruitless word

kural.Translation: Sinners fear not the pride of sin  The worthy dread the ill within
kural.explanation: Those who have experience of evil deeds will not fear, but the excellent will fear the pride of sin
kural.couplet: With sinful act men cease to feel the dread of ill within,The excellent will dread the wanton pride of cherished sin

kural.Translation: Since evil begets evil dire  Fear ye evil more than fire
kural.explanation: Because evil produces evil, therefore should evil be feared more than fire
kural.couplet: Since evils new from evils ever grow,Evil than fire works out more dreaded woe

kural.Translation: The wisest of the wise are those  Who injure not even their foes
kural.explanation: So shalt thou wisdom's highest law, 'tis said, fulfil
kural.couplet: Even to those that hate make no return of ill;So shalt thou wisdom's highest law, 'tis said, fulfil

kural.Translation: His ruin virtue plots who plans  The ruin of another man's
kural.explanation: Even though forgetfulness meditate not the ruin of another Virtue will meditate the ruin of him who thus meditates
kural.couplet: Though good thy soul forget, plot not thy neighbour's fall,Thy plans shall 'virtue's Power' by ruin to thyself forestall

kural.Translation: Who makes poverty plea for ill  Shall reduce himself poorer still
kural.explanation: Commit not evil, saying, "I am poor": if you do, you will become poorer still
kural.couplet: Make not thy poverty a plea for ill;Thy evil deeds will make thee poorer still

kural.Translation: From wounding others let him refrain  Who would from harm himself remain
kural.explanation: Let him not do evil to others who desires not that sorrows should pursue him
kural.couplet: What ranks as evil spare to do, if thou would'st shunAffliction sore through ill to thee by others done

kural.Translation: Men may escape other foes and live  But sin its deadly blow will give
kural.explanation: However great be the enmity men have incurred they may still live The enmity of sin will incessantly pursue and kill
kural.couplet: From every enmity incurred there is to 'scape, a way;The wrath of evil deeds will dog men's steps, and slay

kural.Translation: Ruin follows who evil do  As shadow follows as they go
kural.explanation: Destruction will dwell at the heels of those who commit evil even as their shadow that leaves them not
kural.couplet: Man's shadow dogs his steps where'er he wends;Destruction thus on sinful deeds attends

kural.Translation: Let none who loves himself at all  Think of evil however small
kural.explanation: If a man love himself, let him not commit any sin however small
kural.couplet: Beware, if to thyself thyself is dear,Lest thou to aught that ranks as ill draw near

kural.Translation: He is secure, know ye, from ills  Who slips not right path to do evils
kural.explanation: Know ye that he is freed from destruction who commits no evil, going to neither side of the right path
kural.couplet: The man, to devious way of sin that never turned aside,From ruin rests secure, whatever ills betide

kural.Translation: Duty demands nothing in turn;  How can the world recompense rain?
kural.explanation: Benevolence seeks not a return. What does the world give back to the clouds ?
kural.couplet: Duty demands no recompense; to clouds of heaven,By men on earth, what answering gift is given

kural.Translation: All the wealth that toils give  Is meant to serve those who deserve
kural.explanation: All the wealth acquired with perseverance by the worthy is for the exercise of benevolence
kural.couplet: The worthy say, when wealth rewards their toil-spent hours,For uses of beneficence alone 'tis ours

kural.Translation: In heav'n and earth 'tis hard to find  A greater good than being kind
kural.explanation: It is difficult to obtain another good equal to benevolence either in this world or in that of the gods
kural.couplet: To 'due beneficence' no equal good we know,Amid the happy gods, or in this world below

kural.Translation: He lives who knows befitting act  Others are deemed as dead in fact
kural.explanation: He truly lives who knows (and discharges) the proper duties (of benevolence) He who knows them not will be reckoned among the dead
kural.couplet: Who knows what's human life's befitting grace,He lives; the rest 'mongst dead men have their place

kural.Translation: The wealth that wise and kind do make  Is like water that fills a lake
kural.explanation: The wealth of that man of eminent knowledge who desires to exercise the benevolence approved of by the world, is like the full waters of a city-tank
kural.couplet: The wealth of men who love the 'fitting way,' the truly wise,Is as when water fills the lake that village needs supplies

kural.Translation: Who plenty gets and plenty gives  Is like town-tree teeming with fruits
kural.explanation: The wealth of a man (possessed of the virtue) of benevolence is like the ripening of a fruitful tree in the midst of a town
kural.couplet: A tree that fruits in th' hamlet's central mart,Is wealth that falls to men of liberal heart

kural.Translation: The wealth of a wide-hearted soul  Is a herbal tree that healeth all
kural.explanation: If wealth be in the possession of a man who has the great excellence (of benevolence), it is like a tree which as a medicine is an infallible cure for disease
kural.couplet: Unfailing tree that healing balm distils from every part,Is ample wealth that falls to him of large and noble heart

kural.Translation: Though seers may fall on evil days  Their sense of duty never strays
kural.explanation: The wise who know what is duty will not scant their benevolence even when they are without wealth
kural.couplet: E'en when resources fall, they weary not of 'kindness due,'-They to whom Duty's self appears in vision true

kural.Translation: The good man's poverty and grief  Is want of means to give relief
kural.explanation: The poverty of a benevolent man, is nothing but his inability to exercise the same
kural.couplet: The kindly-hearted man is poor in this alone,When power of doing deeds of goodness he finds none

kural.Translation: By good if ruin comes across  Sell yourself to save that loss
kural.explanation: If it be said that loss will result from benevolence, such loss is worth being procured even by the sale of one's self
kural.couplet: Though by 'beneficence,' the loss of all should come,'Twere meet man sold himself, and bought it with the sum

kural.Translation: To give the poor is charity  The rest is loan and vanity
kural.explanation: To give to the destitute is true charity All other gifts have the nature of (what is done for) a measured return
kural.couplet: Call that a gift to needy men thou dost dispense,All else is void of good, seeking for recompense

kural.Translation: To beg is bad e'en from the good  To give is good, were heaven forbid
kural.explanation: To beg is evil, even though it were said that it is a good path (to heaven) To give is good, even though it were said that those who do so cannot obtain heaven
kural.couplet: Though men declare it heavenward path, yet to receive is ill;Though upper heaven were not, to give is virtue still

kural.Translation: No pleading, \"I am nothing worth,\"  But giving marks a noble birth
kural.explanation: (Even in a low state) not to adopt the mean expedient of saying "I have nothing," but to give, is the characteristic of the mad of noble birth
kural.couplet: 'I've nought' is ne'er the high-born man's reply;He gives to those who raise themselves that cry

kural.Translation: The cry for alms is painful sight  Until the giver sees him bright
kural.explanation: To see men begging from us in disagreeable, until we see their pleasant countenance
kural.couplet: The suppliants' cry for aid yields scant delight,Until you see his face with grateful gladness bright

kural.Translation: Higher's power which hunger cures  Than that of penance which endures
kural.explanation: The power of those who perform penance is the power of enduring hunger It is inferior to the power of those who remove the hunger (of others)
kural.couplet: 'Mid devotees they're great who hunger's pangs sustain,Who hunger's pangs relieve a higher merit gain

kural.Translation: Drive from the poor their gnawing pains  If room you seek to store your gains
kural.explanation: The removal of the killing hunger of the poor is the place for one to lay up his wealth
kural.couplet: Let man relieve the wasting hunger men endure;For treasure gained thus finds he treasure-house secure

kural.Translation: Who shares his food with those who need  Hunger shall not harm his creed
kural.explanation: The fiery disease of hunger shall never touch him who habitually distributes his food to others
kural.couplet: Whose soul delights with hungry men to share his meal,The hand of hunger's sickness sore shall never feel

kural.Translation: The joy of give and take they lose  Hard-hearted rich whose hoarding fails
kural.explanation: Do the hard-eyed who lay up and lose their possessions not know the happiness which springs from the pleasure of giving ?
kural.couplet: Delight of glad'ning human hearts with gifts do they not know.Men of unpitying eye, who hoard their wealth and lose it so

kural.Translation: Worse than begging is that boarding  Alone what one's greed is hoarding
kural.explanation: Solitary and unshared eating for the sake of filling up one's own riches is certainly much more
kural.couplet: They keep their garners full, for self alone the board they spread;-'Tis greater pain, be sure, than begging daily bread

kural.Translation: Nothing is more painful than death  Yet more is pain of giftless dearth
kural.explanation: Nothing is more unpleasant than death: yet even that is pleasant where charity cannot be exercised
kural.couplet: 'Tis bitter pain to die, 'Tis worse to live.For him who nothing finds to give

kural.Translation: They gather fame who freely give  The greatest gain for all that live
kural.explanation: Give to the poor and live with praise There is no greater profit to man than that
kural.couplet: See that thy life the praise of generous gifts obtain;Save this for living man exists no real gain

kural.Translation: The glory of the alms-giver  Is praised aloud as popular
kural.explanation: Whatsoever is spoken in the world will abide as praise upon that man who gives alms to the poor
kural.couplet: The speech of all that speak agrees to crownThe men that give to those that ask, with fair renown

kural.Translation: Nothing else lasts on earth for e'er  Saving high fame of the giver!
kural.explanation: There is nothing that stands forth in the world imperishable, except fame, exalted in solitary greatness
kural.couplet: Save praise alone that soars on high,Nought lives on earth that shall not die

kural.Translation: From hailing gods heavens will cease  To hail the men of lasting praise
kural.explanation: If one has acquired extensive fame within the limits of this earth, the world of the Gods will no longer praise those sages who have attained that world
kural.couplet: If men do virtuous deeds by world-wide ample glory crowned,The heavens will cease to laud the sage for other gifts renowned

kural.Translation: Fame in fall and life in death  Are rare but for the soulful worth
kural.explanation: Prosperity to the body of fame, resulting in poverty to the body of flesh and the stability to the former arising from the death of the latter, are achievable only by the wise
kural.couplet: Loss that is gain, and death of life's true bliss fulfilled,Are fruits which only wisdom rare can yield

kural.Translation: Be born with fame if birth you want  If not of birth you must not vaunt
kural.explanation: If you are born (in this world), be born with qualities conductive to fame From those who are destitute of them it will be better not to be born
