kural.couplet: If man you walk the stage, appear adorned with glory's grace;Save glorious you can shine, 'twere better hide your face

kural.Translation: Why grieve at those who blame the shame  Of those who cannot live in fame?
kural.explanation: Why do those who cannot live with praise, grieve those who despise them, instead of grieving themselves for their own inability
kural.couplet: If you your days will spend devoid of goodly fame,When men despise, why blame them? You've yourself to blame

kural.Translation: To men on earth it is a shame  Not to beget the child of fame
kural.explanation: Not to beget fame will be esteemed a disgrace by the wise in this world
kural.couplet: Fame is virtue's child, they say; if, then,You childless live, you live the scorn of men

kural.Translation: The land will shrink in yield if men  O'erburden it without renown
kural.explanation: The ground which supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce
kural.couplet: The blameless fruits of fields' increase will dwindle down,If earth the burthen bear of men without renown

kural.Translation: They live who live without blemish  The blameful ones do not flurish
kural.explanation: Those live who live without disgrace Those who live without fame live not
kural.couplet: Who live without reproach, them living men we deem;Who live without renown, live not, though living men they seem

kural.Translation: The wealth of wealth is wealth of grace  Earthly wealth e'en the basest has
kural.explanation: The wealth of kindness is wealth of wealth, in as much as the wealth of property is possessed by the basest of men
kural.couplet: Wealth 'mid wealth is wealth 'kindliness';Wealth of goods the vilest too possess

kural.Translation: Seek by sound ways good compassion;  All faiths mark that for-salvation
kural.explanation: (Stand) in the good path, consider, and be kind. Even considering according to the conflicting tenets of the different sects, kindness will be your best aid, (in the acquisition of heavenly bliss.)
kural.couplet: The law of 'grace' fulfil, by methods good due trial made,Though many systems you explore, this is your only aid

kural.Translation: The hearts of mercy shall not go  Into dark worlds of gruesome woe
kural.explanation: They will never enter the world of darkness and wretchedness whose minds are the abode of kindness
kural.couplet: They in whose breast a 'gracious kindliness' resides,See not the gruesome world, where darkness drear abides

kural.Translation: His soul is free from dread of sins  Whose mercy serveth all beings
kural.explanation: (The wise) say that the evils, which his soul would dread, will never come upon the man who exercises kindness and protects the life (of other creatures)
kural.couplet: Who for undying souls of men provides with gracious zeal,In his own soul the dreaded guilt of sin shall never feel

kural.Translation: The wide wind-fed world witness bears:  Men of mercy meet not sorrows
kural.explanation: This great rich earth over which the wind blows, is a witness that sorrow never comes upon the kindhearted
kural.couplet: The teeming earth's vast realm, round which the wild winds blow,Is witness, men of 'grace' no woeful want shall know

kural.Translation: Who grace forsake and graceless act  The former loss and woes forget
kural.explanation: (The wise) say that those who neglect kindness and practise cruelties, neglected virtue (in their former birth), and forgot (the sorrows which they must suffer.)
kural.couplet: Gain of true wealth oblivious they eschew,Who 'grace' forsake, and graceless actions do

kural.Translation: This world is not for weathless ones  That world is not for graceless swines
kural.explanation: As this world is not for those who are without wealth, so that world is not for those who are without kindness
kural.couplet: As to impoverished men this present world is not;The 'graceless' in you world have neither part nor lot

kural.Translation: The wealthless may prosper one day;  The graceless never bloom agay
kural.explanation: Those who are without wealth may, at some future time, become prosperous; those who are destitute of kindness are utterly destitute; for them there is no change
kural.couplet: Who lose the flower of wealth, when seasons change, again may bloom;Who lose 'benevolence', lose all; nothing can change their doom

kural.Translation: Like Truth twisted by confused mind  Wisdom is vain in hearts unkind
kural.explanation: If you consider, the virtue of him who is without kindness is like the perception of the true being by him who is without wisdom
kural.couplet: When souls unwise true wisdom's mystic vision see,The 'graceless' man may work true works of charity

kural.Translation: Think how you feel before the strong  When to the feeble you do wrong
kural.explanation: When a man is about to rush upon those who are weaker than himself, let him remember how he has stood (trembling) before those who are stronger than himself
kural.couplet: When weaker men you front with threat'ning brow,Think how you felt in presence of some stronger foe

kural.Translation: What graciousness can one command  who feeds his flesh by flesh gourmand
kural.explanation: How can he be possessed of kindness, who to increase his own flesh, eats the flesh of other creatures
kural.couplet: How can the wont of 'kindly grace' to him be known,Who other creatures' flesh consumes to feed his own

kural.Translation: The thriftless have no property  And flesh-eaters have no pity
kural.explanation: As those possess no property who do not take care of it, so those possess no kindness who feed on flesh
kural.couplet: No use of wealth have they who guard not their estate;No use of grace have they with flesh who hunger sate

kural.Translation: Who wields a steel is steel-hearted  Who tastes body is hard-hearted
kural.explanation: Like the (murderous) mind of him who carries a weapon (in his hand), the mind of him who feasts with pleasure on the body of another (creature), has no regard for goodness
kural.couplet: Like heart of them that murderous weapons bear, his mind,Who eats of savoury meat, no joy in good can find

kural.Translation: If merciless it is to kill,  To kill and eat is disgraceful
kural.explanation: If it be asked what is kindness and what its opposite, the answer would be preservation and destruction of life; and therefore it is not right to feed on the flesh (obtained by taking away life)
kural.couplet: 'What's grace, or lack of grace'? 'To kill' is this, that 'not to kill';To eat dead flesh can never worthy end fulfil

kural.Translation: Off with flesh; a life you save  The eater hell's mouth shall not waive!
kural.explanation: Not to eat flesh contributes to the continuance of life; therefore if a man eat flesh, hell will not open its mouth (to let him escape out, after he has once fallen in)
kural.couplet: If flesh you eat not, life's abodes unharmed remain;Who eats, hell swallows him, and renders not again

kural.Translation: None would kill and sell the flesh  For eating it if they don't wish
kural.explanation: If the world does not destroy life for the purpose of eating, then no one would sell flesh for the sake of money
kural.couplet: 'We eat the slain,' you say, by us no living creatures die;Who'd kill and sell, I pray, if none came there the flesh to buy

kural.Translation: From eating flesh men must abstain  If they but feel the being's pain
kural.explanation: If men should come to know that flesh is nothing but the unclean ulcer of a body, let them abstain from eating it
kural.couplet: With other beings' ulcerous wounds their hunger they appease;If this they felt, desire to eat must surely cease

kural.Translation: Whose mind from illusion is freed  Refuse on lifeless flesh to feed
kural.explanation: The wise, who have freed themselves from mental delusion, will not eat the flesh which has been severed from an animal
kural.couplet: Whose souls the vision pure and passionless perceive,Eat not the bodies men of life bereave

kural.Translation: Not to-kill-and-eat, truly  Excels thousand pourings of ghee!
kural.explanation: Not to kill and eat (the flesh of) an animal, is better than the pouring forth of ghee etc, in a thousand sacrifices
kural.couplet: Than thousand rich oblations, with libations rare,Better the flesh of slaughtered beings not to share

kural.Translation: All lives shall lift their palms to him  Who eats not flesh nor kills with whim
kural.explanation: All creatures will join their hands together, and worship him who has never taken away life, nor eaten flesh
kural.couplet: Who slays nought,- flesh rejects- his feet beforeAll living things with clasped hands adore

kural.Translation: Pains endure; pain not beings  This is the type of true penance
kural.explanation: The nature of religious discipline consists, in the endurance (by the ascetic) of the sufferings which it brings on himself, and in abstaining from giving pain to others
kural.couplet: To bear due penitential pains, while no offenceHe causes others, is the type of 'penitence'

kural.Translation: Penance is fit for penitents  Not for him who in vain pretends
kural.explanation: Austerities can only be borne, and their benefits enjoyed, by those who have practised them (in a former birth); it will be useless for those who have not done so, to attempt to practise them (now)
kural.couplet: To 'penitents' sincere avails their 'penitence';Where that is not, 'tis but a vain pretence

kural.Translation: Is it to true penitent's aid,  That others austere path avoid?
kural.explanation: It is to provide food etc, for the ascetics who have abandoned (the desire of earthly possessions) that other persons have forgotten (to practise) austerity ?
kural.couplet: Have other men forgotten 'penitence' who striveTo earn for penitents the things by which they live

kural.Translation: In penance lies the power to save  The friends and foil the foe and knave
kural.explanation: If (the ascetic) desire the destruction of his enemies, or the aggrandizement of his friends, it will be effected by (the power of) his austerities
kural.couplet: Destruction to his foes, to friends increase of joyThe 'penitent' can cause, if this his thoughts employ

kural.Translation: What they wish as they wish is won  Here hence by men penance is done
kural.explanation: Religious dislipline is practised in this world, because it secures the attainment of whatever one may wish to enjoy (in the world to come)
kural.couplet: That what they wish may, as they wish, be won,By men on earth are works of painful 'penance' done

kural.Translation: Who do penance achieve their aim  Others desire-rid themselves harm
kural.explanation: Those discharge their duty who perform austerities; all others accomplish their own destruction, through the entanglement of the desire (of riches and sensual pleasure)
kural.couplet: Who works of 'penance' do, their end attain,Others in passion's net enshared, toil but in vain

kural.Translation: Pure and bright gets the gold in fire;  and so the life by pain austere
kural.explanation: Just as gold is purified as heated in the fire, will those shine, who have endured the burning of pain (in frequent austerities)
kural.couplet: The hotter glows the fining fire, the gold the brighter shines;The pain of penitence, like fire, the soul of man refines

kural.Translation: He worship wins from every soul  Who Master is by soul control
kural.explanation: All other creatures will worship him who has attained the control of his own soul
kural.couplet: Who gains himself in utter self-control,Him worships every other living soul

kural.Translation: They can even defy death  Who get by penance godly strenth
kural.explanation: Those who have attained the power which religious discipline confers, will be able also to pass the limit of Yama, (the God of death)
kural.couplet: E'en over death the victory he may gain,If power by penance won his soul obtain

kural.Translation: Many are poor and few are rich  For they care not for penance much
kural.explanation: Because there are few who practise austerity and many who do not, there are many destitute and few rich in this world
kural.couplet: The many all things lack! The cause is plain,The 'penitents' are few The many shun such pain

kural.Translation: Elements five of feigned life  Of a sly hypocrite within laugh
kural.explanation: The five elements (of his body) will laugh within him at the feigned conduct of the deceitful minded man
kural.couplet: Who with deceitful mind in false way walks of covert sin,The five-fold elements his frame compose, decide within

kural.Translation: Of what avail are sky-high shows  When guild the conscience gnaws and knows
kural.explanation: What avails an appearance (of sanctity) high as heaven, if his mind suffers (the indulgence) of conscious sin
kural.couplet: What gain, though virtue's semblance high as heaven his fame exalt,If heart dies down through sense of self-detected fault

kural.Translation: Vaunting sainthood while week within  Seems a grazer with tiger skin
kural.explanation: The assumed appearance of power, by a man who has no power (to restrain his senses and perform austerity), is like a cow feeding on grass covered with a tiger's skin
kural.couplet: As if a steer should graze wrapped round with tiger's skin,Is show of virtuous might when weakness lurks within

kural.Translation: Sinning in saintly show is like  Fowlers in ambush birds to strike
kural.explanation: He who hides himself under the mask of an ascetic and commits sins, like a sportsman who conceals himself in the thicket to catch birds
kural.couplet: 'Tis as a fowler, silly birds to snare, in thicket lurksWhen, clad in stern ascetic garb, one secret evil works

kural.Translation: Who false within but freedom feign  Shall moan \"What have we done\" with pain
kural.explanation: The false conduct of those who say they have renounced all desire will one day bring them sorrows that will make them cry out, "Oh! what have we done, what have we done."
kural.couplet: 'Our souls are free,' who say, yet practise evil secretly,'What folly have we wrought!' by many shames o'er-whelmed, shall cry

kural.Translation: Vilest is he who seems a saint  Cheating the world without restraint
kural.explanation: Amongst living men there are none so hard-hearted as those who without to saking (desire) in their heart, falsely take the appearance of those who have forsaken (it)
kural.couplet: In mind renouncing nought, in speech renouncing every tie,Who guileful live,- no men are found than these of 'harder eye'

kural.Translation: Berry-red is his outward view,  Black like its nose his inward hue
kural.explanation: (The world) contains persons whose outside appears (as fair) as the (red) berry of the Abrus, but whose inside is as black as the nose of that berry
kural.couplet: Outward, they shine as 'kunri' berry's scarlet bright;Inward, like tip of 'kunri' bead, as black as night

kural.Translation: Filthy in mind some bathe in streams  Hiding sins in showy extremes
kural.explanation: There are many men of masked conduct, who perform their ablutions, and (make a show) of
kural.couplet: Many wash in hollowed waters, living lives of hidden shame;Foul in heart, yet high upraised of men in virtuous fame

kural.Translation: Know men by acts and not by forms  Strait arrow kills, bent lute but charms
kural.explanation: As, in its use, the arrow is crooked, and the curved lute is straight, so by their deeds, (and not by their appearance) let (the uprightness or crookedness of) men be estimated
kural.couplet: Cruel is the arrow straight, the crooked lute is sweet,Judge by their deeds the many forms of men you meet

kural.Translation: No balding nor tangling the hair!  Abstain from condemned acts with care
kural.explanation: There is no need of a shaven crown, nor of tangled hair, if a man abstain from those deeds which the wise have condemned
kural.couplet: What's the worth of shaven head or tresses long,If you shun what all the world condemns as wrong

kural.Translation: Let him who would reproachless be  From all frauds guard his conscience free
kural.explanation: Let him, who desires not to be despised, keep his mind from (the desire of) defrauding another of the smallest thing
kural.couplet: Who seeks heaven's joys, from impious levity secure,Let him from every fraud preserve his spirit pure

kural.Translation: \"We will by fraud win other's wealth\"  Even this thought is sin and stealth
kural.explanation: Even the thought (of sin) is sin; think not then of crafiily stealing the property of another
kural.couplet: 'Tis sin if in the mind man but thought conceive;'By fraud I will my neighbour of his wealth bereave.'

kural.Translation: The gain by fraud may overflow  But swift to ruin it shall go
kural.explanation: The property, which is acquired by fraud, will entirely perish, even while it seems to increase
kural.couplet: The gain that comes by fraud, although it seems to growWith limitless increase, to ruin swift shall go

kural.Translation: The fruit that fraud and greed obtain  Shall end in endless grief and pain
kural.explanation: The eager desire of defrauding others will, when it brings forth its fruit, produce undying sorrow
kural.couplet: The lust inveterate of fraudful gain,Yields as its fruit undying pain

kural.Translation: Love and Grace are not their worth  Who watch to waylay dozer's wealth
kural.explanation: The study of kindness and the exercise of benevolence is not with those who watch for another's forgetfulness, though desire of his property
kural.couplet: 'Grace' is not in their thoughts, nor know they kind affection's power,Who neighbour's goods desire, and watch for his unguarded hour

kural.Translation: They cannot walk in measured bounds  who crave and have covetous ends
kural.explanation: They cannot walk steadfastly, according to rule, who eagerly desire to defraud others
kural.couplet: They cannot walk restrained in wisdom's measured bound,In whom inveterate lust of fraudful gain is found

kural.Translation: Men of measured wisdom shun  Black art of fraud and what it won
kural.explanation: That black-knowledge which is called fraud, is not in those who desire that greatness which is called rectitude
kural.couplet: Practice of fraud's dark cunning arts they shun,Who long for power by 'measured wisdom' won

kural.Translation: Virtue abides in righteous hearts  Into minds of frauds deceit darts
kural.explanation: Deceit dwells in the mind of those who are conversant with fraud, even as virtue in the minds of those who are conversant with rectitude
kural.couplet: As virtue dwells in heart that 'measured wisdom' gains;Deceit in hearts of fraudful men established reigns

kural.Translation: They perish in their perfidy  Who know nothing but pilfery
kural.explanation: Those, who are acquainted with nothing but fraud, will perish in the very commission of transgression
kural.couplet: Who have no lore save that which fraudful arts supply,Acts of unmeasured vice committing straightway die

kural.Translation: Even the body rejects thieves;  The honest men, heaven receives
kural.explanation: Even their body will fail the fraudulent; but even the world of the gods will not fail those who are free from fraud
kural.couplet: The fraudful forfeit life and being here below;Who fraud eschew the bliss of heavenly beings know

kural.Translation: If \"What is truth\"? the question be,  It is to speak out evil-free
kural.explanation: Truth is the speaking of such words as are free from the least degree of evil (to others)
kural.couplet: You ask, in lips of men what 'truth' may be;'Tis speech from every taint of evil free

kural.Translation: E'en falsehood may for truth suffice,  When good it brings removing vice
kural.explanation: Even falsehood has the nature of truth, if it confer a benefit that is free from fault
kural.couplet: Falsehood may take the place of truthful word,If blessing, free from fault, it can afford

kural.Translation: Let not a man knowingly lie;  Conscience will scorch and make him sigh
kural.explanation: Let not a man knowingly tell a lie; for after he has told the lie, his mind will burn him (with the memory of his guilt)
kural.couplet: Speak not a word which false thy own heart knowsSelf-kindled fire within the false one's spirit glows

kural.Translation: He lives in loving hearts of all  Who serves the Truth serene in soul
kural.explanation: He who, in his conduct, preserves a mind free from deceit, will dwell in the minds of all men
kural.couplet: True to his inmost soul who lives,- enshrinedHe lives in souls of all mankind

kural.Translation: To speak the truth from heart sincere  Is more than giving and living austere
kural.explanation: He, who speaks truth with all his heart, is superior to those who make gifts and practise austerities
kural.couplet: Greater is he who speaks the truth with full consenting mindThan men whose lives have penitence and charity combined

kural.Translation: Not to lie brings all the praise  All virtues from Truth arise
kural.explanation: There is no praise like the praise of never uttering a falsehood: without causing any suffering, it will lead to every virtue
kural.couplet: No praise like that of words from falsehood free;This every virtue yields spontaneously

kural.Translation: Lie not lie not Naught else you need  All virtues are in Truth indeed
kural.explanation: If a man has the power to abstain from falsehood, it will be well with him, even though he practise no other virtue
kural.couplet: If all your life be utter truth, the truth alone,'Tis well, though other virtuous acts be left undone

kural.Translation: Water makes you pure outward  Truth renders you pure inward
kural.explanation: Purity of body is produced by water and purity of mind by truthfulness
kural.couplet: Outward purity the water will bestow;Inward purity from truth alone will flow

kural.Translation: All lights are not lights for the wise;  Truth light is light bright like Sun-light
kural.explanation: All lamps of nature are not lamps; the lamp of truth is the lamp of the wise
kural.couplet: Every lamp is not a lamp in wise men's sight;That's the lamp with truth's pure radiance bright

kural.Translation: Of all the things we here have seen  Nothing surpasses Truth serene!
kural.explanation: Amidst all that we have seen (described) as real (excellence), there is nothing so good as truthfulness
kural.couplet: Of all good things we've scanned with studious care,There's nought that can with truthfulness compare

kural.Translation: Anger against the weak is wrong  It is futile against the strong
kural.explanation: He restrains his anger who restrains it when it can injure; when it cannot injure, what does it matter whether he restrain it, or not ?
kural.couplet: Where thou hast power thy angry will to work, thy wrath restrain;Where power is none, what matter if thou check or give it rein

kural.Translation: Vain is wrath against men of force  Against the meek it is still worse
kural.explanation: Anger is bad, even when it cannot injure; when it can injure; there is no greater evil
kural.couplet: Where power is none to wreak thy wrath, wrath importent is ill;Where thou hast power thy will to work, 'tis greater, evil still

kural.Translation: Off with wrath with any one  It is the source of sin and pain
kural.explanation: Forget anger towards every one, as fountains of evil spring from it
kural.couplet: If any rouse thy wrath, the trespass straight forget;For wrath an endless train of evils will beget

kural.Translation: Is there a foe like harmful ire  Which kills the smile and joyful cheer?
kural.explanation: What other foe to man works such annoy?
kural.couplet: Wrath robs the face of smiles, the heart of joy,What other foe to man works such annoy

kural.Translation: Thyself to save, from wrath away!  If not thyself the wrath will slay
kural.explanation: If a man would guard himself, let him guard against anger; if he do not guard it, anger will kill him
kural.couplet: If thou would'st guard thyself, guard against wrath alway;'Gainst wrath who guards not, him his wrath shall slay

kural.Translation: Friend-killer is the fatal rage  It burns the helpful kinship-barge
kural.explanation: The fire of anger will burn up even the pleasant raft of friendship
kural.couplet: Wrath, the fire that slayeth whose draweth near,Will burn the helpful 'raft' of kindred dear

kural.Translation: The wrath-lover to doom is bound  Like failless-hand that strikes the ground
kural.explanation: Destruction will come upon him who ragards anger as a good thing, as surely as the hand of him who strikes the ground will not fail
kural.couplet: The hand that smites the earth unfailing feels the sting;So perish they who nurse their wrath as noble thing

kural.Translation: Save thy soul from burning ire  Though tortured like the touch of fire
kural.explanation: Though one commit things against you as painful (to bear) as if a bundle of fire had been thrust upon you, it will be well, to refrain, if possible, from anger
kural.couplet: Though men should work thee woe, like touch of tongues of fire'Tis well if thou canst save thy soul from burning ire

kural.Translation: Wishes he gains as he wishes  If man refrains from rage vicious!
kural.explanation: If a man never indulges anger in his heart, he will at once obtain whatever he has thought of
kural.couplet: If man his soul preserve from wrathful fires,He gains with that whate'er his soul desires

kural.Translation: Dead are they who are anger-fed  Saints are they from whom wrath has fled
kural.explanation: Those, who give way to excessive anger, are no better than dead men; but those, who are freed from it, are equal to those who are freed (from death)
kural.couplet: Men of surpassing wrath are like the men who've passed away;Who wrath renounce, equals of all-renouncing sages they

kural.Translation: The pure by faith mean pain to none  Though princely wealth by that is won
kural.explanation: It is the determination of the spotless not to cause sorrow to others, although they could (by so causing) obtain the wealth which confers greatness
kural.couplet: Though ill to neighbour wrought should glorious pride of wealth secure,No ill to do is fixed decree of men in spirit pure

kural.Translation: The spotless hearts seek not revenge  Though Malice does the worst in rage
kural.explanation: It is the determination of the spotless not to do evil, even in return, to those who have cherished enmity and done them evil
kural.couplet: Though malice work its worst, planning no ill return, to endure,And work no ill, is fixed decree of men in spirit pure

kural.Translation: Revenging even causeless hate  Bad-blood breeds and baneful heat
kural.explanation: In an ascetic inflict suffering even on those who hate him, when he has not done them any evil, it will afterwards give him irretrievable sorrow
kural.couplet: Though unprovoked thy soul malicious foes should sting,Retaliation wrought inevitable woes will bring

kural.Translation: Doing good-turns, put them to shame  Thus chide the evil who do harm
kural.explanation: The (proper) punishment to those who have done evil (to you), is to put them to shame by showing them kindness, in return and to forget both the evil and the good done on both sides
kural.couplet: To punish wrong, with kindly benefits the doers ply;Thus shame their souls; but pass the ill unheeded by

kural.Translation: What does a man from wisdom gain  If he pines not at other's pain?
kural.explanation: What benefit has he derived from his knowledge, who does not endeavour to keep off pain from another as much as from himself ?
kural.couplet: From wisdom's vaunted lore what doth the learner gain,If as his own he guard not others' souls from pain

kural.Translation: What you feel as pain to yourself  Do it not to the other-self
kural.explanation: Let not a man consent to do those things to another which, he knows, will cause sorrow
kural.couplet: What his own soul has felt as bitter pain,From making others feel should man abstain

kural.Translation: Any, anywhere injure not  At any time even in thought
kural.explanation: It is the chief of all virtues not knowingly to do any person evil, even in the lowest degree, and at any time
kural.couplet: To work no wilful woe, in any wise, through all the days,To any living soul, is virtue's highest praise

kural.Translation: How can he injure other souls  Who in his life injury feels
kural.explanation: Why does a man inflict upon other creatures those sufferings, which he has found by experience are sufferings to himself ?
kural.couplet: Whose soul has felt the bitter smart of wrong, how canHe wrongs inflict on ever-living soul of man

kural.Translation: Harm others in the forenoon  Harm seeks thee in afternoon
kural.explanation: If a man inflict sorrow upon others in the morning, it will come upon him unsought in the very evening
kural.couplet: If, ere the noontide, you to others evil do,Before the eventide will evil visit you

kural.Translation: No harm is done by peace-lovers  For pains rebound on pain-givers
kural.explanation: Sorrow will come upon those who cause pain to others; therfore those, who desire to be free from sorrow, give no pain to others
kural.couplet: O'er every evil-doer evil broodeth still;He evil shuns who freedom seeks from ill

kural.Translation: What is Virtue? 'Tis not to kill  For killing causes every ill
kural.explanation: Never to destroy life is the sum of all virtuous conduct The destruction of life leads to every evil
kural.couplet: What is the work of virtue? 'Not to kill';For 'killing' leads to every work of ill

kural.Translation: Share the food and serve all lives  This is the law of all the laws
kural.explanation: The chief of all (the virtues) which authors have summed up, is the partaking of food that has been shared with others, and the preservation of the mainfold life of other creatures
kural.couplet: Let those that need partake your meal; guard every-thing that lives;This the chief and sum of lore that hoarded wisdom gives

kural.Translation: Not to kill is unique good  The next, not to utter falsehood
kural.explanation: Not to destroy life is an incomparably (great) good next to it in goodness ranks freedom from falsehood
kural.couplet: Alone, first of goods things, is 'not to slay';The second is, no untrue word to say

kural.Translation: What way is good? That we can say  The way away from heat to slay
kural.explanation: Good path is that which considers how it may avoid killing any creature
kural.couplet: You ask, What is the good and perfect way?'Tis path of him who studies nought to slay

kural.Translation: Of saints who renounce birth-fearing  The head is he who dreads killing
kural.explanation: Of all those who, fearing the permanence of earthly births, have abandoned desire, he is the chief who, fearing (the guilt of) murder, considers how he may avoid the destruction of life
kural.couplet: Of those who 'being' dread, and all renounce, the chief are they,Who dreading crime of slaughter, study nought to slay

kural.Translation: Life-eating-Death shall spare the breath  Of him who no life puts to death
kural.explanation: Yama, the destroyer of life, will not attack the life of him, who acts under the determination of never destroying life
kural.couplet: Ev'n death that life devours, their happy days shall spare,Who law, 'Thou shall not kill', uphold with reverent care

kural.Translation: Kill not life that others cherish  Even when your life must perish
kural.explanation: Let no one do that which would destroy the life of another, although he should by so doing, lose his own life
kural.couplet: Though thine own life for that spared life the price must pay,Take not from aught that lives gift of sweet life away

kural.Translation: The gain of slaughter is a vice  Though deemed good in sacrifice
kural.explanation: The advantage which might flow from destroying life in sacrifice, is dishonourable to the wise (who renounced the world), even although it should be said to be productive of great good
kural.couplet: Though great the gain of good should seem, the wiseWill any gain by staughter won despise

kural.Translation: Those who live by slaying are  Eaters of carrion bizarre!
kural.explanation: To minds of them who what is vileness know
kural.couplet: Whose trade is 'killing', always vile they show,To minds of them who what is vileness know

kural.Translation: The loathsome poor sickly and sore  Are killers stained by blood before
kural.explanation: (The wise) will say that men of diseased bodies, who live in degradation and in poverty, are those who separated the life from the body of animals (in a former birth)
kural.couplet: Who lead a loathed life in bodies sorely pained,Are men, the wise declare, by guilt of slaughter stained

kural.Translation: The worst of follies it is told  The fleeting as lasting to hold
kural.explanation: That ignorance which considers those things to be stable which are not so, is dishonourable (to the wise)
kural.couplet: Lowest and meanest lore, that bids men trust secure,In things that pass away, as things that shall endure

kural.Translation: Like a drama-crowd wealth gathers  Like passing show its pride too goes
kural.explanation: The acquisition of wealth is like the gathering together of an assembly for a theatre; its expenditure is like the breaking up of that assembly
kural.couplet: As crowds round dancers fill the hall, is wealth's increase;Its loss, as throngs dispersing, when the dances cease

kural.Translation: Wealth wanes away; but when it comes  Take care to do enduring things
kural.explanation: Wealth is perishable; let those who obtain it immediately practise those (virtues) which are imperishable
kural.couplet: Unenduring is all wealth; if you wealth enjoy,Enduring works in working wealth straightway employ

kural.Translation: The showy day is but a saw  Your life, know that, to file and gnaw
kural.explanation: Time, which shows itself (to the ignorant) as if it were something (real) is in the estimation of the wise (only) a saw which cuts down life
kural.couplet: As 'day' it vaunts itself; well understood, 'tis knife',That daily cuts away a portion from thy life

kural.Translation: Ere tongue benumbs and hiccough comes  Rise up to do good deeds betimes
kural.explanation: Let virtuous deeds be done quickly, before the hiccup comes making the tongue silent
kural.couplet: Before the tongue lie powerless, 'mid the gasp of gurgling breath,Arouse thyself, and do good deeds beyond the power of death

kural.Translation: One was yesterday; not today!
kural.explanation: This world possesses the greatness that one who yesterday was is not today
kural.couplet: Existing yesterday, today to nothing hurled!-Such greatness owns this transitory world

kural.Translation: Man knows not his next moment  On crores of things he is intent
kural.explanation: Innumerable are the thoughts which occupy the mind of (the unwise), who know not that they shall live another moment
kural.couplet: Who know not if their happy lives shall last the day,In fancies infinite beguile the hours away

kural.Translation: The soul from body any day  Like bird from egg-shell flies away
kural.explanation: The love of the soul to the body is like (the love of) a bird to its egg which it flies away from and leaves empty
kural.couplet: Birds fly away, and leave the nest deserted bare;Such is the short-lived friendship soul and body share

kural.Translation: Death is like a slumber deep  And birth like waking from that sleep
kural.explanation: Death is like sleep; birth is like awaking from it
kural.couplet: Death is sinking into slumbers deep;Birth again is waking out of sleep

kural.Translation: The life berthed in this body shows  A fixed home it never knows
kural.explanation: It seems as if the soul, which takes a temporary shelter in a body, had not attained a home
kural.couplet: The soul in fragile shed as lodger courts repose:-Is it because no home's conclusive rest it knows

kural.Translation: From what from what a man is free  From that, from that his torments flee
kural.explanation: Whatever thing, a man has renounced, by that thing; he cannot suffer pain
kural.couplet: From whatever, aye, whatever, man gets free,From what, aye, from that, no more of pain hath he

kural.Translation: Give up all to gain the True  And endless joys shall hence seek you
kural.explanation: After a man has renounced (all things), there will still be many things in this world (which he may enjoy); if he should desire them, let him, while it is time abandon (the world)
kural.couplet: 'Renunciation' made- ev'n here true pleasures men acquire;'Renounce' while time is yet, if to those pleasures you aspire

kural.Translation: Curb the senses five and renounce  The carving desires all at once
kural.explanation: Let the five senses be destroyed; and at the same time, let everything be abandoned that (the ascetic) has (formerly) desired
kural.couplet: 'Perceptions of the five' must all expire;-Relinquished in its order each desire

kural.Translation: To have nothing is law of vows  Having the least deludes and snares
kural.explanation: To be altogether destitute is the proper condition of those who perform austerities; if they possess anything, it will change (their resolution) and bring them back to their confused state
kural.couplet: 'Privation absolute' is penance true;'Possession' brings bewilderment anew

kural.Translation: Why add to bonds while this body  Is too much for saints to be birth-free
kural.explanation: What means the addition of other things those who are attempting to cut off (future) births, when even their body is too much (for them)
kural.couplet: To those who sev'rance seek from being's varied strife,Flesh is burthen sore; what then other bonds of life

kural.Translation: Who curbs the pride of I and mine  Gets a world rare for gods to gain
kural.explanation: Shall enter realms above the powers divine
kural.couplet: Who kills conceit that utters 'I' and 'mine',Shall enter realms above the powers divine

kural.Translation: Grief clings on and on to those  Who cling to bonds without release
kural.explanation: Sorrows will never let go their hold of those who give not up their hold of desire
kural.couplet: Who cling to things that cling and eager clasp,Griefs cling to them with unrelaxing grasp

kural.Translation: Who renounce all are free from care  Others suffer delusive snare
kural.explanation: Those who have entirely renounced (all things and all desire) have obtained (absorption into God); all others wander in confusion, entangled in the net of (many) births
kural.couplet: Who thoroughly 'renounce' on highest height are set;The rest bewildered, lie entangled in the net

kural.Translation: Bondage cut off, rebirth is off  The world then seems instable stuff
kural.explanation: At the moment in which desire has been abandoned, (other) births will be cut off; when that has not been done, instability will be seen
kural.couplet: When that which clings falls off, severed is being's tie;All else will then be seen as instability

kural.Translation: Bind Thyself to the unbound one  That binding breaks all bonds anon
kural.explanation: Desire the desire of Him who is without desire; in order to renounce desire, desire that desire
kural.couplet: Cling thou to that which He, to Whom nought clings, hath bid thee cling,Cling to that bond, to get thee free from every clinging thing

kural.Translation: That error entails ignoble birth  Which deems vain things as things of worth
kural.explanation: Inglorious births are produced by the confusion (of mind) which considers those things to be real which are not real
kural.couplet: Of things devoid of truth as real things men deem;-Cause of degraded birth the fond delusive dream

kural.Translation: Men of spotless pure insight  Enjoy delight devoid of night
kural.explanation: A clear, undimmed vision of things will deliver its possessors from the darkness of future births, and confer the felicity (of heaven)
kural.couplet: Darkness departs, and rapture springs to men who see,The mystic vision pure, from all delusion free

kural.Translation: To doubtless minds whose heart is clear  More than earth heaven is near
kural.explanation: Heaven is nearer than earth to those men of purified minds who are freed from from doubt
kural.couplet: When doubts disperse, and mists of error rollAway, nearer is heav'n than earth to sage's soul

kural.Translation: Knowledge of five senses is vain  Without knowing the Truth within
kural.explanation: Even those who have all the knowledge which can be attained by the five senses, will derive no benefit from it, if they are without a knowledge of the true nature of things
kural.couplet: Five-fold perception gained, what benefits accrueTo them whose spirits lack perception of the true

kural.Translation: Knowledge is truth of things to find  In every case of every kind
kural.explanation: (True) knowledge is the perception concerning every thing of whatever kind, that that thing is the true thing
kural.couplet: Whatever thing, of whatsoever kind it be,'Tis wisdom's part in each the very thing to see

kural.Translation: Who learn and here the Truth discern  Enter the path of non-return
kural.explanation: They, who in this birth have learned to know the True Being, enter the road which returns not into this world
kural.couplet: Who learn, and here the knowledge of the true obtain,Shall find the path that hither cometh not again

kural.Translation: One-minded sage sees inner-truth  He is free from thoughts of rebirth
kural.explanation: Let it not be thought that there is another birth for him whose mind having thoroughly considered (all it has been taught) has known the True Being
kural.couplet: The mind that knows with certitude what is, and ponders well,Its thoughts on birth again to other life need not to dwell

kural.Translation: It is knowledge to know Self-Truth  And remove the folly of birth
kural.explanation: True knowledge consists in the removal of ignorance; which is (the cause of) births, and the perception of the True Being who is (the bestower of) heaven
kural.couplet: When folly, cause of births, departs; and soul can viewThe truth of things, man's dignity- 'tis wisdom true

kural.Translation: Know the Refuge; off with bondage  Be free from ills of thraldom, O sage
kural.explanation: He who so lives as to know Him who is the support of all things and abandon all desire, will be freed from the evils which would otherwise cleave to him and destroy (his efforts after absorption)
kural.couplet: The true 'support' who knows- rejects 'supports' he sought before-Sorrow that clings all destroys, shall cling to him no more

kural.Translation: Woes expire when lust, wrath, folly  Expire even to name, fully
kural.explanation: If the very names of these three things, desire, anger, and confusion of mind, be destroyed, then will also perish evils (which flow from them)
kural.couplet: When lust and wrath and error's triple tyranny is o'er,Their very names for aye extinct, then pain shall be no more

kural.Translation: Desire to all, always is seed  From which ceaseless births proceed
kural.explanation: (The wise) say that the seed, which produces unceasing births, at all times, to all creatures, is desire
kural.couplet: The wise declare, through all the days, to every living thingThat ceaseless round of birth from seed of strong desire doth spring

kural.Translation: If long thou must, long for non-birth  It comes by longing no more for earth
kural.explanation: If anything be desired, freedom from births should be desired; that (freedom from births) will be attained by desiring to be without desire
kural.couplet: If desire you feel, freedom from changing birth require!'I' will come, if you desire to 'scape, set free from all desire

kural.Translation: No such wealth is here and there  As peerless wealth of non-desire
kural.explanation: There is in this world no excellence equal to freedom from desire; and even in that world, there is nothing like it
kural.couplet: No glorious wealth is here like freedom from desire;To bliss like this not even there can soul aspire

kural.Translation: To nothing crave is purity  That is the fruit of verity
kural.explanation: Purity (of mind) consists in freedom from desire; and that (freedom from desire) is the fruit of the love of truth
kural.couplet: Desire's decease as purity men know;That, too, from yearning search for truth will grow

kural.Translation: The free are those who desire not  The rest not free in bonds are caught
kural.explanation: They are said to be free (from future birth) who are freed from desire; all others (who, whatever else they may be free from, are not freed from desire) are not thus free
kural.couplet: Men freed from bonds of strong desire are free;None other share such perfect liberty

kural.Translation: Dread desire; Virtue is there  To every soul desire is snare!
kural.explanation: It is the chief duty of (an ascetic) to watch against desire with (jealous) fear; for it has power to deceive (and destroy) him
kural.couplet: Desire each soul beguiles;True virtue dreads its wiles

kural.Translation: Destroy desire; deliverance  Comes as much as you aspire hence
kural.explanation: If a man thoroughly cut off all desire, the deeds, which confer immortality, will come to him, in the path in which he seeks them
kural.couplet: Who thoroughly rids his life of passion-prompted deed,Deeds of unfailing worth shall do, which, as he plans, succeed

kural.Translation: Desire extinct no sorrow-taints  Grief comes on grief where it pretends
kural.explanation: There is no sorrow to those who are without desire; but where that is, (sorrow) will incessantly come, more and more
kural.couplet: Affliction is not known where no desires abide;Where these are, endless rises sorrow's tide

kural.Translation: Desire, the woe of woes destroy  Joy of joys here you enjoy
kural.explanation: Even while in this body, joy will never depart (from the mind, in which) desire, that sorrow of sorrows, has been destroyed
kural.couplet: When dies away desire, that woe of woesEv'n here the soul unceasing rapture knows

kural.Translation: Off with desire insatiate  You gain the native blissful state
kural.explanation: The removal of desire, whose nature it is never to be satisfied, will immediately confer a nature that can never be changed
kural.couplet: Drive from thy soul desire insatiate;Straight'way is gained the moveless blissful state

kural.Translation: Efforts succeed by waxing star  Wealth-losing brings waning star
kural.explanation: Perseverance comes from a prosperous fate, and idleness from an adverse fate
kural.couplet: Wealth-giving fate power of unflinching effort brings;From fate that takes away idle remissness springs

kural.Translation: Loss-fate makes a dull fool of us  Gain-fate makes us prosperous, wise!
kural.explanation: An adverse fate produces folly, and a prosperous fate produces enlarged knowledge
kural.couplet: The fate that loss ordains makes wise men's wisdom foolishness;The fate that gain bestows with ampler powers will wisdom bless

kural.Translation: What matters subtle study deep?  Levels of innate wisdom-keep
kural.explanation: Although (a man) may study the most polished treatises, the knowledge which fate has decreed to him will still prevail
kural.couplet: In subtle learning manifold though versed man be,'The wisdom, truly his, will gain supremacy

kural.Translation: Two natures in the world obtain  Some wealth and others wisdom gain
kural.explanation: There are (through fate) two different natures in the world, hence the difference (observable in men) in (their acquisition of) wealth, and in their attainment of knowledge
kural.couplet: Two fold the fashion of the world: some live in fortune's light;While other some have souls in wisdom's radiance bright

kural.Translation: In making wealth fate changes mood;  The good as bad and bad as good
kural.explanation: In the acquisition of property, every thing favourable becomes unfavourable, and (on the other hand) everything unfavourable becomes favourable, (through the power of fate)
kural.couplet: All things that good appear will oft have ill success;All evil things prove good for gain of happiness

kural.Translation: Things not thine never remain  Things destined are surely thine
kural.explanation: Whatever is not conferred by fate cannot be preserved although it be guarded with most painful care; and that, which fate has made his, cannot be lost, although one should even take it and throw it away
kural.couplet: Things not your own will yield no good, howe'er you guard with pain;Your own, howe'er you scatter them abroad, will yours remain

kural.Translation: Who crores amass enjoy but what  The Dispenser's decrees allot
kural.explanation: Even those who gather together millions will only enjoy them, as it has been determined by the disposer (of all things)
kural.couplet: Save as the 'sharer' shares to each in due degree,To those who millions store enjoyment scarce can be

kural.Translation: The destitute desire will quit  If fate with ills visit them not
kural.explanation: The destitute will renounce desire (and become ascetics), if (fate) do not make them suffer the hindrances to which they are liable, and they pass away
kural.couplet: The destitute with ascetics merit share,If fate to visit with predestined ills would spare

kural.Translation: Who good in time of good perceive  In evil time why should they grieve?
kural.explanation: How is it that those, who are pleased with good fortune, trouble themselves when evil comes, (since both are equally the decree of fate) ?
kural.couplet: When good things come, men view them all as gain;When evils come, why then should they complain

kural.Translation: What power surpasses fate? Its will  Persists against the human skill
kural.explanation: What is stronger than fate ? If we think of an expedient (to avert it), it will itself be with us before (the thought)
kural.couplet: What powers so great as those of Destiny? Man's skillSome other thing contrives; but fate's beforehand still

kural.Translation: People, troops, wealth, forts, council, friends  Who owns these six is lion of kings
kural.explanation: He who possesses these six things, an army, a people, wealth, ministers, friends and a fortress, is a lion among kings
kural.couplet: An army, people, wealth, a minister, friends, fort: six things-Who owns them all, a lion lives amid the kings

kural.Translation: Courage, giving, knowledge and zeal  Are four failless features royal
kural.explanation: Never to fail in these four things, fearlessness, liberality, wisdom, and energy, is the kingly character
kural.couplet: Courage, a liberal hand, wisdom, and energy: these fourAre qualities a king adorn for evermore

kural.Translation: Alertness, learning bravery  Are adjuncts three of monarchy
kural.explanation: These three things, viz, vigilance, learning, and bravery, should never be wanting in the ruler of a country
kural.couplet: A sleepless promptitude, knowledge, decision strong:These three for aye to rulers of the land belong

kural.Translation: A brave noble king refrains from vice  Full of virtue and enterprise
kural.explanation: He is a king who, with manly modesty, swerves not from virtue, and refrains from vice
kural.couplet: Kingship, in virtue failing not, all vice restrains,In courage failing not, it honour's grace maintains

kural.Translation: The able king gets, stores and guards  And spends them for people's safeguards
kural.explanation: He is a king who is able to acquire (wealth), to lay it up, to guard, and to distribute it
kural.couplet: A king is he who treasure gains, stores up, defends,And duly for his kingdom's weal expends

kural.Translation: That land prospers where the king is  Easy to see, not harsh of words
kural.explanation: The whole world will exalt the country of the king who is easy of access, and who is free from harsh language
kural.couplet: Where king is easy of access, where no harsh word repels,That land's high praises every subject swells

kural.Translation: The world commends and acts his phrase  Who sweetly speaks and gives with grace
kural.explanation: The world will praise and submit itself to the mind of the king who is able to give with affability, and to protect all who come to him
kural.couplet: With pleasant speech, who gives and guards with powerful liberal hand,He sees the world obedient all to his command

kural.Translation: He is the Lord of men who does  Sound justice and saves his race
kural.explanation: That king, will be esteemed a God among men, who performs his own duties, and protects (his subjects).
kural.couplet: Who guards the realm and justice strict maintains,That king as god o'er subject people reigns

kural.Translation: Under his shelter thrives the world  Who bears remarks bitter and bold
kural.explanation: The whole world will dwell under the umbrella of the king, who can bear words that embitter the ear
kural.couplet: The king of worth, who can words bitter to his ear endure,Beneath the shadow of his power the world abides secure

kural.Translation: He is the Light of Kings who has  Bounty, justice, care and grace
kural.explanation: He is the light of kings who has there four things, beneficence, benevolence, rectitude, and care for his people
kural.couplet: Gifts, grace, right sceptre, care of people's weal;These four a light of dreaded kings reveal

kural.Translation: Lore worth learning, learn flawlessly  Live by that learning thoroughly
kural.explanation: Let a man learn thoroughly whatever he may learn, and let his conduct be worthy of his learning
kural.couplet: So learn that you may full and faultless learning gain,Then in obedience meet to lessons learnt remain

kural.Translation: Letter, number, art and science  Of living kind both are the eyes
kural.explanation: Letters and numbers are the two eyes of man
kural.couplet: The twain that lore of numbers and of letters giveAre eyes, the wise declare, to all on earth that live

kural.Translation: The learned alone have eyes on face  The ignorant two sores of disgrace
kural.explanation: The learned are said to have eyes, but the unlearned have (merely) two sores in their face
kural.couplet: Men who learning gain have eyes, men say;Blockheads' faces pairs of sores display

kural.Translation: To meet with joy and part with thought  Of learned men this is the art
kural.explanation: It is the part of the learned to give joy to those whom they meet, and on leaving, to make them think (Oh! when shall we meet them again.)
kural.couplet: You meet with joy, with pleasant thought you part;Such is the learned scholar's wonderous art

kural.Translation: Like poor before rich they yearn:  For knowledge: the low never learn
kural.explanation: The unlearned are inferior to the learned, before whom they stand begging, as the destitute before the wealthy
kural.couplet: With soul submiss they stand, as paupers front a rich man's face;Yet learned men are first; th'unlearned stand in lowest place

kural.Translation: As deep you dig the sand spring flows  As deep you learn the knowledge grows
kural.explanation: Water will flow from a well in the sand in proportion to the depth to which it is dug, and knowledge will flow from a man in proportion to his learning
kural.couplet: In sandy soil, when deep you delve, you reach the springs below;The more you learn, the freer streams of wisdom flow

kural.Translation: All lands and towns are learner's own  Why not till death learning go on!
kural.explanation: How is it that any one can remain without learning, even to his death, when (to the learned man) every country is his own (country), and every town his own (town) ?
kural.couplet: The learned make each land their own, in every city find a home;Who, till they die; learn nought, along what weary ways they roam

kural.Translation: The joy of learning in one birth  Exalts man upto his seventh
kural.explanation: The learning, which a man has acquired in one birth, will yield him pleasure during seven births
kural.couplet: The man who store of learning gains,In one, through seven worlds, bliss attains

kural.Translation: The learned foster learning more  On seeing the world enjoy their lore
kural.explanation: The learned will long (for more learning), when they see that while it gives pleasure to themselves, the world also derives pleasure from it
kural.couplet: Their joy is joy of all the world, they see; thus moreThe learners learn to love their cherished lore

kural.Translation: Learning is wealth none could destroy  Nothing else gives genuine joy
kural.explanation: Learning is the true imperishable riches; all other things are not riches
kural.couplet: Learning is excellence of wealth that none destroy;To man nought else affords reality of joy

kural.Translation: Like play of chess on squareless board  Vain is imperfect loreless word
kural.explanation: To speak in an assembly (of the learned) without fullness of knowledge, is like playing at chess (on a board) without squares
kural.couplet: Like those at draughts would play without the chequered square,Men void of ample lore would counsels of the learned share

kural.Translation: Unlearned man aspiring speech  Is breastless lady's love-approach
kural.explanation: The desire of the unlearned to speak (in an assembly), is like a woman without breasts desiring (the enjoyment of ) woman-hood
kural.couplet: Like those who doat on hoyden's undeveloped charms are they,Of learning void, who eagerly their power of words display

kural.Translation: Ev'n unread men are good and wise  If before the wise, they hold their peace
kural.explanation: The unlearned also are very excellent men, if they know how to keep silence before the learned
kural.couplet: The blockheads, too, may men of worth appear,If they can keep from speaking where the learned hear

kural.Translation: The unread's wit though excellent  Is not valued by the savant
kural.explanation: Although the natural knowledge of an unlearned man may be very good, the wise will not accept for true knowledge
kural.couplet: From blockheads' lips, when words of wisdom glibly flow,The wise receive them not, though good they seem to show

kural.Translation: A man untaught when speech he vaunts  Sadly fails before savants
kural.explanation: The self-conceit of an unlearned man will fade away, as soon as he speaks in an assembly (of
kural.couplet: As worthless shows the worth of man unlearned,When council meets, by words he speaks discerned

kural.Translation: People speak of untaught minds  \"They just exist like barren lands\"
kural.explanation: The unlearned are like worthless barren land: all that can be said of them is, that they exist
kural.couplet: 'They are': so much is true of men untaught;But, like a barren field, they yield us nought

kural.Translation: Like painted clay-doll is his show  Grand subtle lore who fails to know
kural.explanation: The beauty and goodness of one who is destitute of knowledge by the study of great and exquisite works, is like (the beauty and goodness) of a painted earthen doll
kural.couplet: Who lack the power of subtle, large, and penetrating sense,Like puppet, decked with ornaments of clay, their beauty's vain pretence

kural.Translation: Wealth in the hand of fools is worse  Than a learned man's empty purse
kural.explanation: Wealth, gained by the unlearned, will give more sorrow than the poverty which may come upon the learned
kural.couplet: To men unlearned, from fortune's favour greater-evil springsThan poverty to men of goodly wisdom brings

kural.Translation: Lower are fools of higher birth  Than low-born men of learning's worth
kural.explanation: The unlearned, though born in a high caste, are not equal in dignity to the learned; though they may have been born in a low caste
kural.couplet: Lower are men unlearned, though noble be their race,Than low-born men adorned with learning's grace

kural.Translation: Like beasts before men, dunces are  Before scholars of shining lore
kural.explanation: As beasts by the side of men, so are other men by the side of those who are learned in celebrated works
kural.couplet: Learning's irradiating grace who gain,Others excel, as men the bestial train

kural.Translation: Wealth of wealths is listening's wealth  It is the best of wealths on earth
kural.explanation: Wealth (gained) by the ear is wealth of wealth; that wealth is the chief of all wealth
kural.couplet: Wealth of wealth is wealth acquired be ear attent;Wealth mid all wealth supremely excellent

kural.Translation: Some food for the stomach is brought  When the ear gets no food for thought
kural.explanation: When there is no food for the ear, give a little also to the stomach
kural.couplet: When 'tis no longer time the listening ear to feedWith trifling dole of food supply the body's need

kural.Translation: Whose ears get lots of wisdom-food  Equal gods on oblations fed
kural.explanation: Those who in this world enjoy instruction which is the food of the ear, are equal to the Gods, who enjoy the food of the sacrifices
kural.couplet: Who feed their ear with learned teachings rare,Are like the happy gods oblations rich who share

kural.Translation: Though not learned, hear and heed  That serves a staff and stay in need
kural.explanation: Although a man be without learning, let him listen (to the teaching of the learned); that will be to him a staff in adversity
kural.couplet: Though learning none hath he, yet let him hear alway:In weakness this shall prove a staff and stay

kural.Translation: Virtuous men's wisdom is found  A strong staff on slippery ground
kural.explanation: The words of the good are like a staff in a slippery place
kural.couplet: Like staff in hand of him in slippery ground who straysAre words from mouth of those who walk in righteous ways

kural.Translation: Lend ear to good words however few  That much will highly exalt you
kural.explanation: Let a man listen, never so little, to good (instruction), even that will bring him great dignity
kural.couplet: Let each man good things learn, for e'en as heShall learn, he gains increase of perfect dignity

kural.Translation: Who listen well and learn sharply  Not ev'n by slip speak foolishly
kural.explanation: Not even when they have imperfectly understood (a matter), will those men speak foolishly, who have profoundly studied and diligently listened (to instruction)
kural.couplet: Not e'en through inadvertence speak they foolish word,With clear discerning mind who've learning's ample lessons heard

kural.Translation: That ear though hearing is dulled  Which is not by wisdom drilled
kural.explanation: The ear which has not been bored by instruction, although it hears, is deaf
kural.couplet: Where teaching hath not oped the learner's ear,The man may listen, but he scarce can hear

kural.Translation: A modest mouth is hard for those  Who care little to counsels wise
kural.explanation: It is a rare thing to find modesty, a reverend mouth- with those who have not received choice instruction
kural.couplet: 'Tis hard for mouth to utter gentle, modest word,When ears discourse of lore refined have never heard

kural.Translation: Who taste by mouth and not by ear  What if they fare ill or well here?
kural.explanation: What does it matter whether those men live or die, who can judge of tastes by the mouth, and not by the ear ?
kural.couplet: His mouth can taste, but ear no taste of joy can give!What matter if he die, or prosperous live

kural.Translation: Wisdom's weapon wards off all woes  It is a fort defying foes
kural.explanation: Wisdom is a weapon to ward off destruction; it is an inner fortress which enemies cannot destroy
kural.couplet: True wisdom wards off woes, A circling fortress high;Its inner strength man's eager foes Unshaken will defy

kural.Translation: Wisdom checks the straying senses  Expels evils, impels goodness
kural.explanation: Not to permit the mind to go where it lists, to keep it from evil, and to employ it in good, this is wisdom
kural.couplet: Wisdom restrains, nor suffers mind to wander where it would;From every evil calls it back, and guides in way of good

kural.Translation: To grasp the Truth from everywhere  From everyone is wisdom fair
kural.explanation: To discern the truth in every thing, by whomsoever spoken, is wisdom
kural.couplet: Though things diverse from divers sages' lips we learn,'Tis wisdom's part in each the true thing to discern

kural.Translation: Speaking out thoughts in clear trends  Wisdom subtle sense comprehends
kural.explanation: To speak so as that the meaning may easily enter the mind of the hearer, and to discern the subtlest thought which may lie hidden in the words of others, this is wisdom
kural.couplet: Wisdom hath use of lucid speech, words that acceptance win,And subtle sense of other men's discourse takes in

kural.Translation: The wise-world the wise befriend  They bloom nor gloom, equal in mind
kural.explanation: To secure the friendship of the great is true wisdom; it is (also) wisdom to keep (that friendship unchanged, and) not opening and closing (like the lotus flower)
kural.couplet: Wisdom embraces frank the world, to no caprice exposed;Unlike the lotus flower, now opened wide, now petals strictly closed

kural.Translation: As moves the world so move the wise  In tune with changing times and ways
kural.explanation: To live as the world lives, is wisdom
kural.couplet: As dwells the world, so with the world to dwellIn harmony- this is to wisely live and well

kural.Translation: The wise foresee what is to come  The unwise lack in that wisdom
kural.explanation: The wise are those who know beforehand what will happen; those who do not know this are the unwise
kural.couplet: The wise discern, the foolish fail to see,And minds prepare for things about to be

kural.Translation: Fear the frightful and act wisely  Not to fear the frightful's folly
kural.explanation: Not to fear what ought to be feared, is folly; it is the work of the wise to fear what should be feared
kural.couplet: Folly meets fearful ills with fearless heart;To fear where cause of fear exists is wisdom's part

kural.Translation: No frightful evil shocks the wise  Who guard themselves against surprise
kural.explanation: No terrifying calamity will happen to the wise, who (foresee) and guard against coming evils
kural.couplet: The wise with watchful soul who coming ills foresee;From coming evil's dreaded shock are free

kural.Translation: Who have wisdom they are all full  Whatev'r they own, misfits are nil
kural.explanation: Those who possess wisdom, possess every thing; those who have not wisdom, whatever they may possess, have nothing
kural.couplet: The wise is rich, with ev'ry blessing blest;The fool is poor, of everything possessed

kural.Translation: Plenty is their prosperity  Who're free from wrath pride lust petty
kural.explanation: Truly great is the excellence of those (kings) who are free from pride, anger, and lust
kural.couplet: Who arrogance, and wrath, and littleness of low desire restrain,To sure increase of lofty dignity attain

kural.Translation: Mean pride, low pleasure, avarice  These add blemishes to a prince
kural.explanation: Avarice, undignified pride, and low pleasures are faults in a king
kural.couplet: A niggard hand, o'erweening self-regard, and mirthUnseemly, bring disgrace to men of kingly brith

kural.Translation: Though millet-small their faults might seem  Men fearing disgrace, Palm-tall deem
kural.explanation: Those who fear guilt, if they commit a fault small as a millet seed, will consider it to be as large as a palmyra tree
kural.couplet: Though small as millet-seed the fault men deem;As palm tree vast to those who fear disgrace 'twill seem

kural.Translation: Watch like treasure freedom from fault  Our fatal foe is that default
kural.explanation: Guard against faults as a matter (of great consequence; for) faults are a deadly enemy
kural.couplet: Freedom from faults is wealth; watch heedfully'Gainst these, for fault is fatal enmity

kural.Translation: Who fails to guard himself from flaw  Loses his life like flame-lit straw
kural.explanation: The prosperity of him who does not timely guard against faults, will perish like straw before fire
kural.couplet: His joy who guards not 'gainst the coming evil day,Like straw before the fire shall swift consume away

kural.Translation: What fault can be the king's who cures  First his faults, then scans others
kural.explanation: What fault will remain in the king who has put away his own evils, and looks after the evils of others
kural.couplet: Faultless the king who first his own faults cures, and thenPermits himself to scan faults of other men

kural.Translation: That miser's wealth shall waste and end  Who would not for a good cause spend
kural.explanation: The wealth of the avaricious man, who does not expend it for the purposes for which he ought to expend it will waste away and not continue
kural.couplet: Who leaves undone what should be done, with niggard mind,His wealth shall perish, leaving not a wrack behind

kural.Translation: The gripping greed of miser's heart  Is more than fault the worst apart
kural.explanation: Griping avarice is not to be reckoned as one among other faults; (it stands alone - greater than all)
kural.couplet: The greed of soul that avarice men call,When faults are summed, is worst of all

kural.Translation: Never boast yourself in any mood  Nor do a deed that does no good
kural.explanation: Let no (one) praise himself, at any time; let him not desire to do useless things
kural.couplet: Never indulge in self-complaisant mood,Nor deed desire that yields no gain of good

kural.Translation: All designs of the foes shall fail  If one his wishes guards in veil
kural.explanation: If (a king) enjoys, privately the things which he desires, the designs of his enemies will be useless
kural.couplet: If, to your foes unknown, you cherish what you love,Counsels of men who wish you harm will harmless prove

kural.Translation: Weigh their worth and friendship gain  Of men of virtue and mature brain
kural.explanation: Let (a king) ponder well its value, and secure the friendship of men of virtue and of mature knowledge
kural.couplet: As friends the men who virtue know, and riper wisdom share,Their worth weighed well, the king should choose with care

kural.Translation: Cherish the help of men of skill  Who ward and safe-guard you from ill
kural.explanation: Let (a king) procure and kindly care for men who can overcome difficulties when they occur, and guard against them before they happen
kural.couplet: Cherish the all-accomplished men as friends,Whose skill the present ill removes, from coming ill defends

kural.Translation: Honour and have the great your own  Is rarest of the rare things known
kural.explanation: To cherish great men and make them his own, is the most difficult of all difficult things
kural.couplet: To cherish men of mighty soul, and make them all their own,Of kingly treasures rare, as rarest gift is known

kural.Translation: To have betters as intimates  Power of all powers promotes
kural.explanation: So to act as to make those men, his own, who are greater than himself is of all powers the highest
kural.couplet: To live with men of greatness that their own excels,As cherished friends, is greatest power that with a monarch dwells

kural.Translation: Ministers are the monarch's eyes  Round him should be the right and wise
kural.explanation: As a king must use his ministers as eyes (in managing his kingdom), let him well examine their character and qualifications before he engages them
kural.couplet: The king, since counsellors are monarch's eyes,Should counsellors select with counsel wise

kural.Translation: To move with worthy friends who knows  Has none to fear from frightful foes
kural.explanation: There will be nothing left for enemies to do, against him who has the power of acting (so as to secure) the fellowship of worthy men
kural.couplet: The king, who knows to live with worthy men allied,Has nought to fear from any foeman's pride

kural.Translation: No foe can foil his powers  whose friends reprove him when he errs
kural.explanation: Who are great enough to destroy him who has servants that have power to rebuke him ?
kural.couplet: What power can work his fall, who faithful ministersEmploys, that thunder out reproaches when he errs

kural.Translation: The careless king whom none reproves  Ruins himself sans harmful foes
kural.explanation: The king, who is without the guard of men who can rebuke him, will perish, even though there be no one to destroy him
kural.couplet: The king with none to censure him, bereft of safeguards all,Though none his ruin work, shall surely ruined fall

kural.Translation: No capital, no gain in trade  No prop secure sans good comrade
kural.explanation: There can be no gain to those who have no capital; and in like manner there can be no permanence to
kural.couplet: Who owns no principal, can have no gain of usury;Who lacks support of friends, knows no stability

kural.Translation: To give up good friends is ten times worse  Than being hated by countless foes
kural.explanation: It is tenfold more injurious to abandon the friendship of the good, than to incur the hatred of the many
kural.couplet: Than hate of many foes incurred, works greater woeTen-fold, of worthy men the friendship to forego

kural.Translation: The ignoble the noble fear  The mean hold them as kinsmen dear
kural.explanation: (True) greatness fears the society of the base; it is only the low - minded who will regard them as friends
kural.couplet: The great of soul will mean association fear;The mean of soul regard mean men as kinsmen dear

kural.Translation: With soil changes water's taste  With mates changes the mental state
kural.explanation: As water changes (its nature), from the nature of the soil (in which it flows), so will the character of men resemble that of their associates
kural.couplet: The waters' virtues change with soil through which they flow;As man's companionship so will his wisdom show

kural.Translation: Wisdom depends upon the mind  The worth of man upon his friend
kural.explanation: The power of knowing is from the mind; (but) his character is from that of his associates
kural.couplet: Perceptions manifold in men are of the mind alone;The value of the man by his companionship is known

kural.Translation: Wisdom seems to come from mind  But it truly flows from the kind
kural.explanation: Wisdom appears to rest in the mind, but it really exists to a man in his companions
kural.couplet: Man's wisdom seems the offspring of his mind;'Tis outcome of companionship we find

kural.Translation: Purity of the thought and deed  Comes from good company indeed
kural.explanation: Chaste company is the staff on which come, these two things, viz, purity of mind and purity of conduct
kural.couplet: Both purity of mind, and purity of action clear,Leaning no staff of pure companionship, to man draw near

kural.Translation: Pure-hearted get good progeny  Pure friendship acts with victory
kural.explanation: To the pure-minded there will be a good posterity By those whose associates are pure, no deeds will be done that are not good
kural.couplet: From true pure-minded men a virtuous race proceeds;To men of pure companionship belong no evil deeds

kural.Translation: Goodness of mind increases gain  Good friendship fosters fame again
kural.explanation: Goodness of mind will give wealth, and good society will bring with it all praise, to men
kural.couplet: Goodness of mind to lives of men increaseth gain;And good companionship doth all of praise obtain

kural.Translation: Men of wisdom, though good in mind  In friends of worth a new strength find
kural.explanation: Yet good companionship is confirmation strong
kural.couplet: To perfect men, though minds right good belong,Yet good companionship is confirmation strong

kural.Translation: Good mind decides the future bliss  Good company gains strength to this
kural.explanation: Future bliss is (the result) of goodness of mind; and even this acquires strength from the society of the good
kural.couplet: Although to mental goodness joys of other life belong,Yet good companionship is confirmation strong

kural.Translation: No help good company exeeds;  The bad to untold anguish leads
kural.explanation: There is no greater help than the company of the good; there is no greater source of sorrow than the company of the wicked
kural.couplet: Than good companionship no surer help we know;Than bad companionship nought causes direr woe

kural.Translation: Weigh well output the loss and gain  And proper action ascertain
kural.explanation: Let a man reflect on what will be lost, what will be acquired and (from these) what will be his ultimate gain, and (then, let him) act
kural.couplet: Expenditure, return, and profit of the deedIn time to come; weigh these- than to the act proceed

kural.Translation: Nothing is hard for him who acts  With worthy counsels weighing facts
kural.explanation: There is nothing too difficult to (be attained by) those who, before they act, reflect well themselves, and thoroughly consider (the matter) with chosen friends
kural.couplet: With chosen friends deliberate; next use the private thought;Then act By those who thus proceed all works with ease are wrought

kural.Translation: The wise risk not their capital  In doubtful gains and lose their all
kural.explanation: Wise men will not, in the hopes of profit, undertake works that will consume their principal
kural.couplet: To risk one's all and lose, aiming at added gain,Is rash affair, from which the wise abstain

kural.Translation: They who scornful reproach fear  Commence no work not made clear
kural.explanation: Those who fear reproach will not commence anything which has not been (thoroughly considered) and made clear to them
kural.couplet: A work of which the issue is not clear,Begin not they reproachful scorn who fear

kural.Translation: Who marches without plans and ways  His field is sure to foster foes
kural.explanation: One way to promote the prosperity of an enemy, is (for a king) to set out (to war) without having thoroughly weighed his ability (to cope with its chances)
kural.couplet: With plans not well matured to rise against your foe,Is way to plant him out where he is sure to grow

kural.Translation: Doing unfit action ruins Failing fit-act also ruins
kural.explanation: He will perish who does not what is not fit to do; and he also will perish who does not do what it is fit to
kural.couplet: 'Tis ruin if man do an unbefitting thing;Fit things to leave undone will equal ruin bring

kural.Translation: Think and dare a proper deed  Dare and think is bad in need
kural.explanation: Consider, and then undertake a matter; after having undertaken it, to say "We will consider," is folly
kural.couplet: Think, and then dare the deed! Who cry,'Deed dared, we'll think,' disgraced shall be

kural.Translation: Toil without a plan ahead Is doomed to fall though supported
kural.explanation: The work, which is not done by suitable methods, will fail though many stand to uphold it
kural.couplet: On no right system if man toil and strive,Though many men assist, no work can thrive

kural.Translation: Attune the deeds to habitude Or ev'n good leads to evil feud
kural.explanation: There are failures even in acting well, when it is done without knowing the various dispositions of men
kural.couplet: Though well the work be done, yet one mistake is made,To habitudes of various men when no regard is paid

kural.Translation: Do deeds above reproachfulness The world refutes uncomely mess
