kural.explanation: Let a man reflect, and do things which bring no reproach; the world will not approve, with him, of things which do not become of his position to adopt
kural.couplet: Plan and perform no work that others may despise;What misbeseems a king the world will not approve as wise

kural.Translation: Judge act and might and foeman's strength The allies' strength and go at length
kural.explanation: Let (one) weigh well the strength of the deed (he purposes to do), his own strength, the strength of his enemy, and the strength of the allies (of both), and then let him act
kural.couplet: The force the strife demands, the force he owns, the force of foes,The force of friends; these should he weigh ere to the war he goes

kural.Translation: Nothing hampers the firm who know What they can and how to go
kural.explanation: There is nothing which may not be accomplished by those who, before they attack (an enemy), make themselves acquainted with their own ability, and with whatever else is (needful) to be known, and
kural.couplet: Who know what can be wrought, with knowledge of the means, on this,Their mind firm set, go forth, nought goes with them amiss

kural.Translation: Many know not their meagre might Their pride breaks up in boastful fight
kural.explanation: There are many who, ignorant of their (want of) power (to meet it), have haughtily set out to war, and broken down in the midst of it
kural.couplet: Ill-deeming of their proper powers, have many monarchs striven,And midmost of unequal conflict fallen asunder riven

kural.Translation: Who adapts not, outsteps measure And brags himself-his fall is sure
kural.explanation: He will quickly perish who, ignorant of his own resources flatters himself of his greatness, and does
kural.couplet: Who not agrees with those around, no moderation knows,In self-applause indulging, swift to ruin goes

kural.Translation: Even the gentle peacock's plume Cart's axle breaks by gross volume
kural.explanation: The axle tree of a bandy, loaded only with peacocks' feathers will break, if it be greatly overloaded
kural.couplet: With peacock feathers light, you load the wain;Yet, heaped too high, the axle snaps in twain

kural.Translation: Beyond the branches' tip who skips Ends the life as his body rips
kural.explanation: There will be an end to the life of him who, having climbed out to the end of a branch, ventures to go further
kural.couplet: Who daring climbs, and would himself upraiseBeyond the branch's tip, with life the forfeit pays

kural.Translation: Know the limit; grant with measure This way give and guard your treasure
kural.explanation: Let a man know the measure of his ability (to give), and let him give accordingly; such giving is the way to preserve his property
kural.couplet: With knowledge of the measure due, as virtue bids you give!That is the way to guard your wealth, and seemly live

kural.Translation: The outflow must not be excess No matter how small income is
kural.explanation: Even though the income (of a king) be small, it will not cause his (ruin), if his outgoings be not larger than his income
kural.couplet: Incomings may be scant; but yet, no failure there,If in expenditure you rightly learn to spare

kural.Translation: Who does not know to live in bounds His life seems rich but thins and ends
kural.explanation: The prosperity of him who lives without knowing the measure (of his property), will perish, even while it seems to continue
kural.couplet: Who prosperous lives and of enjoyment knows no bound,His seeming wealth, departing, nowhere shall be found

kural.Translation: Wealth amassed quickly vanishes Sans level if one lavishes
kural.explanation: The measure of his wealth will quickly perish, whose liberality weighs not the measure of his property
kural.couplet: Beneficence that measures not its bound of means,Will swiftly bring to nought the wealth on which it leans

kural.Translation: By day the crow defeats the owl Kings need right time their foes to quell
kural.explanation: A crow will overcome an owl in the day time; so the king who would conquer his enemy must have (a suitable) time
kural.couplet: A crow will conquer owl in broad daylight;The king that foes would crush, needs fitting time to fight

kural.Translation: Well-ordered seasoned act is cord That fortune binds in bon accord
kural.explanation: Acting at the right season, is a cord that will immoveably bind success (to a king)
kural.couplet: The bond binds fortune fast is ordered effort made,Strictly observant still of favouring season's aid

kural.Translation: What is hard for him who acts With proper means and time and tacts?
kural.explanation: Is there anything difficult for him to do, who acts, with (the right) instruments at the right time ?
kural.couplet: Can any work be hard in very fact,If men use fitting means in timely act

kural.Translation: Choose proper time and act and place Even the world you win with ease
kural.explanation: Though (a man) should meditate (the conquest of) the world, he may accomplish it if he acts in the right time, and at the right place
kural.couplet: The pendant world's dominion may be won,In fitting time and place by action done

kural.Translation: Who want to win the world sublime Wait unruffled biding their time
kural.explanation: They who thoughtfully consider and wait for the (right) time (for action), may successfully meditate (the conquest of) the world
kural.couplet: Who think the pendant world itself to subjugate,With mind unruffled for the fitting time must wait

kural.Translation: By self-restraint stalwarts keep fit Like rams retreating but to butt
kural.explanation: The self-restraint of the energetic (while waiting for a suitable opportunity), is like the drawing back of a fighting-ram in order to butt
kural.couplet: The men of mighty power their hidden energies repress,As fighting ram recoils to rush on foe with heavier stress

kural.Translation: The wise jut not their vital fire They watch their time with hidden ire
kural.explanation: The wise will not immediately and hastily shew out their anger; they will watch their time, and restrain it within
kural.couplet: The glorious once of wrath enkindled make no outward show,At once; they bide their time, while hidden fires within them glow

kural.Translation: Bear with hostiles when you meet them Fell down their head in fateful time
kural.explanation: If one meets his enemy, let him show him all respect, until the time for his destruction is come; when that is come, his head will be easily brought low
kural.couplet: If foes' detested form they see, with patience let them bear;When fateful hour at last they spy,- the head lies there

kural.Translation: When comes the season ripe and rare Dare and do hard things then and there
kural.explanation: If a rare opportunity occurs, while it lasts, let a man do that which is rarely to be accomplished (but for such an opportunity)
kural.couplet: When hardest gain of opportunity at last is won,With promptitude let hardest deed be done

kural.Translation: In waiting time feign peace like stork In fighting time strike like its peck
kural.explanation: At the time when one should use self-control, let him restrain himself like a heron; and, let him like it, strike, when there is a favourable opportunity
kural.couplet: As heron stands with folded wing, so wait in waiting hour;As heron snaps its prey, when fortune smiles, put forth your power

kural.Translation: No action take, no foe despise Until you have surveyed the place
kural.explanation: Let not (a king) despise (an enemy), nor undertake any thing (against him), until he has obtained (a suitable) place for besieging him
kural.couplet: Begin no work of war, depise no foe,Till place where you can wholly circumvent you know

kural.Translation: Many are gains of fortresses Ev'n to kings of power and prowess
kural.explanation: Even to those who are men of power and expedients, an attack in connection with a fortification will yield many advantages
kural.couplet: Though skill in war combine with courage tried on battle-field,The added gain of fort doth great advantage yield

kural.Translation: Weaklings too withstand foe's offence In proper fields of strong defence
kural.explanation: Even the powerless will become powerful and conquer, if they select a proper field (of action), and guard themselves, while they make war on their enemies
kural.couplet: E'en weak ones mightily prevail, if place of strong defence,They find, protect themselves, and work their foes offence

kural.Translation: If fighters fight in vantage field The plans of foes shall be baffled
kural.explanation: If they who draw near (to fight) choose a suitable place to approach (their enemy), the latter, will have to relinquish the thought which they once entertained, of conquering them
kural.couplet: The foes who thought to triumph, find their thoughts were vain,If hosts advance, seize vantage ground, and thence the fight maintain

kural.Translation: In water crocodile prevails In land before others it fails
kural.explanation: In deep water, a crocodile will conquer (all other animals); but if it leave the water, other animals will conquer it
kural.couplet: The crocodile prevails in its own flow of water wide,If this it leaves, 'tis slain by anything beside

kural.Translation: Sea-going ship goes not on shore Nor on sea the strong-wheeled car
kural.explanation: Wide chariots, with mighty wheels, will not run on the ocean; neither will ships that the traverse ocean, move on the earth
kural.couplet: The lofty car, with mighty wheel, sails not o'er watery main,The boat that skims the sea, runs not on earth's hard plain

kural.Translation: No aid but daring dash they need When field is chosen right for deed
kural.explanation: You will need no other aid than fearlessness, if you thoroughly reflect (on what you are to do), and select (a suitable) place for your operations
kural.couplet: Save their own fearless might they need no other aid,If in right place they fight, all due provision made

kural.Translation: Though force is small, if place is right One quells a foe of well-armed might
kural.explanation: The power of one who has a large army will perish, if he goes into ground where only a small army can act
kural.couplet: If lord of army vast the safe retreat assailOf him whose host is small, his mightiest efforts fail

kural.Translation: To face a foe at home is vain Though fort and status are not fine
kural.explanation: It is a hazardous thing to attack men in their own country, although they may neither have power nor a good fortress
kural.couplet: Though fort be none, and store of wealth they lack,'Tis hard a people's homesteads to attack

kural.Translation: A fox can kill a war tusker Fearless with feet in deep quagmire
kural.explanation: A fox can kill a fearless, warrior-faced elephant, if it go into mud in which its legs sink down
kural.couplet: The jackal slays, in miry paths of foot-betraying fen,The elephant of fearless eye and tusks transfixing armed men

kural.Translation: Pleasure, gold, fear of life Virtue- Test by these four and trust the true
kural.explanation: Let (a minister) be chosen, after he has been tried by means of these four things, viz,-his virtue, (love of) money, (love of) sexual pleasure, and tear of (losing) life
kural.couplet: How treats he virtue, wealth and pleasure? How, when life's at stake,Comports himself? This four-fold test of man will full assurance make

kural.Translation: Spotless name of noble birth Shamed of stain-that choice is worth
kural.explanation: (The king's) choice should (fall) on him, who is of good family, who is free from faults, and who has the modesty which fears the wounds (of sin)
kural.couplet: Of noble race, of faultless worth, of generous prideThat shrinks from shame or stain; in him may king confide

kural.Translation: Though deep scholars of stainless sense Rare is freedom from ignorance
kural.explanation: When even men, who have studied the most difficult works, and who are free from faults, are (carefully) examined, it is a rare thing to find them without ignorance
kural.couplet: Though deeply learned, unflecked by fault, 'tis rare to see,When closely scanned, a man from all unwisdom free

kural.Translation: Good and evil in man weigh well Judge him by virtues which prevail
kural.explanation: Let (a king) consider (a man's) good qualities, as well as his faults, and then judge (of his character) by that which prevails
kural.couplet: Weigh well the good of each, his failings closely scan,As these or those prevail, so estimate the man

kural.Translation: By the touchstone of deeds is seen If any one is great or mean
kural.explanation: A man's deeds are the touchstone of his greatness and littleness
kural.couplet: Of greatness and of meanness too,The deeds of each are touchstone true

kural.Translation: Choose not those men without kinsmen Without affine or shame of sin
kural.explanation: Let (a king) avoid choosing men who have no relations; such men have no attachment, and thereforehave no fear of crime
kural.couplet: Beware of trusting men who have no kith of kin;No bonds restrain such men, no shame deters from sin

kural.Translation: On favour leaning fools you choose; Folly in all its forms ensues
kural.explanation: Yields all his being up to folly's blind control
kural.couplet: By fond affection led who trusts in men of unwise soul,Yields all his being up to folly's blind control

kural.Translation: To trust an untried stranger brings Endless troubles on all our kins
kural.explanation: Sorrow that will not leave even his posterity will come upon him chooses a stranger whose character he has not known
kural.couplet: Who trusts an untried stranger, brings disgrace,Remediless, on all his race

kural.Translation: Trust not without testing and then Find proper work for trusted men
kural.explanation: Let (a king) choose no one without previous consideration; after he has made his choice, let him unhesitatingly select for each such duties as are appropriate
kural.couplet: Trust no man whom you have not fully tried,When tested, in his prudence proved confide

kural.Translation: Trust without test; The trusted doubt; Both entail troubles in and out
kural.explanation: To make choice of one who has not been examined, and to entertain doubts respecting one who has been chosen, will produce irremediable sorrow
kural.couplet: Trust where you have not tried, doubt of a friend to feel,Once trusted, wounds inflict that nought can heal

kural.Translation: Employ the wise who will discern The good and bad and do good turn
kural.explanation: He should be employed (by a king), whose nature leads him to choose the good, after having weighed both the evil and the good in any undertaking
kural.couplet: Who good and evil scanning, ever makes the good his joy;Such man of virtuous mood should king employ

kural.Translation: Let him act who resource swells; Fosters wealth and prevents ills
kural.explanation: Let him do (the king's) work who can enlarge the sources (of revenue), increase wealth and considerately prevent the accidents (which would destroy it)
kural.couplet: Who swells the revenues, spreads plenty o'er the land,Seeks out what hinders progress, his the workman's hand

kural.Translation: Trust him in whom these four you see: Love, wit, non-craving, clarity
kural.explanation: Let the choice (of a king) fall upon him who largely possesses these four things, love, knowledge, a clear mind and freedom from covetousness
kural.couplet: A loyal love with wisdom, clearness, mind from avarice free;Who hath these four good gifts should ever trusted be

kural.Translation: Though tried and found fit, yet we see Many differ before duty
kural.explanation: Even when (a king) has tried them in every possible way, there are many men who change, from the nature of the works (in which they may be employed)
kural.couplet: Even when tests of every kind are multiplied,Full many a man proves otherwise, by action tried

kural.Translation: Wise able men with power invest Not by fondness but by hard test
kural.explanation: (A king's) work can only be accomplished by a man of wisdom and patient endurance; it is not of a nature to be given to one from mere personal attachment
kural.couplet: No specious fav'rite should the king's commission bear,But he that knows, and work performs with patient care

kural.Translation: Discern the agent and the deed And just in proper time proceed
kural.explanation: Let (a king) act, after having considered the agent (whom he is to employ), the deed (he desires to do), and the time which is suitable to it
kural.couplet: Let king first ask, 'Who shall the deed perform?' and 'What the deed?'Of hour befitting both assured, let every work proceed

kural.Translation: This work, by this, this man can do Like this entrust the duty due
kural.explanation: After having considered, "this man can accomplish this, by these means", let (the king) leave with him the discharge of that duty
kural.couplet: 'This man, this work shall thus work out,' let thoughtful king command;Then leave the matter wholly in his servant's hand

kural.Translation: His fitness for the duty scan Leave him to do the best he can
kural.explanation: Having considered what work a man is fit for, let (the king) employ him in that work
kural.couplet: As each man's special aptitude is known,Bid each man make that special work his own

kural.Translation: Who do duty for duty's sake Doubt them; and fortune departs quick
kural.explanation: Prosperity will leave (the king) who doubts the friendship of the man who steadily labours in the discharge of his duties
kural.couplet: Fortune deserts the king who ill can bear,Informal friendly ways of men his tolls who share

kural.Translation: Worker straight the world is straight The king must look to this aright
kural.explanation: Let a king daily examine the conduct of his servants; if they do not act crookedly, the world will not act crookedly
kural.couplet: Let king search out his servants' deeds each day;When these do right, the world goes rightly on its way

kural.Translation: Let fortunes go; yet kinsmen know The old accustomed love to show
kural.explanation: Even when (a man's) property is all gone, relatives will act towards him with their accustomed (kindness)
kural.couplet: When wealth is fled, old kindness still to show,Is kindly grace that only kinsmen know

kural.Translation: The gift of loving Kins bestows  Fadeless fortune's fresh flowers
kural.explanation: If (a man's) relatives remain attached to him with unchanging love, it will be a source of everincreasing wealth
kural.couplet: The gift of kin's unfailing love bestowsMuch gain of good, like flower that fadeless blows

kural.Translation: A kinless wealth is like a tank Which overflows without a bank
kural.explanation: The wealth of one who does not mingle freely with his relatives, will be like the filling of water in a
kural.couplet: His joy of life who mingles not with kinsmen gathered round,Is lake where streams pour in, with no encircling bound

kural.Translation: The fruit of growing wealth is gained When kith and kin are happy found
kural.explanation: To live surrounded by relatives, is the advantage to be derived from the acquisition of wealth
kural.couplet: The profit gained by wealth's increase,Is living compassed round by relatives in peace

kural.Translation: Loving words and liberal hand Encircle kith and kin around
kural.explanation: He will be surrounded by numerous relatives who manifests generosity and affability
kural.couplet: Who knows the use of pleasant words, and liberal gifts can give,Connections, heaps of them, surrounding him shall live

kural.Translation: Large giver and wrathless man Commands on earth countless kinsmen
kural.explanation: No one, in all the world, will have so many relatives (about him), as he who makes large gift, and does not give way to anger
kural.couplet: Than one who gifts bestows and wrath restrains,Through the wide world none larger following gains

kural.Translation: The crows hide not; thy call and eat Welfare abides a man of heart
kural.explanation: The crows do not conceal (their prey), but will call out for others (to share with them) while they eat it; wealth will be with those who show a similar disposition (towards their relatives)
kural.couplet: The crows conceal not, call their friends to come, then eat;Increase of good such worthy ones shall meet

kural.Translation: From public gaze when kings perceive Each one's merits so many thrive
kural.explanation: Many relatives will live near a king, when they observe that he does not look on all alike, but that he looks on each man according to his merit
kural.couplet: Where king regards not all alike, but each in his degree,'Neath such discerning rule many dwell happily

kural.Translation: Forsaken friends will come and stay When cause for discord goes away
kural.explanation: Those who have been friends and have afterwards forsaken him, will return and join themselves (to him), when the cause of disagreement is not to be found in him
kural.couplet: Who once were his, and then forsook him, as beforeWill come around, when cause of disagreement is no more

kural.Translation: Who leaves and returns with motive The king should test him and receive
kural.explanation: When one may have left him, and for some cause has returned to him, let the king fulfil the object (for which he has come back) and thoughtfully receive him again
kural.couplet: Who causeless went away, then to return, for any cause, ask leave;The king should sift their motives well, consider, and receive

kural.Translation: Worse than wrath in excess is Forgetfulness in joy-excess
kural.explanation: More evil than excessive anger, is forgetfulness which springs from the intoxication of great joy
kural.couplet: 'Tis greater ill, it rapture of o'erweening gladness to the soulBring self-forgetfulness than if transcendent wrath control

kural.Translation: Negligence kills renown just as Ceaseless want wisdom destroys
kural.explanation: Forgetfulness will destroy fame, even as constant poverty destroys knowledge
kural.couplet: Perpetual, poverty is death to wisdom of the wise;When man forgets himself his glory dies

kural.Translation: Forgetful nature fails of fame All schools of thinkers say the same
kural.explanation: Thoughtlessness will never acquire fame; and this tenet is upheld by all treatises in the world
kural.couplet: 'To self-oblivious men no praise'; this ruleDecisive wisdom sums of every school

kural.Translation: The fearful find no fortress here The forgetful find good never
kural.explanation: Just as the coward has no defence (by whatever fortifications ha may be surrounded), so the thoughtless has no good (whatever advantages he may possess)
kural.couplet: 'To cowards is no fort's defence'; e'en soThe self-oblivious men no blessing know

kural.Translation: Failing foresight the guardless man Shall rue his folly later on
kural.explanation: The thoughtless man, who provides not against the calamities that may happen, will afterwards repent for his fault
kural.couplet: To him who nought foresees, recks not of anything,The after woe shall sure repentance bring

kural.Translation: Forget none; watch with wakeful care Miss none; the gain is sans compare
kural.explanation: There is nothing comparable with the possession of unfailing thoughtfulness at all times; and towards all persons
kural.couplet: Towards all unswerving, ever watchfulness of soul retain,Where this is found there is no greater gain

kural.Translation: With cautious care pursue a thing Impossible there is nothing
kural.explanation: There is nothing too difficult to be accomplished, if a man set about it carefully, with unflinching endeavour
kural.couplet: Though things are arduous deemed, there's nought may not be won,When work with mind's unslumbering energy and thought is done

kural.Translation: Do what the wise commend as worth If not, for seven births no mirth
kural.explanation: Let (a man) observe and do these things which have been praised (by the wise); if he neglects and fails to perform them, for him there will be no (happiness) throughout the seven births
kural.couplet: Let things that merit praise thy watchful soul employ;Who these despise attain through sevenfold births no joy

kural.Translation: When joy deludes, their fate recall Whom negligence has made to fall
kural.explanation: Let (a king) think of those who have been ruined by neglect, when his mind is elated with joy
kural.couplet: Think on the men whom scornful mind hath brought to nought,When exultation overwhelms thy wildered thought

kural.Translation: Easy it is a thing to get When the mind on it is set
kural.explanation: It is easy for (one) to obtain whatever he may think of, if he can again think of it
kural.couplet: 'Tis easy what thou hast in mind to gain,If what thou hast in mind thy mind retain

kural.Translation: Test and attest impartially Consult and act the laws justly
kural.explanation: To examine into (the crimes which may be committed), to show no favour (to any one), to desire to act with impartiality towards all, and to inflict (such punishments) as may be wisely resolved on,
kural.couplet: Search out, to no one favour show; with heart that justice lovesConsult, then act; this is the rule that right approves

kural.Translation: The earth looks up to sky and thrives And mankind to king's rod of justice
kural.explanation: When there is rain, the living creation thrives; and so when the king rules justly, his subjects thrive
kural.couplet: All earth looks up to heav'n whence raindrops fall;All subjects look to king that ruleth all

kural.Translation: The Sage's scripture and virtue spring From the sceptre of a stately king
kural.explanation: The sceptre of the king is the firm support of the Vedas of the Brahmin, and of all virtues therein described
kural.couplet: Learning and virtue of the sages spring,From all-controlling sceptre of the king

kural.Translation: The world clings to the ruler's feet Whose sceptre clasps the people's heart
kural.explanation: The world will constantly embrace the feet of the great king who rules over his subjects with love
kural.couplet: Whose heart embraces subjects all, lord over mighty landWho rules, the world his feet embracing stands

kural.Translation: Full rains and yields enrich the land Which is ruled by a righteous hand
kural.explanation: Rain and plentiful crops will ever dwell together in the country of the king who sways his sceptre with justice
kural.couplet: Where king, who righteous laws regards, the sceptre wields,There fall the showers, there rich abundance crowns the fields

kural.Translation: Not the spear but the sceptre straight That brings success to monarch's might
kural.explanation: It is not the javelin that gives victory, but the king's sceptre, if it do no injustice
kural.couplet: Not lance gives kings the victory,But sceptre swayed with equity

kural.Translation: The king protects the entire earth And justice protects his royal worth
kural.explanation: The king defends the whole world; and justice, when administered without defect, defends the king
kural.couplet: The king all the whole realm of earth protects;And justice guards the king who right respects

kural.Translation: Hard of access, the unjust king He shall himself his ruin bring
kural.explanation: The king who gives not facile audience (to those who approach him), and who does not examine and pass judgment (on their complaints), will perish in disgrace
kural.couplet: Hard of access, nought searching out, with partial handThe king who rules, shall sink and perish from the land

kural.Translation: Save his subjects and chide the wrong Is flawless duty of a king
kural.explanation: In guarding his subjects (against injury from others), and in preserving them himself; to punish crime
kural.couplet: Abroad to guard, at home to punish, bringsNo just reproach; 'tis work assigned to kings

kural.Translation: Killing killers, the king, behold Weeds removes from cropful field
kural.explanation: For a king to punish criminals with death, is like pulling up the weeds in the green corn
kural.couplet: By punishment of death the cruel to restrain,Is as when farmer frees from weeds the tender grain

kural.Translation: The unjust tyrant oppressor  Is worse than cruel murderer
kural.explanation: The king who gives himself up to oppression and acts unjustly (towards his subjects) is more cruel than the man who leads the life of a murderer
kural.couplet: Than one who plies the murderer's trade, more cruel is the kingWho all injustice works, his subjects harassing

kural.Translation: Sceptered tyrant exacting gold Is \"give\" of lanced robber bold
kural.explanation: The request (for money) of him who holds the sceptre is like the word of a highway robber who stands with a weapon in hand and says "give up your wealth"
kural.couplet: As 'Give' the robber cries with lance uplift,So kings with sceptred hand implore a gift

kural.Translation: Spy wrongs daily and do justice Or day by day the realm decays
kural.explanation: The country of the king who does not daily examine into the wrongs done and distribute justice, will daily fall to ruin
kural.couplet: Who makes no daily search for wrongs, nor justly rules, that kingDoth day by day his realm to ruin bring

kural.Translation: The king shall wealth and subjects lose If his sceptre he dares abuse
kural.explanation: The king, who, without reflecting (on its evil consequences), perverts justice, will lose at once both his wealth and his subjects
kural.couplet: Whose rod from right deflects, who counsel doth refuse,At once his wealth and people utterly shall lose

kural.Translation: Groaning tears caused by tyrant's sway  File the royal wealth away
kural.explanation: Will not the tears, shed by a people who cannot endure the oppression which they suffer (from their king), become a saw to waste away his wealth ?
kural.couplet: His people's tears of sorrow past endurance, are not theySharp instruments to wear the monarch's wealth away

kural.Translation: Glory endures by sceptre right Without it wanes the royal light
kural.explanation: Righteous government gives permanence to (the fame of) kings; without that their fame will have no endurance
kural.couplet: To rulers' rule stability is sceptre right;When this is not, quenched is the rulers' light

kural.Translation: Dry like the earth without rainfall Is graceless king to creatures all
kural.explanation: As is the world without rain, so live a people whose king is without kindness
kural.couplet: As lack of rain to thirsty lands beneath,Is lack of grace in kings to all that breathe

kural.Translation: To have is worse than having not If ruler is unjust despot
kural.explanation: Property gives more sorrow than poverty, to those who live under the sceptre of a king without justice
kural.couplet: To poverty it adds a sharper sting,To live beneath the sway of unjust king

kural.Translation: The sky withdraws season's shower If the king misuses his power
kural.explanation: If the king acts contrary to justice, rain will become unseasonable, and the heavens will withhold their showers
kural.couplet: Where king from right deflecting, makes unrighteous gain,The seasons change, the clouds pour down no rain

kural.Translation: The *six-functioned forget their lore Cows give less if kings guard no more * the six functions are: learning, teaching,  giving,  getting, sacrificing, kindling sacrifice These are duties of Vedic savants
kural.explanation: If the guardian (of the country) neglects to guard it, the produce of the cows will fail, and the men of six duties viz, the Brahmins will forget the vedas
kural.couplet: Where guardian guardeth not, udder of kine grows dry,And Brahmans' sacred lore will all forgotten lie

kural.Translation: A king enquires and gives sentence  Just to prevent future offence
kural.explanation: He is a king who having equitably examined (any injustice which has been brought to his notice), suitably punishes it, so that it may not be again committed
kural.couplet: Who punishes, investigation made in due degree,So as to stay advance of crime, a king is he

kural.Translation: Wield fast the rod but gently lay This strict mildness prolongs the sway
kural.explanation: Let the king, who desires that his prosperity may long remain, commence his preliminary enquires with strictness, and then punish with mildness
kural.couplet: For length of days with still increasing joys on Heav'n who call,Should raise the rod with brow severe, but let it gently fall

kural.Translation: His cruel rod of dreadful deed Brings king's ruin quick indeed
kural.explanation: The cruel-sceptred king, who acts so as to put his subjects in fear, will certainly and quickly come to ruin
kural.couplet: Where subjects dread of cruel wrongs endure,Ruin to unjust king is swift and sure

kural.Translation: As men the king a tyrant call  His days dwindled, hasten his fall
kural.explanation: The king who is spoken of as cruel will quickly perish; his life becoming shortened
kural.couplet: 'Ah! cruel is our king', where subjects sadly say,His age shall dwindle, swift his joy of life decay

kural.Translation: Whose sight is scarce, whose face is foul His wealth seems watched by a ghoul
kural.explanation: The great wealth of him who is difficult of access and possesses a sternness of countenance, is like that which has been obtained by a devil
kural.couplet: Whom subjects scarce may see, of harsh forbidding countenance;His ample wealth shall waste, blasted by demon's glance

kural.Translation: Whose word is harsh, whose sight is rude His wealth and power quickly fade
kural.explanation: The abundant wealth of the king whose words are harsh and whose looks are void of kindness, will instantly perish instead of abiding long, with him
kural.couplet: The tyrant, harsh in speach and hard of eye,His ample joy, swift fading, soon shall die

kural.Translation: Reproofs rough and punishments rude Like files conquering power corrode
kural.explanation: Severe words and excessive punishments will be a file to waste away a king's power for destroying (his enemies)
kural.couplet: Harsh words and punishments severe beyond the right,Are file that wears away the monarch's conquering might

kural.Translation: The king who would not take counsels Rages with wrath-his fortune fails
kural.explanation: The prosperity of that king will waste away, who without reflecting (on his affairs himself), commits them to his ministers, and (when a failure occurs) gives way to anger, and rages against them
kural.couplet: Who leaves the work to those around, and thinks of it no more;If he in wrathful mood reprove, his prosperous days are o'er

kural.Translation: The king who builds not fort betimes Fears his foes in wars and dies
kural.explanation: The king who has not provided himself with a place of defence, will in times of war be seized with fear and quickly perish
kural.couplet: Who builds no fort whence he may foe defy,In time of war shall fear and swiftly die

kural.Translation: The crushing burden borne by earth Is tyrants bound to fools uncouth
kural.explanation: The earth bears up no greater burden than ignorant men whom a cruel sceptre attaches to itself (as the ministers of its evil deeds)
kural.couplet: Tyrants with fools their counsels share:Earth can no heavier burthen bear

kural.Translation: Living in the world implies The bounteous dame of benign eyes
kural.explanation: The world exists through that greatest ornament (of princes), a gracious demeanour
kural.couplet: Since true benignity, that grace exceeding great, residesIn kingly souls, world in happy state abides

kural.Translation: World lives by looks of lovely worth Who lack them are burdens of earth
kural.explanation: The prosperity of the world springs from the kindliness, the existence of those who have no (kindliness) is a burden to the earth
kural.couplet: The world goes on its wonted way, since grace benign is there;All other men are burthen for the earth to bear

kural.Translation: Of tuneless song what is the use? Without gracious looks what are eyes?
kural.explanation: Of what avail is a song if it be inconsistent with harmony ? what is the use of eyes which possess no kindliness
kural.couplet: Where not accordant with the song, what use of sounding chordsWhat gain of eye that no benignant light affords

kural.Translation: Except that they are on the face  What for are eyes sans measured grace
kural.explanation: Beyond appearing to be in the face, what good do they do, those eyes in which is no well-regulated kindness ?
kural.couplet: The seeming eye of face gives no expressive light,When not with duly meted kindness bright

kural.Translation: Kind looks are jewels for eyes to wear Without them they are felt as sore
kural.explanation: Kind looks are the ornaments of the eyes; without these they will be considered (by the wise) to be merely two sores
kural.couplet: Benignity is eyes' adorning grace;Without it eyes are wounds disfiguring face

kural.Translation: Like trees on inert earth they grow Who don't eye to eye kindness show
kural.explanation: They resemble the trees of the earth, who although they have eyes, never look kindly (on others)
kural.couplet: Whose eyes 'neath brow infixed diffuse no rayOf grace; like tree in earth infixed are they

kural.Translation: Ungracious men lack real eyes Men of real eyes show benign grace
kural.explanation: Men without kind looks are men without eyes; those who (really) have eyes are also not devoid of kind looks
kural.couplet: Eyeless are they whose eyes with no benignant lustre shine;Who've eyes can never lack the light of grace benign

kural.Translation: Who gracious are but dutiful Have right for this earth beautiful
kural.explanation: The world is theirs (kings) who are able to show kindness, without injury to their affairs, (administration of justice)
kural.couplet: Who can benignant smile, yet leave no work undone;By them as very own may all the earth be won

kural.Translation: To be benign and bear with foes Who vex us is true virtue's phase
kural.explanation: Patiently to bear with, and show kindness to those who grieve us, is the most excellent of all dispositions
kural.couplet: To smile on those that vex, with kindly face,Enduring long, is most excelling grace

kural.Translation: Men of graceful courtesy Take hemlock and look cheerfully
kural.explanation: Those who desire (to cultivate that degree of) urbanity which all shall love, even after swallowing the poison served to them by their friends, will be friendly with them
kural.couplet: They drink with smiling grace, though poison interfused they see,Who seek the praise of all-esteemed courtesy

kural.Translation: A king should treat these two as eyes  The code of laws and careful spies
kural.explanation: Let a king consider as his eyes these two things, a spy and a book (of laws) universally esteemed
kural.couplet: These two: the code renowned and spies,In these let king confide as eyes

kural.Translation: All that happens, always, to all  The king should know in full detail
kural.explanation: 'Tis duty of the king to learn with speed
kural.couplet: Each day, of every subject every deed,'Tis duty of the king to learn with speed

kural.Translation: Conquests are not for the monarch Who cares not for the Spy's remark
kural.explanation: There is no way for a king to obtain conquests, who knows not the advantage of discoveries made by a spy
kural.couplet: By spies who spies, not weighing things they bring,Nothing can victory give to that unwary king

kural.Translation: His officers, kinsmen and foes  Who watch keenly are worthy spies
kural.explanation: He is a spy who watches all men, to wit, those who are in the king's employment, his relatives, and his enemies
kural.couplet: His officers, his friends, his enemies,All these who watch are trusty spies

kural.Translation: Fearless gaze, suspectless guise  Guarding secrets mark the spies
kural.explanation: A spy is one who is able to assume an appearance which may create no suspicion (in the minds of others), who fears no man's face, and who never reveals (his purpose)
kural.couplet: Of unsuspected mien and all-unfearing eyes,Who let no secret out, are trusty spies

kural.Translation: Guised as monks they gather secrets They betray them not under threats
kural.explanation: He is a spy who, assuming the appearance of an ascetic, goes into (whatever place he wishes), examines into (all, that is needful), and never discovers himself, whatever may be done to him
kural.couplet: As monk or devotee, through every hindrance making way,A spy, whate'er men do, must watchful mind display

kural.Translation: A spy draws out other's secrets Beyond a doubt he clears his facts
kural.explanation: A spy is one who is able to discover what is hidden and who retains no doubt concerning what he has known
kural.couplet: A spy must search each hidden matter out,And full report must render, free from doubt

kural.Translation: The reports given by one spy By another spy verify
kural.explanation: Let not a king receive the information which a spy has discovered and made known to him, until he has examined it by another spy
kural.couplet: Spying by spies, the things they tellTo test by other spies is well

kural.Translation: Engage the spies alone, apart When three agree confirm report
kural.explanation: Let a king employ spies so that one may have no knowledge of the other; and when the information of three agrees together, let him receive it
kural.couplet: One spy must not another see: contrive it so;And things by three confirmed as truth you know

kural.Translation: Give not the spy open reward It would divulge the secret heard!
kural.explanation: Let not a king publicly confer on a spy any marks of his favour; if he does, he will divulge his own secret
kural.couplet: Reward not trusty spy in others' sight,Or all the mystery will come to light

kural.Translation: To own is to own energy All others own but lethargy
kural.explanation: Energy makes out the man of property; as for those who are destitute of it, do they (really) possess what they possess ?
kural.couplet: 'Tis energy gives men o'er that they own a true control;They nothing own who own not energy of soul

kural.Translation: Psychic heart is wealth indeed Worldly wealth departs in speed
kural.explanation: The possession of (energy of) mind is true property; the possession of wealth passes away and abides not
kural.couplet: The wealth of mind man owns a real worth imparts,Material wealth man owns endures not, utterly departs

kural.Translation: The strong in will do not complain  The loss of worldly wealth and gain
kural.explanation: They who are possessed of enduring energy will not trouble themselves, saying, "we have lost our property."
kural.couplet: 'Lost is our wealth,' they utter not this cry distressed,The men of firm concentred energy of soul possessed

kural.Translation: Fortune enquires, enters with boom Where tireless strivers have their home
kural.explanation: Wealth will find its own way to the man of unfailing energy
kural.couplet: The man of energy of soul inflexible,Good fortune seeks him out and comes a friend to dwell

kural.Translation: Water depth is lotus height  Mental strength is men's merit
kural.explanation: The stalks of water-flowers are proportionate to the depth of water; so is men's greatness proportionate to their minds
kural.couplet: With rising flood the rising lotus flower its stem unwinds;The dignity of men is measured by their minds

kural.Translation: Let thoughts be always great and grand  Though they fail their virtues stand
kural.explanation: In all that a king thinks of, let him think of his greatness; and if it should be thrust from him (by fate), it will have the nature of not being thrust from him
kural.couplet: Whate'er you ponder, let your aim be loftly still,Fate cannot hinder always, thwart you as it will

kural.Translation: Elephants are firm when arrows hit Great minds keep fit ev'n in defeat
kural.explanation: The strong minded will not faint, even when all is lost; the elephant stands firm, even when wounded by a shower of arrows
kural.couplet: The men of lofty mind quail not in ruin's fateful hour,The elephant retains his dignity mind arrows' deadly shower

kural.Translation: Heartless persons cannot boast \"We are liberal to our best\"
kural.explanation: Those who have no (greatness of) mind, will not acquire the joy of saying in the world, "we have excercised liaberality"
kural.couplet: The soulless man can never gainTh' ennobling sense of power with men

kural.Translation: Huge elephant sharp in tusk quails  When tiger, less in form, assails
kural.explanation: Although the elephant has a large body, and a sharp tusk, yet it fears the attack of the tiger
kural.couplet: Huge bulk of elephant with pointed tusk all armed,When tiger threatens shrinks away alarmed

kural.Translation: Mental courage is true manhood Lacking that man is like a wood
kural.explanation: Energy is mental wealth; those men who are destitute of it are only trees in the form of men
kural.couplet: Firmness of soul in man is real excellance;Others are trees, their human form a mere pretence

kural.Translation: Quenchless lamp of ancestry goes When foul idleness encloses
kural.explanation: By the darkness, of idleness, the indestructible lamp of family (rank) will be extinguished
kural.couplet: Of household dignity the lustre beaming bright,Flickers and dies when sluggish foulness dims its light

kural.Translation: To make your home an ideal home Loath sloth as sloth; refuse it room
kural.explanation: Let those, who desire that their family may be illustrious, put away all idleness from their conduct
kural.couplet: Let indolence, the death of effort, die,If you'd uphold your household's dignity

kural.Translation: The fool who fosters sluggishness Before he dies ruins his house
kural.explanation: The (lustre of the) family of the ignorant man, who acts under the influence of destructive laziness will perish, even before he is dead
kural.couplet: Who fosters indolence within his breast, the silly elf!The house from which he springs shall perish ere himself

kural.Translation: Who strive not high, sunk deep in sloth Ruin their house by evil growth
kural.explanation: Family (greatness) will be destroyed, and faults will increase, in those men who give way to laziness, and put forth no dignified exertions
kural.couplet: His family decays, and faults unheeded thrive,Who, sunk in sloth, for noble objects doth not strive

kural.Translation: To lag, forget, idle and doze These four are pleasure boats of loss
kural.explanation: Procrastination, forgetfulness, idleness, and sleep, these four things, form the vessel which is desired by those destined to destruction
kural.couplet: Delay, oblivion, sloth, and sleep: these fourAre pleasure-boat to bear the doomed to ruin's shore

kural.Translation: With all the wealth of lords of earth The slothful gain nothing of worth
kural.explanation: It is a rare thing for the idle, even when possessed of the riches of kings who ruled over the whole earth, to derive any great benefit from it
kural.couplet: Though lords of earth unearned possessions gain,The slothful ones no yield of good obtain

kural.Translation: The slothful lacking noble deeds Subject themselves to scornful words
kural.explanation: Those who through idleness, and do not engage themselves in dignified exertion, will subject
kural.couplet: Who hug their sloth, nor noble works attempt,Shall bear reproofs and words of just contempt

kural.Translation: If sloth invades a noble house It will become a slave of foes
kural.explanation: If idleness take up its abode in a king of high birth, it will make him a slave of his enemies
kural.couplet: If sloth a dwelling find mid noble family,Bondsmen to them that hate them shall they be

kural.Translation: The blots on race and rule shall cease When one from sloth gets his release
kural.explanation: When a man puts away idleness, the reproach which has come upon himself and his family will disappear
kural.couplet: Who changes slothful habits savesHimself from all that household rule depraves

kural.Translation: The slothless king shall gain en masse *All regions trod by Lord apace * Hindu mythology holds that Lord Vishnu measured with his feet the three worlds
kural.explanation: The king who never gives way to idleness will obtain entire possession of (the whole earth) passed over by him who measured (the worlds) with His foot
kural.couplet: The king whose life from sluggishness is rid,Shall rule o'er all by foot of mighty god bestrid

kural.Translation: Feel not frustrate saying This hard Who tries attains striving's reward
kural.explanation: Yield not to the feebleness which says, "this is too difficult to be done"; labour will give the greatness (of mind) which is necessary (to do it)
kural.couplet: Say not, 'Tis hard', in weak, desponding hour,For strenuous effort gives prevailing power

kural.Translation: In doing work don't break and shirk The world will quit who quits his work
kural.explanation: Take care not to give up exertion in the midst of a work; the world will abandon those who abandon their unfinished work
kural.couplet: In action be thou, 'ware of act's defeat;The world leaves those who work leave incomplete

kural.Translation: On excellence of industry Depends magnanimous bounty
kural.explanation: The lustre of munificence will dwell only with the dignity of laboriousness or efforts
kural.couplet: In strenuous effort doth resideThe power of helping others: noble pride

kural.Translation: Bounty of man who never strives Like sword in eunuch's hand it fails
kural.explanation: The liberality of him, who does not labour, will fail, like the manliness of a hermaphrodite, who has a sword in its hand
kural.couplet: Beneficent intent in men by whom no strenuous work is wrought,Like battle-axe in sexless being's hand availeth nought

kural.Translation: Work who likes and not pleasure  Wipes grief of friends, pillar secure
kural.explanation: He who desires not pleasure, but desires labour, will be a pillar to sustain his relations, wiping away their sorrows
kural.couplet: Whose heart delighteth not in pleasure, but in action finds delight,He wipes away his kinsmen's grief and stands the pillar of their might

kural.Translation: Industry adds prosperity Indolence brings but poverty
kural.explanation: Labour will produce wealth; idleness will bring poverty
kural.couplet: Effort brings fortune's sure increase,Its absence brings to nothingness

kural.Translation: Illuck abides with sloth they say *Laxmi's gifts with labourers stay *Laxmi the Goddes of wealth and prosperity
kural.explanation: They say that the black Mudevi (the goddess of adversity) dwells with laziness, and the Latchmi (the goddess of prosperity) dwells with the labour of the industrious
kural.couplet: In sluggishness is seen misfortune's lurid form, the wise declare;Where man unslothful toils, she of the lotus flower is there

kural.Translation: Misfortune is disgrace to none The shame is nothing learnt or done
kural.explanation: Adverse fate is no disgrace to any one; to be without exertion and without knowing what should be known, is disgrace
kural.couplet: 'Tis no reproach unpropitious fate should ban;But not to do man's work is foul disgrace to man

kural.Translation: Though fate is against fulfilment Hard labour has ready payment
kural.explanation: Although it be said that, through fate, it cannot be attained, yet labour, with bodily exertion, will yield its reward
kural.couplet: Though fate-divine should make your labour vain;Effort its labour's sure reward will gain

kural.Translation: Tireless Toiler's striving hand Shall leave even the fate behind
kural.explanation: They who labour on, without fear and without fainting will see even fate (put) behind their back
kural.couplet: Who strive with undismayed, unfaltering mind,At length shall leave opposing fate behind

kural.Translation: Laugh away troubles; there is No other way to conquer woes
kural.explanation: If troubles come, laugh; there is nothing like that, to press upon and drive away sorrow
kural.couplet: Smile, with patient, hopeful heart, in troublous hour;Meet and so vanquish grief; nothing hath equal power

kural.Translation: Deluging sorrows come to nought When wise men face them with firm thought
kural.explanation: A flood of troubles will be overcome by the (courageous) thought which the minds of the wise will entertain, even in sorrow
kural.couplet: Though sorrow, like a flood, comes rolling on,When wise men's mind regards it,- it is gone

kural.Translation: Grief they face and put to grief Who grieve not grief by mind's relief
kural.explanation: They give sorrow to sorrow, who in sorrow do not suffer sorrow
kural.couplet: Who griefs confront with meek, ungrieving heart,From them griefs, put to grief, depart

kural.Translation: Who pulls like bulls patiently on Causes grief to grieve anon
kural.explanation: Troubles will vanish (i.e., will be troubled) before the man who (struggles against difficulties) as a
kural.couplet: Like bullock struggle on through each obstructed way;From such an one will troubles, troubled, roll away

kural.Translation: Before the brave grief grieves and goes Who dare a host of pressing woes
kural.explanation: The troubles of that man will be troubled (and disappear) who, however thickly they may come upon him, does not abandon (his purpose)
kural.couplet: When griefs press on, but fail to crush the patient heart,Then griefs defeated, put to grief, depart

kural.Translation: The wise that never gloat in gain Do not fret in fateful ruin
kural.explanation: Will those men ever cry out in sorrow, "we are destitute" who, (in their prosperity), give not way to (undue desire) to keep their wealth
kural.couplet: Who boasted not of wealth, nor gave it all their heart,Will not bemoan the loss, when prosperous days depart

kural.Translation: The wise worry no more of woes Knowing body's butt of sorrows
kural.explanation: The great will not regard trouble as trouble, knowing that the body is the butt of trouble
kural.couplet: 'Man's frame is sorrow's target', the noble mind reflects,Nor meets with troubled mind the sorrows it expects

kural.Translation: Who seek not joy, deem grief norm By sorrows do not come to harm
kural.explanation: That man never experiences sorrow, who does not seek for pleasure, and who considers distress to be natural (to man)
kural.couplet: He seeks not joy, to sorrow man is born, he knows;Such man will walk unharmed by touch of human woes

kural.Translation: In joy to joy who is not bound In grief he grieves not dual round!
kural.explanation: He does not suffer sorrow, in sorrow who does not look for pleasure in pleasure
kural.couplet: Mid joys he yields not heart to joys' controlMid sorrows, sorrow cannot touch his soul

kural.Translation: His glory is esteemed by foes Who sees weal in wanton woes!
kural.explanation: The elevation, which even his enemies will esteem, will be gained by him, who regards pain as pleasure
kural.couplet: Who pain as pleasure takes, he shall acquireThe bliss to which his foes in vain aspire

kural.Translation: He is minister who chooses Right means, time, mode and rare ventures
kural.explanation: The minister is one who can make an excellent choice of means, time, manner of execution, and the difficult undertaking (itself)
kural.couplet: A minister is he who grasps, with wisdom large,Means, time, work's mode, and functions rare he must discharge

kural.Translation: With these he guards people, -by his Knowledge, firmness and manliness
kural.explanation: The minister is one who in addition to the aforesaid five things excels in the possession of firmness,
kural.couplet: A minister must greatness own of guardian power, determined mind,Learn'd wisdom, manly effort with the former five combined

kural.Translation: A minister cherishes friends Divides foes and the parted blends
kural.explanation: The minister is one who can effect discord (among foes), maintain the good-will of his friends and restore to friendship those who have seceded (from him)
kural.couplet: A minister is he whose power can foes divide,Attach more firmly friends, of severed ones can heal the breaches wide

kural.Translation: A minister must sift reflect Select and say surely one fact
kural.explanation: The minister is one who is able to comprehend (the whole nature of an undertaking), execute it in the best manner possible, and offer assuring advice (in time of necessity)
kural.couplet: A minister has power to see the methods help afford,To ponder long, then utter calm conclusive word

kural.Translation: Have him for help who virtue knows Right wisdom speaks, ever apt in acts
kural.explanation: He is the best helper (of the king) who understanding the duties, of the latter, is by his special learning, able to tender the fullest advice, and at all times conversant with the best method (of
kural.couplet: The man who virtue knows, has use of wise and pleasant wordsWith plans for every season apt, in counsel aid affords

kural.Translation: Which subtler brain can stand before The keen in brain with learned love?
kural.explanation: What (contrivances) are there so acute as to resist those who possess natural acuteness in addition to learning ?
kural.couplet: When native subtilty combines with sound scholastic lore,'Tis subtilty surpassing all, which nothing stands before

kural.Translation: Albeit you know to act from books Act after knowing world's outlooks
kural.explanation: Though you are acquainted with the (theoretical) methods (of performing an act), understand the ways of the world and act accordingly
kural.couplet: Though knowing all that books can teach, 'tis truest tactTo follow common sense of men in act

kural.Translation: The man in place must tell the facts Though the ignorant king refutes
kural.explanation: Although the king be utterly ignorant, it is the duty of the minister to give (him) sound advice
kural.couplet: 'Tis duty of the man in place aloud to sayThe very truth, though unwise king may cast his words away

kural.Translation: Seventy crores of foes are better Than a minister with mind bitter
kural.explanation: Far better are seventy crores of enemies (for a king) than a minister at his side who intends (his) ruin
kural.couplet: A minister who by king's side plots evil thingsWorse woes than countless foemen brings

kural.Translation: The unresolved, though well designed To fulfil an act they have no mind
kural.explanation: Those ministers who are destitute of (executive) ability will fail to carry out their projects, although they may have contrived aright
kural.couplet: For gain of end desired just counsel nought availsTo minister, when tact in execution fails

kural.Translation: The goodness called goodness of speech Is goodness which nothing can reach
kural.explanation: The possession of that goodness which is called the goodness of speech is (even to others) better than any other goodness
kural.couplet: A tongue that rightly speaks the right is greatest gain,It stands alone midst goodly things that men obtain

kural.Translation: Since gain or ruin speeches bring Guard against the slips of tongue
kural.explanation: Since (both) wealth and evil result from (their) speech, ministers should most carefully guard themselves against faultiness therein
kural.couplet: Since gain and loss in life on speech depend,From careless slip in speech thyself defend

kural.Translation: A speech is speech that holds ears And attracts ev'n those that are averse
kural.explanation: The (minister's) speech is that which seeks (to express) elements as bind his friends (to himself) and is so delivered as to make even his enemies desire (his friendship)
kural.couplet: 'Tis speech that spell-bound holds the listening ear,While those who have not heard desire to hear

kural.Translation: Weigh thy words and speak; because  No wealth or virtue words surpass
kural.explanation: Understand the qualities (of your hearers) and (then) make your speech; for superior to it, there is neither virtue nor wealth
kural.couplet: Speak words adapted well to various hearers' state;No higher virtue lives, no gain more surely great

kural.Translation: Speak out thy world so that no word Can win it and say untoward
kural.explanation: Deliver your speech, after assuring yourself that no counter speech can defeat your own
kural.couplet: Speak out your speech, when once 'tis past disputeThat none can utter speech that shall your speech refute

kural.Translation: Spotless men speak what is sweet And grasp in others what is meet
kural.explanation: It is the opinion of those who are free from defects in diplomacy that the minister should speak so as to make his hearers desire (to hear more) and grasp the meaning of what he hears himself
kural.couplet: Charming each hearer's ear, of others' words to seize the sense,Is method wise of men of spotless excellence

kural.Translation: No foe defies the speaker clear Flawless, puissant, and free from fear
kural.explanation: It is impossible for any one to conquer him by intrique who possesses power of speech, and is neither faulty nor timid
kural.couplet: Mighty in word, of unforgetful mind, of fearless speech,'Tis hard for hostile power such man to overreach

kural.Translation: The world will quickly carry out The words of counsellors astute
kural.explanation: If there be those who can speak on various subjects in their proper order and in a pleasing manner, the world would readily accept them
kural.couplet: Swiftly the listening world will gather round,When men of mighty speech the weighty theme propound

kural.Translation: They overspeak who do not seek A few and flawless words to speak
kural.explanation: They will desire to utter many words, who do not know how to speak a few faultless ones
kural.couplet: Who have not skill ten faultless words to utter plain,Their tongues will itch with thousand words man's ears to pain

kural.Translation: Who can't express what they have learnt Are bunch of flowers not fragrant
kural.explanation: Those who are unable to set forth their acquirements (before others) are like flowers blossoming in a cluster and yet without fragrance
kural.couplet: Like scentless flower in blooming garland boundAre men who can't their lore acquired to other's ears expound

kural.Translation: Friendship brings gain; but action pure Does every good thing we desire
kural.explanation: The efficacy of support will yield (only) wealth; (but) the efficacy of action will yield all that is desired
kural.couplet: The good external help confers is worldly gain;By action good men every needed gift obtain

kural.Translation: Eschew always acts that do not  Bring good nor glory on their part
kural.explanation: Ministers should at all times avoid acts which, in addition to fame, yield no benefit (for the future)
kural.couplet: From action evermore thyself restrainOf glory and of good that yields no gain

kural.Translation: Those in the world desire for fame Should shun the deed that dims their name
kural.explanation: Those who say, "we will become (better)" should avoid the performance of acts that would destroy (their fame)
kural.couplet: Who tell themselves that nobler things shall yet be wonAll deeds that dim the light of glory must they shun

kural.Translation: Though perils press the faultless wise Shun deeds of mean, shameful device
kural.explanation: Those who have infallible judgement though threatened with peril will not do acts which have brought disgrace (on former ministers)
kural.couplet: Though troubles press, no shameful deed they do,Whose eyes the ever-during vision view

kural.Translation: Do not wrong act and grieve, \"Alas\"  If done, do not repeat it twice
kural.explanation: Let a minister never do acts of which he would have to grieve saying, "what is this I have done"; (but) should he do (them), it were good that he grieved not
kural.couplet: Do nought that soul repenting must deplore,If thou hast sinned, 'tis well if thou dost sin no more

kural.Translation: Though she who begot thee hungers Shun acts denounced by ancient seers
kural.explanation: Though a minister may see his mother starve; let him do not act which the wise would (treat with contempt)
kural.couplet: Though her that bore thee hung'ring thou behold, no deedDo thou, that men of perfect soul have crime decreed

kural.Translation: Pinching poverty of the wise Is more than wealth hoarded by Vice
kural.explanation: Far more excellent is the extreme poverty of the wise than wealth obtained by heaping up of sinful
kural.couplet: Than store of wealth guilt-laden souls obtain,The sorest poverty of perfect soul is richer gain

kural.Translation: Those who dare a forbidden deed Suffer troubles though they succeed
kural.explanation: The actions of those, who have not desisted from doing deeds forbidden (by the great), will, even if they succeed, cause them sorrow
kural.couplet: To those who hate reproof and do forbidden thingWhat prospers now, in after days shall anguish bring

kural.Translation: Gains from weeping, weeping go Though lost, from good deeds blessings flow
kural.explanation: All that has been obtained with tears (to the victim) will depart with tears (to himself); but what has been by fair means; though with loss at first, will afterwards yield fruit
kural.couplet: What's gained through tears with tears shall go;From loss good deeds entail harvests of blessings grow

kural.Translation: The wealth gathered in guilty ways Is water poured in wet clay vase
kural.explanation: (For a minister) to protect (his king) with wealth obtained by foul means is like preserving a vessel of wet clay by filling it with water
kural.couplet: In pot of clay unburnt he water pours and would retain,Who seeks by wrong the realm in wealth and safety to maintain

kural.Translation: A powerful mind does powerful act And all the rest are imperfect
kural.explanation: Firmness in action is (simply) one's firmness of mind; all other (abilities) are not of this nature
kural.couplet: What men call 'power in action' know for 'power of mind'Externe to man all other aids you find

kural.Translation: Shun failing fuss; fail not purpose These two are maxims of the wise
kural.explanation: Not to perform a ruinous act, and not to be discouraged by the ruinous termination of an act, are the two maxims which, the wise say, from the principles of those who have investigated the subject
kural.couplet: 'Each hindrance shun', 'unyielding onward press, If obstacle be there,'These two define your way, so those that search out truth declare

kural.Translation: The strong achieve and then display Woe unto work displayed midway
kural.explanation: So to perform an act as to publish it (only) at its termination is (true) manliness; for to announce it beforehand, will cause irremediable sorrow
kural.couplet: Man's fitting work is known but by success achieved;In midst the plan revealed brings ruin ne'er to be retrieved

kural.Translation: Easy it is to tell a fact But hard it is to know and act
kural.explanation: To say (how an act is to be performed) is (indeed) easy for any one; but far difficult it is to do according to what has been said
kural.couplet: Easy to every man the speech that shows the way;Hard thing to shape one's life by words they say

kural.Translation: Dynamic deeds of a doughty soul Shall win the praise of king and all
kural.explanation: The firmness in action of those who have become great by the excellence (of their counsel) will, by attaining its fulfilment in the person of the king, be esteemed (by all).
kural.couplet: The power in act of men renowned and great,With king acceptance finds and fame through all the state

kural.Translation: The will-to-do achieves the deed When mind that wills is strong indeed
kural.explanation: If those who have planned (an undertaking) possess firmness (in executing it) they will obtain what they have desired even as they have desired it
kural.couplet: Whate'er men think, ev'n as they think, may men obtain,If those who think can steadfastness of will retain

kural.Translation: Scorn not the form: for men there are Like linchpin of big rolling car
kural.explanation: Let none be despised for (their) size; (for) the world has those who resemble the linch-pin of the big rolling car
kural.couplet: Despise not men of modest bearing; Look not at form, but what men are:For some there live, high functions sharing, Like linch-pin of the mighty car

kural.Translation: Waver not; do wakefully  The deed resolved purposefully
kural.explanation: An act that has been firmly resolved on must be as firmly carried out without delay
kural.couplet: What clearly eye discerns as right, with steadfast will,And mind unslumbering, that should man fulfil

kural.Translation: Do with firm will though pains beset  The deed that brings delight at last
kural.explanation: Though it should cause increasing sorrow (at the outset), do with firmness the act that yield bliss (in the end)
kural.couplet: Though toil and trouble face thee, firm resolve hold fast,And do the deeds that pleasure yield at last

kural.Translation: The world merits no other strength But strength of will-to-do at length
kural.explanation: The great will not esteem those who esteem not firmness of action, whatever other abilities the latter may possess
kural.couplet: The world desires not men of every power possessed,Who power in act desire not,- crown of all the rest

kural.Translation: When counsel takes a resolve strong Weak delay of action is wrong
kural.explanation: Consultation ends in forming a resolution (to act); (but) delay in the execution of that resolve is an evil
kural.couplet: The Resolve is counsel's end, If resolutions halt In weak delays, still unfulfilled, 'tis grievous fault

kural.Translation: Delay such acts as need delay Delay not acts that need display
kural.explanation: Sleep over such (actions) as may be slept over; (but) never over such as may not be slept over
kural.couplet: Slumber when sleepy work's in hand beware Thou slumber not when action calls for sleepless care

kural.Translation: It's best to act when feasible If not see what is possible
kural.explanation: Whenever it is possible (to overcome your enemy) the act (of fighting) is certainly good; if not, endeavour to employ some more successful method
kural.couplet: When way is clear, prompt let your action be; When not, watch till some open path you see

kural.Translation: Work or foe left unfinished Flare up like fire unextinguished
kural.explanation: When duly considered, the incomplete execution of an undertaking and hostility will grow and destroy one like the (unextinguished) remnant of a fire
kural.couplet: With work or foe, when you neglect some little thing, If you reflect, like smouldering fire, 'twill ruin bring

kural.Translation: Money and means, time, place and deed Decide these five and then proceed
kural.explanation: Do an act after a due consideration of the (following) five, viz money, means, time, execution and place
kural.couplet: Treasure and instrument and time and deed and place of act These five, till every doubt remove, think o'er with care exact

kural.Translation: Weigh well the end, hindrance, profit  And then pursue a fitting act
kural.explanation: An act is to be performed after considering the exertion required, the obstacles to be encountered, and the great profit to be gained (on its completion)
kural.couplet: Accomplishment, the hindrances, large profits won By effort these compare,- then let the work be done

kural.Translation: Know first the secret from experts That is the way of fruitful acts
kural.explanation: The method of performance for one who has begun an act is to ascertain the mind of him who knows the secret thereof
kural.couplet: Who would succeed must thus begin first let him ask The thoughts of them who thoroughly know the task

kural.Translation: Lure a tusker by a tusker Achieve a deed by deed better
kural.explanation: To make one undertaking the means of accomplishing another (similar to it) is like making one rutting elephant the means of capturing another
kural.couplet: By one thing done you reach a second work's accomplishment; So furious elephant to snare its fellow brute is sent

kural.Translation: Than doing good to friends it is More urgent to befriend the foes
kural.explanation: One should rather hasten to secure the alliance of the foes (of one's foes) than perform good offices to one's friends
kural.couplet: Than kindly acts to friends more urgent thing to do, Is making foes to cling as friends attached to you

kural.Translation: Small statesmen fearing people's fear Submit to foes superior
kural.explanation: Ministers of small states, afraid of their people being frightened, will yield to and acknowledge their superior foes, if the latter offer them a chance of reconciliation
kural.couplet: The men of lesser realm, fearing the people's inward dread, Accepting granted terms, to mightier ruler bow the head

kural.Translation: Love, noble birth, good courtesy Pleasing kings mark true embassy
kural.explanation: The qualification of an ambassador are affection (for his relations) a fitting birth, and the possession of attributes pleasing to royalty
kural.couplet: Benevolence high birth, the courtesy kings love:-These qualities the envoy of a king approve

kural.Translation: Envoys must bear love for their prince Knowledge and learned eloquence
kural.explanation: Love (to his sovereign), knowledge (of his affairs), and a discriminating power of speech (before other sovereigns) are the three sine qua non qualifications of an ambassador
kural.couplet: Love, knowledge, power of chosen words, three things,Should he possess who speaks the words of kings

kural.Translation: Savant among savants, he pleads  Before lanced king, triumphant words
kural.explanation: To be powerful in politics among those who are learned (in ethics) is the character of him who speaks
kural.couplet: Mighty in lore amongst the learned must he be,Midst jav'lin-bearing kings who speaks the words of victory

kural.Translation: Who has these three: good form, sense, lore Can act as bold ambassador
kural.explanation: He may go on a mission (to foreign rulers) who has combined in him all these three viz, (natural) sense, an attractive bearing and well-tried learning
kural.couplet: Sense, goodly grace, and knowledge exquisiteWho hath these three for envoy's task is fit

kural.Translation: Not harsh, the envoy's winsome ways Does good by pleasant words concise
kural.explanation: He is an ambassador who (in the presence of foreign rulers) speaks briefly, avoids harshness, talks so as to make them smile, and thus brings good (to his own sovereign)
kural.couplet: In terms concise, avoiding wrathful speech, who utters pleasant word,An envoy he who gains advantage for his lord

kural.Translation: Learned; fearless, the envoy tends Convincing words which time demands
kural.explanation: He is an ambassador who having studied (politics) talks impressively, is not afraid of angry looks, and knows (to employ) the art suited to the time
kural.couplet: An envoy meet is he, well-learned, of fearless eyeWho speaks right home, prepared for each emergency

kural.Translation: Knowing duty time and place The envoy employs mature phrase
kural.explanation: He is chief (among ambassadors) who understands the proper decorum (before foreign princes), seeks the (proper) occasion, knows the (most suitable) place, and delivers his message after (due)
kural.couplet: He is the best who knows what's due, the time considered well,The place selects, then ponders long ere he his errand tell

kural.Translation: The true envoy of three virtues Is pure helpful and bold in views
kural.explanation: The qualifications of him who faithfully delivers his (sovereign's) message are purity, the support (of foreign ministers), and boldness, with truthfulness in addition to the (aforesaid) three
kural.couplet: Integrity, resources, soul determined, truthfulnessWho rightly speaks his message must these marks possess

kural.Translation: The envoy who ports the king's message Has flawless words and heart's courage
kural.explanation: He alone is fit to communicate (his sovereign's) reply, who possesses the firmness not to utter even inadvertently what may reflect discredit (on the latter)
kural.couplet: His faltering lips must utter no unworthy thing,Who stands, with steady eye, to speak the mandates of his king

kural.Translation: Braving death the bold envoy Assures his king's safety and joy
kural.explanation: He is the ambassador who fearlessly seeks his sovereign's good though it should cost him his life (to deliver his message)
kural.couplet: Death to the faithful one his embassy may bring;To envoy gains assured advantage for his king

kural.Translation: Move with hostile kings as with fire  Not coming close nor going far
kural.explanation: Thus let them act who dwell beneath of warlike kings the palace-roof
kural.couplet: Who warm them at the fire draw not too near, nor keep too much aloof;Thus let them act who dwell beneath of warlike kings the palace-roof

kural.Translation: Crave not for things which kings desire  This brings thee their fruitful favour
kural.explanation: For ministers not to cover the things desired by their kings will through the kings themselves yield them everlasting wealth
kural.couplet: To those who prize not state that kings are wont to prize,The king himself abundant wealth supplies

kural.Translation: Guard thyself from petty excess Suspected least, there's no redress
kural.explanation: Ministers who would save themselves should avoid (the commission of) serious errors for if the king's suspicion is once roused, no one can remove it
kural.couplet: Who would walk warily, let him of greater faults beware;To clear suspicions once aroused is an achievement rare

kural.Translation: Whisper not; nor smile exchange Amidst august men's assemblage
kural.explanation: While in the presence of the sovereign, ministers should neither whisper to nor smile at others
kural.couplet: All whispered words and interchange of smiles repress,In presence of the men who kingly power possess

kural.Translation: Hear not, ask not the king's secret Hear only when he lets it out
kural.explanation: (When the king is engaged) in secret counsel (with others), ministers should neither over-hear anything whatever nor pry into it with inquisitive questions, but (wait to) listen when it is divulged (by
kural.couplet: Seek not, ask not, the secret of the king to hear;But if he lets the matter forth, give ear

kural.Translation: Discern his mood and time and tell No dislikes but what king likes well
kural.explanation: Knowing the (king's disposition and seeking the right time, (the minister) should in a pleasing manner suggest things such as are desirable and not disagreeable
kural.couplet: Knowing the signs, waiting for fitting time, with courteous care,Things not displeasing, needful things, declare

kural.Translation: Tell pleasing things; and never tell Even if pressed what is futile
kural.explanation: Ministers should (always) give agreeable advice but on no occasion recommend useless actions, though requested (to do so)
kural.couplet: Speak pleasant things, but never utter idle word;Not though by monarch's ears with pleasure heard

kural.Translation: As young and kinsman do not slight; Look with awe king's light and might
kural.explanation: Ministers should behave in accordance with the (Divine) light in the person of kings and not despise them saying, "He is our junior (in age) and connected with our family!"
