kural.couplet: Say not, 'He's young, my kinsman,' despising thus your king;But reverence the glory kingly state doth bring

kural.Translation: The clear-visioned do nothing base Deeming they have the monarch's grace
kural.explanation: Those whose judgement is firm will not do what is disagreeable (to the sovereign) saying (within
kural.couplet: 'We've gained his grace, boots nought what graceless acts we do',So deem not sages who the changeless vision view

kural.Translation: Worthless acts based on friendship old  Shall spell ruin and woe untold
kural.explanation: The (foolish) claim with which a minister does unbecoming acts because of his (long) familiarity (with the king) will ensure his ruin
kural.couplet: Who think 'We're ancient friends' and do unseemly things;To these familiarity sure ruin brings

kural.Translation: Who reads the mind by look, untold Adorns the changeless sea-girt world
kural.explanation: The minister who by looking (at the king) understands his mind without being told (of it), will be a perpetual ornament to the world which is surrounded by a never-drying sea
kural.couplet: Who knows the sign, and reads unuttered thought, the gem is he,Of earth round traversed by the changeless sea

kural.Translation: Take him as God who reads the thought Of another man with without a doubt
kural.explanation: He is to be esteemed a god who is able to ascertain without a doubt what is within (one's mind)
kural.couplet: Undoubting, who the minds of men can scan,As deity regard that gifted man

kural.Translation: By sign who scans the sign admit At any cost in cabinet
kural.explanation: The king should ever give whatever (is asked) of his belongings and secure him who, by the indications (of his own mind) is able to read those of another
kural.couplet: Who by the sign the signs interprets plain,Give any member up his aid to gain

kural.Translation: Untold, he who divines the thought Though same in form is quite apart
kural.explanation: Those who understand one's thoughts without being informed (thereof) and those who do not, may (indeed) resemble one another bodily; still are they different (mentally)
kural.couplet: Who reads what's shown by signs, though words unspoken be,In form may seem as other men, in function nobler far is he

kural.Translation: Among senses what for is eye If thought by thought one can't descry?
kural.explanation: Of what use are the eyes amongst one's members, if they cannot by their own indications dive those of another ?
kural.couplet: By sign who knows not sings to comprehend, what gain,'Mid all his members, from his eyes does he obtain

kural.Translation: What throbs in mind the face reflects Just as mirror nearby objects
kural.explanation: As the mirror reflects what is near so does the face show what is uppermost in the mind
kural.couplet: As forms around in crystal mirrored clear we find,The face will show what's throbbing in the mind

kural.Translation: Than face what is subtler to tell First if the mind feels well or ill
kural.explanation: Is there anything so full of knowledge as the face ? (No) it precedes the mind, whether (the latter is) pleased or vexed
kural.couplet: Than speaking countenance hath aught more prescient skill?Rejoice or burn with rage, 'tis the first herald still

kural.Translation: Just standing in front would suffice For those who read the mind on face
kural.explanation: If the king gets those who by looking into his mind can understand (and remove) what has occurred (to him) it is enough that he stand looking at their face
kural.couplet: To see the face is quite enough, in presence brought,When men can look within and know the lurking thought

kural.Translation: Friend or foe the eyes will show To those who changing outlooks know
kural.explanation: If a king gets ministers who can read the movements of the eye, the eyes (of foreign kings) will (themselves) reveal (to him) their hatred or friendship
kural.couplet: The eye speaks out the hate or friendly soul of man;To those who know the eye's swift varying moods to scan

kural.Translation: The scale of keen discerning minds  Is eye and eye that secrets finds
kural.explanation: The measuring-rod of those (ministers) who say "we are acute" will on inquiry be found to be their (own) eyes and nothing else
kural.couplet: The men of keen discerning soul no other test apply(When you their secret ask) than man's revealing eye

kural.Translation: The pure in thought and eloquence  Adapt their words to audience
kural.explanation: Let the pure who know the arrangement of words speak with deliberation after ascertaining (the nature of) the court (then assembled)
kural.couplet: Men pure in heart, who know of words the varied force,Should to their audience known adapt their well-arranged discourse

kural.Translation: Who know the art of speech shall suit Their chosen words to time in fact
kural.explanation: Let the good who know the uses of words speak with a clear knowledge after ascertaining the time (suited to the court)
kural.couplet: Good men to whom the arts of eloquence are known,Should seek occasion meet, and say what well they've made their own

kural.Translation: They speak in vain at length who talk Words unversed which ears don't take
kural.explanation: Those who undertake to speak without knowing the (nature of the) court are ignorant of the quality of words as well as devoid of the power (of learning)
kural.couplet: Unversed in councils, who essays to speakKnows not the way of suasive words,- and all is weak

kural.Translation: Before the bright be brilliant light Before the muff be mortar white
kural.explanation: Ministers should be lights in the assembly of the enlightned, but assume the pure whiteness of mortar (ignorance) in that of fools
kural.couplet: Before the bright ones shine as doth the lightBefore the dull ones be as purest stucco white

kural.Translation: Modest restraint all good excels Which argues not before elders
kural.explanation: The modesty by which one does not rush forward and speak in (an assembly of) superiors is the best among all (one's) good qualities
kural.couplet: Midst all good things the best is modest grace,That speaks not first before the elders' face

kural.Translation: Tongue-slip before the talented wise is like slipping from righteous ways
kural.explanation: (For a minister) to blunder in the presence of those who have acquired a vast store of learning and know (the value thereof) is like a good man stumbling (and falling away) from the path (of virtue)
kural.couplet: As in the way one tottering falls, is slip beforeThe men whose minds are filled with varied lore

kural.Translation: The learning of the learned shines Valued by flawless scholar-minds
kural.explanation: The learning of those who have read and understood (much) will shine in the assembly of those who faultlessly examine (the nature of) words
kural.couplet: The learning of the learned sage shines brightTo those whose faultless skill can value it aright

kural.Translation: To address understanding ones Is to water beds of growing grains
kural.explanation: Lecturing to those who have the ability to understand (for themselves) is like watering a bed of plants that are growing (of themselves)
kural.couplet: To speak where understanding hearers you obtain,Is sprinkling water on the fields of growing grain

kural.Translation: O ye who speak before the keen Forgetful, address not the mean
kural.explanation: Those who are able to speak good things impressively in an assembly of the good should not even forgetfully speak them in that of the low
kural.couplet: In councils of the good, who speak good things with penetrating power,In councils of the mean, let them say nought, e'en in oblivious hour

kural.Translation: To hostiles who wise words utters Pours ambrosia into gutters
kural.explanation: To utter (a good word) in the assembly of those who are of inferior rank is like dropping nectar on the ground
kural.couplet: Ambrosia in the sewer spilt, is wordSpoken in presence of the alien herd

kural.Translation: The pure fail not in power of words Knowing grand council's moods and modes
kural.explanation: The pure who know the classification of words having first ascertained the nature (of the court) will not (through fear) falter in their speech before the powerful body
kural.couplet: Men, pure in heart, who know of words the varied force,The mighty council's moods discern, nor fail in their discourse

kural.Translation: Among scholars he is scholar Who holds scholars with learned lore
kural.explanation: Those who can agreeably set forth their acquirements before the learned will be regarded as the most learned among the learned
kural.couplet: Who what they've learned, in penetrating words heve learned to say,Before the learn'd among the learn'd most learn'd are they

kural.Translation: Many brave foes and die in fields The fearless few face wise councils
kural.explanation: Many indeed may (fearlessly) die in the presence of (their) foes; (but) few are those who are fearless in the assembly (of the learned)
kural.couplet: Many encountering death in face of foe will hold their ground;Who speak undaunted in the council hall are rarely found

kural.Translation: Impress the learned with your lore From greater savants learn still more
kural.explanation: (Ministers) should agreeably set forth their acquirements before the learned and acquire more (knowledge) from their superiors (in learning)
kural.couplet: What you have learned, in penetrating words speak out beforeThe learn'd; but learn what men more learn'd can teach you more

kural.Translation: Grammar and logic learn so that Foes you can boldly retort
kural.explanation: In order to reply fearlessly before a foreign court, (ministers) should learn logic according to the rules (of grammar)
kural.couplet: By rule, to dialectic art your mind apply,That in the council fearless you may make an apt reply

kural.Translation: To cowards what can sword avail And books to those who councils fail?
kural.explanation: What have they to do with a sword who are not valiant, or they with learning who are afraid of an intelligent assembly ?
kural.couplet: To those who lack the hero's eye what can the sword availOr science what, to those before the council keen who quail

kural.Translation: Like eunuch's sword in field, is vain His lore who fears men of brain
kural.explanation: The learning of him who is diffident before an assembly is like the shining sword of an hermaphrodite in the presence of his foes
kural.couplet: As shining sword before the foe which 'sexless being' bears,Is science learned by him the council's face who fears

kural.Translation: Though learned much his lore is dead Who says no good before the good
kural.explanation: Those who cannot agreeably speak good things before a good assembly are indeed unprofitable persons inspite of all their various acquirements
kural.couplet: Though many things they've learned, yet useless are they all,To man who cannot well and strongly speak in council hall

kural.Translation: Who fear to face good assembly Are learned idiots, certainly
kural.explanation: They who, though they have learned and understood, are yet afraid of the assembly of the good, are said to be inferior (even) to the illiterate
kural.couplet: Who, though they've learned, before the council of the good men quake,Than men unlearn'd a lower place must take

kural.Translation: They are breathing dead who dare not Empress before the wise their art
kural.explanation: Those who through fear of the assembly are unable to set forth their learning in an interesting manner, though alive, are yet like the dead
kural.couplet: Who what they've learned, in penetrating words know not to say,The council fearing, though they live, as dead are they

kural.Translation: It's country which has souls of worth Unfailing yields and ample wealth
kural.explanation: A kingdom is that in which (those who carry on) a complete cultivation, virtuous persons, and
kural.couplet: Where spreads fertility unfailing, where resides a band,Of virtuous men, and those of ample wealth, call that a 'land'

kural.Translation: The Land has large luring treasure Where pests are nil and yields are sure
kural.explanation: A kingdom is that which is desire for its immense wealth, and which grows greatly in prosperity, being free from destructive causes
kural.couplet: That is a 'land' which men desire for wealth's abundant share,Yielding rich increase, where calamities are rare

kural.Translation: It's land that bears pressing burdens And pays its tax which king demands
kural.explanation: A kingdom is that which can bear any burden that may be pressed on it (from adjoining kingdoms) and (yet) pay the full tribute to its sovereign
kural.couplet: When burthens press, it bears; Yet, With unfailing handTo king due tribute pays: that is the 'land'

kural.Translation: It is country which is free from Fierce famine, plague and foemen's harm
kural.explanation: A kingdom is that which continues to be free from excessive starvation, irremediable epidemics, and destructive foes
kural.couplet: That is a 'land' whose peaceful annals know,Nor famine fierce, nor wasting plague, nor ravage of the foe

kural.Translation: Sects and ruinous foes are nil No traitors in a land tranquil
kural.explanation: A kingdom is that which is without various (irregular) associations, destructive internal enemies, and murderous savages who (sometimes) harass the sovereign
kural.couplet: From factions free, and desolating civil strife, and bandOf lurking murderers that king afflict, that is the 'land'

kural.Translation: The land of lands no ruin knows Even in grief its wealth yet grows
kural.explanation: The learned say that the best kingdom is that which knows no evil (from its foes), and, if injured (at all), suffers no diminution in its fruitfulness
kural.couplet: Chief of all lands is that, where nought disturbs its peace;Or, if invaders come, still yields its rich increase

kural.Translation: Waters up and down, hills and streams With strong forts as limbs country beams
kural.explanation: The constituents of a kingdom are the two waters (from above and below), well situated hills and an undestructible fort
kural.couplet: Waters from rains and springs, a mountain near, and waters thence;These make a land, with fortress' sure defence

kural.Translation: Rich yield, delight, defence and wealth Are jewels of lands with blooming health
kural.explanation: Freedom from epidemics, wealth, produce, happiness and protection (to subjects); these five, the learned, say, are the ornaments of a kingdom
kural.couplet: A country's jewels are these five: unfailing health,Fertility, and joy, a sure defence, and wealth

kural.Translation: A land is land which yields unsought Needing hard work the land is nought
kural.explanation: The learned say that those are kingdom whose wealth is not laboured for, and those not, whose wealth is only obtained through labour
kural.couplet: That is a land that yields increase unsought,That is no land whose gifts with toil are bought

kural.Translation: Though a land has thus every thing It is worthless without a king
kural.explanation: Although in possession of all the above mentioned excellences, these are indeed of no use to a country, in the absence of harmony between the sovereign and the sujects
kural.couplet: Though blest with all these varied gifts' increase,A land gains nought that is not with its king at peace

kural.Translation: The fort is vital for offence Who fear the foes has its defence
kural.explanation: A fort is an object of importance to those who march (against their foes) as well as to those who through fear (of pursuers) would seek it for shelter
kural.couplet: A fort is wealth to those who act against their foes;Is wealth to them who, fearing, guard themselves from woes

kural.Translation: A crystal fount, a space a mount Thick woods form a fort paramount
kural.explanation: A fort is that which has everlasting water, plains, mountains and cool shady forests
kural.couplet: A fort is that which owns fount of waters crystal clear,An open space, a hill, and shade of beauteous forest near

kural.Translation: An ideal fort's so says science: High, broad, strong and hard for access
kural.explanation: The learned say that a fortress is an enclosure having these four (qualities) viz, height, breadth, strength and inaccessibility
kural.couplet: Height, breadth, strength, difficult access:Science declares a fort must these possess

kural.Translation: Ample in space, easy to hold The fort foils enemies bold
kural.explanation: A fort is that which has an extensive space within, but only small places to be guarded, and such as can destroy the courage of besieging foes
kural.couplet: A fort must need but slight defence, yet ample be,Defying all the foeman's energy

kural.Translation: Impregnable with stores of food Cosy to live-That fort is good
kural.explanation: A fort is that which cannot be captured, which abounds in suitable provisions, and affords a position of easy defence to its inmates
kural.couplet: Impregnable, containing ample stores of food,A fort for those within, must be a warlike station good

kural.Translation: A fort is full of stores and arms And brave heroes to meet alarms
kural.explanation: A fort is that which has all (needful) things, and excellent heroes that can help it against destruction (by foes)
kural.couplet: A fort, with all munitions amply stored,In time of need should good reserves afford

kural.Translation: Besieging foes a fort withstands Darts and mines of treacherous hands
kural.explanation: A fort is that which cannot be captured by blockading, assaulting, or undermining it
kural.couplet: A fort should be impregnable to foes who gird it round,Or aim there darts from far, or mine beneath the ground

kural.Translation: A fort holds itself and defies The attacks of encircling foes
kural.explanation: That is a fort whose inmates are able to overcome without losing their ground, even abler men who have besieged it
kural.couplet: Howe'er the circling foe may strive access to win,A fort should give the victory to those who guard within

kural.Translation: A fort it is that fells the foes And gains by deeds a name glorious
kural.explanation: A fort is that which derives excellence from the stratagems made (by its inmates) to defeat their enemies in the battlefield
kural.couplet: At outset of the strife a fort should foes dismay;And greatness gain by deeds in every glorious day

kural.Translation: But a fort however grand Is nil if heroes do not stand
kural.explanation: Although a fort may possess all (the above-said) excellence, it is, as it were without these, if its inmates possess not the excellence of action
kural.couplet: Howe'er majestic castled walls may rise,To craven souls no fortress strength supplies

kural.Translation: Naught exists that can, save wealth Make the worthless as men of worth
kural.explanation: Besides wealth there is nothing that can change people of no importance into those of (some) importance
kural.couplet: Nothing exists save wealth, that canChange man of nought to worthy man

kural.Translation: The have-nothing poor all despise The men of wealth all raise and praise
kural.explanation: All despise the poor; (but) all praise the rich
kural.couplet: Those who have nought all will despise;All raise the wealthy to the skies

kural.Translation: Waneless wealth is light that goes To every land and gloom removes
kural.explanation: The imperishable light of wealth goes into regions desired (by its owner) and destroys the darkness (of enmity therein)
kural.couplet: Wealth, the lamp unfailing, speeds to every land,Dispersing darkness at its lord's command

kural.Translation: The blameless wealth from fairest means Brings good virtue and also bliss
kural.explanation: The wealth acquired with a knowledge of the proper means and without foul practices will yield virtue and happiness
kural.couplet: Their wealth, who blameless means can use aright,Is source of virtue and of choice delight

kural.Translation: Riches devoid of love and grace Off with it; it is disgrace!
kural.explanation: (Kings) should rather avoid than seek the accumulation of wealth which does not flow in with mercy and love
kural.couplet: Wealth gained by loss of love and grace,Let man cast off from his embrace

kural.Translation: Escheats, derelicts; spoils of war Taxes duties are king's treasure
kural.explanation: The spoils of slaughtered foes; these are the royal revenues
kural.couplet: Wealth that falls to him as heir, wealth from the kingdom's dues,

kural.Translation: Grace the child of love is nourished By the wet-nurse of wealth cherished
kural.explanation: The child mercy which is borne by love grows under the care of the rich nurse of wealth
kural.couplet: 'Tis love that kindliness as offspring bears:And wealth as bounteous nurse the infant rears

kural.Translation: Treasures in hand fulfil all things Like hill-tuskers the wars of kings
kural.explanation: An undertaking of one who has wealth in one's hands is like viewing an elephant-fight from a hill-top
kural.couplet: As one to view the strife of elephants who takes his stand,On hill he's climbed, is he who works with money in his hand

kural.Translation: Make wealth; there is no sharper steel The insolence of foes to quell
kural.explanation: Accumulate wealth; it will destroy the arrogance of (your) foes; there is no weapon sharper than it
kural.couplet: Make money! Foeman's insolence o'ergrownTo lop away no keener steel is known

kural.Translation: They have joy and virtue at hand Who acquire treasures abundant
kural.explanation: To those who have honestly acquired an abundance of riches, the other two, (virtue and pleasure) are things easy (of acquisition)
kural.couplet: Who plenteous store of glorious wealth have gained,By them the other two are easily obtained

kural.Translation: The daring well-armed winning force Is king's treasure and main resource
kural.explanation: The army which is complete in (its) parts and conquers without fear of wounds is the chief wealth of the king
kural.couplet: A conquering host, complete in all its limbs, that fears no wound,Mid treasures of the king is chiefest found

kural.Translation: Through shots and wounds brave heroes hold Quailing not in fall, the field
kural.explanation: Ancient army can alone have the valour which makes it stand by its king at the time of defeat, fearless of wounds and unmindful of its reduced strength
kural.couplet: In adverse hour, to face undaunted might of conquering foe,Is bravery that only veteran host can show

kural.Translation: Sea-like ratfoes roar What if? They perish at a cobra's whiff
kural.explanation: What if (a host of) hostile rats roar like the sea ? They will perish at the mere breath of the cobra
kural.couplet: Though, like the sea, the angry mice send forth their battle cry;What then? The dragon breathes upon them, and they die

kural.Translation: The army guards its genial flame Not crushed, routed nor marred in name
kural.explanation: That indeed is an army which has stood firm of old without suffering destruction or deserting (to the enemy)
kural.couplet: That is a host, by no defeats, by no desertions shamed,For old hereditary courage famed

kural.Translation: The real army with rallied force Resists even Death-God fierce
kural.explanation: That indeed is an army which is capable of offering a united resistance, even if Yama advances against it with fury
kural.couplet: That is a 'host' that joins its ranks, and mightily withstands,Though death with sudden wrath should fall upon its bands

kural.Translation: Manly army has merits four:- Stately-march, faith, honour, valour
kural.explanation: Valour, honour, following in the excellent-footsteps (of its predecessors) and trust-worthiness; these four alone constitute the safeguard of an army
kural.couplet: Valour with honour, sure advance in glory's path, with confidence;To warlike host these four are sure defence

kural.Translation: Army sets on to face to foes Knowing how the trend of war goes
kural.explanation: That is an army which knowing the art of warding off an impending struggle, can bear against the dust-van (of a hostile force)
kural.couplet: A valiant army bears the onslaught, onward goes,Well taught with marshalled ranks to meet their coming foes

kural.Translation: Army gains force by grand array Lacking in stay or dash in fray
kural.explanation: Though destitute of courage to fight and strength (to endure), an army may yet gain renown by the splendour of its appearance
kural.couplet: Though not in war offensive or defensive skilled;An army gains applause when well equipped and drilled

kural.Translation: Army shall win if it is free From weakness, aversion, poverty
kural.explanation: An army can triumph (over its foes) if it is free from diminution; irremediable aversion and poverty
kural.couplet: Where weakness, clinging fear and povertyAre not, the host will gain the victory

kural.Translation: With troops in large numbers on rolls Army can't march missing gen'rals
kural.explanation: Though an army may contain a large number of permanent soldiers, it cannot last if it has no generals
kural.couplet: Though men abound, all ready for the war,No army is where no fit leaders are

kural.Translation: Stand not before my chief, O foes! Many who stood, in stones repose
kural.explanation: O my foes, stand not before my leader; (for) many are those who did so but afterwards stood (in the shape of) statues
kural.couplet: Ye foes stand not before my lord for many a oneWho did my lord withstand, now stands in stone

kural.Translation: To lift a lance that missed a tusker Is prouder than shaft that hit a hare
kural.explanation: It is more pleasant to hold the dart that has missed an elephant than that which has hit hare in the forest
kural.couplet: Who aims at elephant, though dart should fail, has greater praiseThan he who woodland hare with winged arrow slays

kural.Translation: Valour is fight with fierce courage Mercy to the fallen is its edge
kural.explanation: The learned say that fierceness (incontest with a foe) is indeed great valour; but to become a benefactor in case of accident (to a foe) is the extreme (limit) of that valour
kural.couplet: Fierceness in hour of strife heroic greatness shows;Its edge is kindness to our suffering foes

kural.Translation: At the tusker he flings his lance One in body smiles another chance
kural.explanation: The hero who after casting the lance in his hand on an elephant, comes (in search of another) will pluck the one (that sticks) in his body and laugh (exultingly)
kural.couplet: At elephant he hurls the dart in hand; for weapon pressed,He laughs and plucks the javelin from his wounded breast

kural.Translation: When lances dart if heroes wink \"It is a rout\" the world will think
kural.explanation: Is it not a defeat to the valiant to wink and destroy their ferocious look when a lance in cast at them (by their foe) ?
kural.couplet: To hero fearless must it not defeat appear,If he but wink his eye when foemen hurls his spear

kural.Translation: The brave shall deem the days as vain Which did not battle-wounds sustain
kural.explanation: The hero will reckon among wasted days all those on which he had not received severe wounds
kural.couplet: The heroes, counting up their days, set down as vainEach day when they no glorious wound sustain

kural.Translation: Their anklets aloud jingle their name Who sacrifice their life for fame
kural.explanation: The fastening of ankle-ring by those who disire a world-wide renown and not (the safety of) their lives is like adorning (themselves)
kural.couplet: Who seek for world-wide fame, regardless of their life,The glorious clasp adorns, sign of heroic strife

kural.Translation: The king may chide, they pursue strife; They fear loss of glory; not life
kural.explanation: The heroes who are not afraid of losing their life in a contest will not cool their ardour, even if the king prohibits (their fighting)
kural.couplet: Fearless they rush where'er 'the tide of battle rolls';The king's reproof damps not the ardour of their eager souls

kural.Translation: Who will blame the heroes that lose Their lives in war to keep their vows?
kural.explanation: Who would reproach with failure those who seal their oath with their death ?
kural.couplet: Who says they err, and visits them scorn,Who die and faithful guard the vow they've sworn

kural.Translation: Such a death shall be prayed for Which draws the the tears of the ruler
kural.explanation: If (heroes) can so die as to fill with tears the eyes of their rulers, such a death deserves to be obtained even by begging
kural.couplet: If monarch's eyes o'erflow with tears for hero slain,Who would not beg such boon of glorious death to gain

kural.Translation: Like friendship what's so hard to gain? That guards one against acts villain?
kural.explanation: What so sure defence 'gainst all that foe can do?
kural.couplet: What so hard for men to gain as friendship trueWhat so sure defence 'gainst all that foe can do

kural.Translation: Good friendship shines like waxing moon, The bad withers like waning moon
kural.explanation: The friendship of the wise waxes like the new moon; (but) that of fools wanes like the full moon
kural.couplet: Friendship with men fulfilled of good Waxes like the crescent moon;Friendship with men of foolish mood, Like the full orb, waneth soon

kural.Translation: Like taste in books good friendship grows The more one moves the more he knows
kural.explanation: Like learning, the friendship of the noble, the more it is cultivated, the more delightful does it become
kural.couplet: Learned scroll the more you ponder, Sweeter grows the mental food;So the heart by use grows fonder, Bound in friendship with the good

kural.Translation: Not to laugh is friendship made But to hit when faults exceed
kural.explanation: Friendship is to be practised not for the purpose of laughing but for that of being beforehand in giving one another sharp rebukes in case of transgression
kural.couplet: Nor for laughter only friendship all the pleasant day,But for strokes of sharp reproving, when from right you stray

kural.Translation: No close living nor clasping grip Friendship's feeling heart's fellowship
kural.explanation: Living together and holding frequent intercourse are not necessary (for friendship); (mutual) understanding can alone create a claim for it
kural.couplet: Not association constant, not affection's token bind;'Tis the unison of feeling friends unites of kindred mind

kural.Translation: Friendship is not more smile on face It is the smiling heart's embrace
kural.explanation: The love that dwells (merely in the smiles of the face is not friendship; (but) that which dwells deep in the smiles of the heart is true friendship
kural.couplet: Not the face's smile of welcome shows the friend sincere,But the heart's rejoicing gladness when the friend is near

kural.Translation: From ruin friendship saves and shares The load of pain and right path shows
kural.explanation: (True) friendship turns aside from evil (ways) makes (him) walk in the (good) way, and, in case of loss if shares his sorrow (with him)
kural.couplet: Friendship from ruin saves, in way of virtue keeps;In troublous time, it weeps with him who weeps

kural.Translation: Friendship hastens help in mishaps Like hands picking up dress that slips
kural.explanation: (True) friendship hastens to the rescue of the afflicted (as readily) as the hand of one whose garment is loosened (before an assembly)
kural.couplet: As hand of him whose vesture slips away,Friendship at once the coming grief will stay

kural.Translation: Friendship is enthroned on the strength That always helps with utmost warmth
kural.explanation: Friendship may be said to be on its throne when it possesses the power of supporting one at all times and under all circumstances, (in the practice or virtue and wealth)
kural.couplet: And where is friendship's royal seat? In stable mind,Where friend in every time of need support may find

kural.Translation: \"Such we are and such they are!\" Ev'n this boast will friendship mar
kural.explanation: Though friends may praise one another saying, "He is so intimate with us, and we so much (with him)"; (still) such friendship will appear mean
kural.couplet: Mean is the friendship that men blazon forth,'He's thus to me' and 'such to him my worth'

kural.Translation: Than testless friendship nought is worse For contacts formed will scarcely cease
kural.explanation: As those who are of a friendly nature will not forsake (a friend) after once loving (him), there is no evil so great as contracting a friendship without due inquiry
kural.couplet: To make an untried man your friend is ruin sure;For friendship formed unbroken must endure

kural.Translation: Friendship made without frequent test Shall end in grief and death at last
kural.explanation: The friendship contracted by him who has not made repeated inquiry will in the end grieve (him) to death
kural.couplet: Alliance with the man you have not proved and proved again,In length of days will give you mortal pain

kural.Translation: Temper, descent, defects and kins Trace well and take companions
kural.explanation: Make friendship (with one) after ascertaining (his) character, birth, defects and the whole of one's relations
kural.couplet: Temper, descent, defects, associations freeFrom blame: know these, then let the man be friend to thee

kural.Translation: Take as good friend at any price The nobly born who shun disgrace
kural.explanation: The friendship of one who belongs to a (good) family and is afraid of (being charged with) guilt, is worth even purchasing
kural.couplet: Who, born of noble race, from guilt would shrink with shame,Pay any price so you as friend that man may claim

kural.Translation: Who make you weep and chide wrong trends And lead you right are worthy friends
kural.explanation: You should examine and secure the friendship of those who can speak so as to make you weep over a crime (before its commission) or rebuke you severely (after you have done it) and are able to teach
kural.couplet: Make them your chosen friend whose words repentance move,With power prescription's path to show, while evil they reprove

kural.Translation: Is there a test like misfortune A rod to measure out kinsmen?
kural.explanation: Even in ruin there is some good; (for) it is a rod by which one may measure fully (the affection of one's) relations
kural.couplet: Ruin itself one blessing lends:'Tis staff that measures out one's friends

kural.Translation: Keep off contacts with fools; that is The greatest gain so say the wise
kural.explanation: It is indead a gain for one to renounce the friendship of fools
kural.couplet: 'Tis gain to any man, the sages say,Friendship of fools to put away

kural.Translation: Off with thoughts that depress the heart Off with friends that in woe depart
kural.explanation: Do not think of things that discourage your mind, nor contract friendship with those who would forsake you in adversity
kural.couplet: Think not the thoughts that dwarf the soul; nor takeFor friends the men who friends in time of grief forsake

kural.Translation: Friends who betray at ruin's brink Burn our mind ev'n at death to think
kural.explanation: The very thought of the friendship of those who have deserted one at the approach of adversity will burn one's mind at the time of death
kural.couplet: Of friends deserting us on ruin's brink,'Tis torture e'en in life's last hour to think

kural.Translation: The blameless ones as friends embarace; Give something and give up the base
kural.explanation: Continue to enjoy the friendship of the pure; (but) renounce even with a gift, the friendship of those who do not agree (with the world)
kural.couplet: Cling to the friendship of the spotless one's; whate'er you payRenounce alliance with the men of evil way

kural.Translation: That friendship is good amity Which restrains not one's liberty
kural.explanation: Imtimate friendship is that which cannot in the least be injured by (things done through the) right (of longstanding intimacy)
kural.couplet: Familiarity is friendship's silent pact,That puts restraint on no familiar act

kural.Translation: Friendship's heart is freedom close; Wise men's duty is such to please
kural.explanation: The constituents of friendship are (things done through) the right of intimacy; to be pleased with such a right is the duty of the wise
kural.couplet: Familiar freedom friendship's very frame supplies;To be its savour sweet is duty of the wise

kural.Translation: Of long friendship what is the use Righteous freedom if men refuse?
kural.explanation: Of what avail is long-standing friendship, if friends do not admit as their own actions done through the right of intimacy ?
kural.couplet: When to familiar acts men kind response refuse,What fruit from ancient friendship's use

kural.Translation: Things done unasked by loving friends Please the wise as familiar trends!
kural.explanation: If friends, through the right of friendship, do (anything) without being asked, the wise will be pleased with them on account of its desirability
kural.couplet: When friends unbidden do familiar acts with loving heart,Friends take the kindly deed in friendly part

kural.Translation: Offence of friends feel it easy As folloy or close intimacy
kural.explanation: If friends should perform what is painful, understand that it is owing not only to ignorance, but also to the strong claims of intimacy
kural.couplet: Not folly merely, but familiar carelessness,Esteem it, when your friends cause you distress

kural.Translation: They forsake not but continue In friendship's bounds though loss ensue
kural.explanation: Those who stand within the limits (of true friendship) will not even in adversity give up the intimacy of long-standing friends
kural.couplet: Who stand within the bounds quit not, though loss impends,Association with the old familiar friends

kural.Translation: Comrades established in firm love Though ruin comes waive not their vow
kural.explanation: Those who have (long) stood in the path of affection will not give it up even if their friends cause (them) their ruin
kural.couplet: True friends, well versed in loving ways,Cease not to love, when friend their love betrays

kural.Translation: Fast friends who list not tales of ill Though wronged they say \"that day is well\"
kural.explanation: To those who understand that by which they should not listen to (tales about) the faults of their friends, that is a (profitable) day on which the latter may commit a fault
kural.couplet: In strength of friendship rare of friend's disgrace who will not hear,The day his friend offends will day of grace to him appear

kural.Translation: To love such friends the world desires Whose friendship has unbroken ties
kural.explanation: They will be loved by the world, who have not forsaken the friendship of those with whom they have kept up an unbroken long-standing intimacy
kural.couplet: Friendship of old and faithful friends,Who ne'er forsake, the world commends

kural.Translation: Even foes love for better ends Those who leave not long-standing friends
kural.explanation: Even enemies will love those who have never changed in their affection to their long-standingfriends
kural.couplet: Ill-wishers even wish them well, who guardFor ancient friends, their wonted kind regard

kural.Translation: Swallowing love of soulless men Had better wane than wax anon
kural.explanation: The decrease of friendship with those who look as if they would eat you up (through excess of love) while they are really destitute of goodness is far better than its increase
kural.couplet: Though evil men should all-absorbing friendship show,Their love had better die away than grow

kural.Translation: Who fawn in wealth and fail in dearth Gain or lose; such friends have no worth
kural.explanation: Of what avail is it to get or lose the friendship of those who love when there is gain and leave when there is none ?
kural.couplet: What though you gain or lose friendship of men of alien heart,Who when you thrive are friends, and when you fail depart

kural.Translation: Cunning friends who calculate  Are like thieves and whores wicked
kural.explanation: Friendship who calculate the profits (of their friendship), prostitutes who are bent on obtaining their gains, and thieves are (all) of the same character
kural.couplet: These are alike: the friends who ponder friendship's gainThose who accept whate'er you give, and all the plundering train

kural.Translation: Better be alone than trust in those That throw in field like faithless horse
kural.explanation: Solitude is more to be desired than the society of those who resemble the untrained horses which throw down (their riders) in the fields of battle
kural.couplet: A steed untrained will leave you in the tug of war;Than friends like that to dwell alone is better far

kural.Translation: Friends low and mean that give no help- Leave them is better than to keep
kural.explanation: It is far better to avoid that to contract the evil friendship of the base who cannot protect (their friends) even when appointed to do so
kural.couplet: 'Tis better not to gain than gain the friendship profitlessOf men of little minds, who succour fails when dangers press

kural.Translation: Million times the wise man's hate Is better than a fool intimate
kural.explanation: The hatred of the wise is ten-million times more profitable than the excessive intimacy of the fool
kural.couplet: Better ten million times incur the wise man's hate,Than form with foolish men a friendship intimate

kural.Translation: Ten-fold crore you gain from foes Than from friends who are vain laughers
kural.explanation: What comes from enemies is a hundred million times more profitable than what comes from the friendship of those who cause only laughter
kural.couplet: From foes ten million fold a greater good you gain,Than friendship yields that's formed with laughers vain

kural.Translation: Without a word those friends eschew Who spoil deeds which they can do
kural.explanation: Gradually abandon without revealing (beforehand) the friendship of those who pretend inability to carry out what they (really) could do
kural.couplet: Those men who make a grievous toil of what they doOn your behalf, their friendship silently eschew

kural.Translation: Even in dreams the tie is bad With those whose deed is far from word
kural.explanation: The friendship of those whose actions do not agree with their words will distress (one) even in (one's) dreams
kural.couplet: E'en in a dream the intercourse is bitternessWith men whose deeds are other than their words profess

kural.Translation: Keep aloof from those that smile At home and in public revile
kural.explanation: Avoid even the least approach to a contraction of friendship with those who would love you in private but ridicule you in public
kural.couplet: In anywise maintain not intercourse with those,Who in the house are friends, in hall are slandering foes

kural.Translation: The friendship by an enemy shown Is anvil in time, to strike you down
kural.explanation: The friendship of those who behave like friends without inward affection is a weapon that may be thrown when a favourable opportunity presents itself
kural.couplet: Anvil where thou shalt smitten be, when men occasion find,Is friendship's form without consenting mind

kural.Translation: Who pretend kinship but are not Their friendship's fickle like woman's heart
kural.explanation: The friendship of those who seem to be friends while they are not, will change like the love of women
kural.couplet: Friendship of those who seem our kin, but are not really kindWill change from hour to hour like woman's mind

kural.Translation: They may be vast in good studies But heartfelt-love is hard for foes
kural.explanation: Though (one's) enemies may have mastered many good books, it will be impossible for them to become truly loving at heart
kural.couplet: To heartfelt goodness men ignoble hardly may attain,Although abundant stores of goodly lore they gain

kural.Translation: Fear foes whose face has winning smiles Whose heart is full of cunning guiles
kural.explanation: One should fear the deceitful who smile sweetly with their face but never love with their heart
kural.couplet: 'Tis fitting you should dread dissemblers' guile,Whose hearts are bitter while their faces smile

kural.Translation: Do not trust in what they tell Whose mind with your mind goes ill
kural.explanation: In nothing whatever is it proper to rely on the words of those who do not love with their heart
kural.couplet: When minds are not in unison, 'its never; just,In any words men speak to put your trust

kural.Translation: The words of foes is quickly seen Though they speak like friends in fine
kural.explanation: Though (one's) foes may utter good things as though they were friends, once will at once understand (their evil, import)
kural.couplet: Though many goodly words they speak in friendly tone,The words of foes will speedily be known

kural.Translation: Trust not the humble words of foes Danger darts from bending bows
kural.explanation: Since the bending of the bow bespeaks evil, one should not accept (as good) the humiliating speeches of one's foes
kural.couplet: To pliant speech from hostile lips give thou no ear;'Tis pliant bow that show the deadly peril near

kural.Translation: Adoring hands of foes hide arms Their sobbing tears have lurking harms
kural.explanation: A weapon may be hid in the very hands with which (one's) foes adore (him) (and) the tears they shed are of the same nature
kural.couplet: In hands that worship weapon ten hidden lies;Such are the tears that fall from foeman's eyes

kural.Translation: In open who praise, at heart despise Cajole and crush them in friendly guise
kural.explanation: It is the duty of kings to affect great love but make it die (inwardly); as regard those foes who shew them great friendship but despise them (in their heart)
kural.couplet: 'Tis just, when men make much of you, and then despise,To make them smile, and slap in friendship's guise

kural.Translation: When foes, in time, play friendship's part Feign love on face but not in heart
kural.explanation: When one's foes begin to affect friendship, one should love them with one's looks, and, cherishing no love in the heart, give up (even the former)
kural.couplet: When time shall come that foes as friends appear,Then thou, to hide a hostile heart, a smiling face may'st wear

kural.Translation: This is folly's prominent vein To favour loss and forego gain
kural.explanation: Folly is one (of the chief defects); it is that which (makes one) incur loss and forego gain
kural.couplet: What one thing merits folly's special name.Letting gain go, loss for one's own to claim

kural.Translation: Folly of follies is to lead A lewd and lawless life so bad
kural.explanation: The greatest folly is that which leads one to take delight in doing what is forbidden
kural.couplet: 'Mid follies chiefest folly is to fix your loveOn deeds which to your station unbefitting prove

kural.Translation: Shameless, aimless, callous, listless Such are the marks of foolishness
kural.explanation: Shamelessness indifference (to what must be sought after), harshness, and aversion for everything (that ought to be desired) are the qualities of the fool
kural.couplet: Ashamed of nothing, searching nothing out, of loveless heart,Nought cherishing, 'tis thus the fool will play his part

kural.Translation: No fool equals the fool who learns Knows, teaches, but self-control spurns
kural.explanation: There are no greater fools than he who, though he has read and understood (a great deal) and even taught it to others, does not walk according to his own teaching
kural.couplet: The sacred law he reads and learns, to other men expounds,-Himself obeys not; where can greater fool be found

kural.Translation: The fool suffers seven fold hells In single birth of hellish ills
kural.explanation: A fool can procure in a single birth a hell into which he may enter and suffer through all the seven births
kural.couplet: The fool will merit hell in one brief life on earth,In which he entering sinks through sevenfold round of birth

kural.Translation: A know-nothing fool daring a deed Not only fails but feels fettered
kural.explanation: If the fool, who knows not how to act undertakes a work, he will (certainly) fail (But) is it all ? He will even adorn himself with fetters
kural.couplet: When fool some task attempts with uninstructed pains,It fails; nor that alone, himself he binds with chains

kural.Translation: Strangers feast and kinsmen fast  When fools mishandle fortunes vast
kural.explanation: If a fool happens to get an immense fortune, his neighbours will enjoy it while his relations starve
kural.couplet: When fools are blessed with fortune's bounteous store,Their foes feed full, their friends are prey to hunger sore

kural.Translation: Fools possessing something on hand Like dazed and drunken stupids stand
kural.explanation: A fool happening to possess something is like the intoxication of one who is (already) giddy
kural.couplet: When folly's hand grasps wealth's increase, 'twill beAs when a mad man raves in drunken glee

kural.Translation: Friendship with fools is highly sweet For without a groan we part
kural.explanation: The friendship between fools is exceedingly delightful (to each other): for at parting there will be
kural.couplet: Friendship of fools is very pleasant thing,Parting with them will leave behind no sting

kural.Translation: Entrance of fools where Savants meet Looks like couch trod by unclean feet
kural.explanation: The appearance of a fool in an assembly of the learned is like placing (one's) unwashed feet on a bed
kural.couplet: Like him who seeks his couch with unwashed feet,Is fool whose foot intrudes where wise men meet

kural.Translation: Want of wisdom is want of wants Want of aught else the world nev'r counts
kural.explanation: The want of wisdom is the greatest of all wants; but that of wealth the world will not regard as such
kural.couplet: Want of knowledge, 'mid all wants the sorest want we deem;Want of other things the world will not as want esteem

kural.Translation: When fool bestows with glee a gift It comes but by getter's merit
kural.explanation: (The cause of) a fool cheerfully giving (something) is nothing else but the receiver's merit (in a former birth)
kural.couplet: The gift of foolish man, with willing heart bestowed, is nought,But blessing by receiver's penance bought

kural.Translation: The self-torments of fools exceed Ev'n tortures of their foes indeed
kural.explanation: The suffering that fools inflict upon themselves is hardly possible even to foes
kural.couplet: With keener anguish foolish men their own hearts wring,Than aught that even malice of their foes can bring

kural.Translation: Stupidity is vanity That cries \"We have sagacity\"
kural.explanation: What is called want of wisdom is the vanity which says, "We are wise"
kural.couplet: What is stupidity? The arrogance that cries,'Behold, we claim the glory of the wise.'

kural.Translation: Feigning knowledge that one has not Leads to doubt ev'n that he has got
kural.explanation: Fools pretending to know what has not been read (by them) will rouse suspicion even as to what they have thoroughly mastered
kural.couplet: If men what they have never learned assume to know,Upon their real learning's power a doubt 'twill throw

kural.Translation: Fools their nakedness conceal And yet their glaring faults reveal
kural.explanation: Even to cover one's nakedness would be folly, if (one's) faults were not covered (by forsaking them)
kural.couplet: Fools are they who their nakedness conceal,And yet their faults unveiled reveal

kural.Translation: The fool that slights sacred counsels Upon himself great harm entails
kural.explanation: The fool who neglects precious counsel does, of his own accord, a great injury to himself
kural.couplet: From out his soul who lets the mystic teachings die,Entails upon himself abiding misery

kural.Translation: He listens not nor himself knows Plague is his life until it goes
kural.explanation: The fool will not perform (his duties) even when advised nor ascertain them himself; such a soul is a
kural.couplet: Advised, he heeds not; of himself knows nothing wise;This man's whole life is all one plague until he dies

kural.Translation: Sans Self-sight in vain one opens Sight To the blind who bet their sight as right
kural.explanation: One who would teach a fool will (simply) betray his folly; and the fool would (still) think himself "wise in his own conceit"
kural.couplet: That man is blind to eyes that will not see who knowledge shows;-The blind man still in his blind fashion knows

kural.Translation: To people's \"Yes\" who proffer \"No\" Deemed as ghouls on earth they go
kural.explanation: He who denies the existence of what the world believes in will be regarded as a demon on earth
kural.couplet: Who what the world affirms as false proclaim,O'er all the earth receive a demon's name

kural.Translation: Hatred is a plague that divides And rouses illwill on all sides
kural.explanation: The disease which fosters the evil of disunion among all creatures is termed hatred by the wise
kural.couplet: Hostility disunion's plague will bring,That evil quality, to every living thing

kural.Translation: Rouse not hatred and confusion Though foes provoke disunion
kural.explanation: Though disagreeable things may be done from (a feeling of) disunion, it is far better that nothing painful be done from (that of) hatred
kural.couplet: Though men disunion plan, and do thee much despite'Tis best no enmity to plan, nor evil deeds requite

kural.Translation: Shun the plague of enmity And win everlasting glory
kural.explanation: To rid one-self of the distressing dtsease of hatred will bestow (on one) a never-decreasing imperishable fame
kural.couplet: If enmity, that grievous plague, you shun,Endless undying praises shall be won

kural.Translation: Hate-the woe of woes destroy; Then joy of joys you can enjoy
kural.explanation: If hatred which is the greatest misery is destroyed, it will yield the greatest delight
kural.couplet: Joy of joys abundant grows,When malice dies that woe of woes

kural.Translation: Who can overcome them in glory That are free from enmity?
kural.explanation: Who indeed would think of conquering those who naturally shrink back from hatred ?
kural.couplet: If men from enmity can keep their spirits free,Who over them shall gain the victory

kural.Translation: His fall and ruin are quite near Who holds enmity sweet and dear
kural.explanation: Failure and ruin are not far from him who says it is sweet to excel in hatred
kural.couplet: The life of those who cherished enmity hold dear,To grievous fault and utter death is near

kural.Translation: They cannot see the supreme Truth Who hate and injure without ruth
kural.explanation: Who only know to work men woe, fulfilled of enmity
kural.couplet: The very truth that greatness gives their eyes can never see,Who only know to work men woe, fulfilled of enmity

kural.Translation: To turn from enmity is gain Fomenting it brings fast ruin
kural.explanation: Shrinking back from hatred will yield wealth; indulging in its increase will hasten ruin
kural.couplet: 'Tis gain to turn the soul from enmity;Ruin reigns where this hath mastery

kural.Translation: Fortune favours when hate recedes Hatred exceeding ruin breeds
kural.explanation: At the approach of wealth one will not think of hatred (but) to secure one's ruin, one will look to its increase
kural.couplet: Men think not hostile thought in fortune's favouring hour,They cherish enmity when in misfortune's power

kural.Translation: All evils come from enmity All goodness flow from amity
kural.explanation: All calamities are caused by hatred; but by the delight (of friendship) is caused the great wealth of good virtues
kural.couplet: From enmity do all afflictive evils flow;But friendliness doth wealth of kindly good bestow

kural.Translation: Turn from strife with foes too strong With the feeble for battle long
kural.explanation: Avoid offering resistance to the strong; (but) never fail to cherish enmity towards the weak
kural.couplet: With stronger than thyself, turn from the strife away;With weaker shun not, rather court the fray

kural.Translation: Loveless, aidless, powerless king Can he withstand an enemy strong?
kural.explanation: How can he who is unloving, destitute of powerful aids, and himself without strength overcome the might of his foe ?
kural.couplet: No kinsman's love, no strength of friends has he;How can he bear his foeman's enmity

kural.Translation: Unskilled, timid, miser, misfit He is easy for foes to hit
kural.explanation: In the estimation of foes miserably weak is he, who is timid, ignorant, unsociable and niggardly
kural.couplet: A craven thing! knows nought, accords with none, gives nought away;To wrath of any foe he falls an easy prey

kural.Translation: The wrathful restive man is prey To any, anywhere any day
kural.explanation: He who neither refrains from anger nor keeps his secrets will at all times and in all places be easily conquered by all
kural.couplet: His wrath still blazes, every secret told; each dayThis man's in every place to every foe an easy prey

kural.Translation: Crooked, cruel, tactless and base Any foe can fell him with ease
kural.explanation: (A) pleasing (object) to his foes is he who reads not moral works, does nothing that is enjoined by them cares not for reproach and is not possessed of good qualities
kural.couplet: No way of right he scans, no precepts bind, no crimes affright,No grace of good he owns; such man's his foes' delight

kural.Translation: Blind in rage and mad in lust To have his hatred is but just
kural.explanation: Highly to be desired is the hatred of him whose anger is blind, and whose lust increases beyond measure
kural.couplet: Blind in his rage, his lustful passions rage and swell;If such a man mislikes you, like it well

kural.Translation: Pay and buy his enmity Who muddles chance with oddity
kural.explanation: It is indeed necessary to obtain even by purchase the hatred of him who having begun (a work) does what is not conductive (to its accomplishment)
kural.couplet: Unseemly are his deeds, yet proffering aid, the man draws nigh:His hate- 'tis cheap at any price- be sure to buy

kural.Translation: With no virtue but full of vice He loses friends and delights foes
kural.explanation: He will become friendless who is without (any good) qualities and whose faults are many; (such a character) is a help to (his) foes
kural.couplet: No gracious gifts he owns, faults many cloud his fame;His foes rejoice, for none with kindred claim

kural.Translation: The joy of heroes knows no bounds When timid fools are opponents
kural.explanation: There will be no end of lofty delights to the victorious, if their foes are (both) ignorant and timid
kural.couplet: The joy of victory is never far removed from thoseWho've luck to meet with ignorant and timid foes

kural.Translation: Glory's light he will not gain Who fails to fight a fool and win
kural.explanation: The light (of fame) will never be gained by him who gains not the trifling reputation of having fought an unlearned (foe)
kural.couplet: The task of angry war with men unlearned in virtue's loreWho will not meet, glory shall meet him never more

kural.Translation: Let not one even as a sport The ill-natured enmity court
kural.explanation: The evil of hatred is not of a nature to be desired by one even in sport
kural.couplet: For Hate, that ill-conditioned thing not e'en in jestLet any evil longing rule your breast

kural.Translation: Incur the hate of bow-ploughers But not the hate of word-ploughers
kural.explanation: Though you may incur the hatred of warriors whose ploughs are bows, incur not that of ministers whose ploughs are words
kural.couplet: Although you hate incur of those whose ploughs are bows,Make not the men whose ploughs are words your foes

kural.Translation: Forlorn, who rouses many foes The worst insanity betrays
kural.explanation: He who being alone, incurs the hatred of many is more infatuated than even mad men
kural.couplet: Than men of mind diseased, a wretch more utterly forlorn,Is he who stands alone, object of many foeman's scorn

kural.Translation: This world goes safely in his grace Whose heart makes friends even of foes
kural.explanation: Whose worthy rule can change his foes to friends
kural.couplet: The world secure on his dexterity depends,Whose worthy rule can change his foes to friends

kural.Translation: Alone, if two foes you oppose Make one of them your ally close
kural.explanation: He who is alone and helpless while his foes are two should secure one of them as an agreeable help (to himself)
kural.couplet: Without ally, who fights with twofold enemy o'ermatched,Must render one of these a friend attached

kural.Translation: Trust or distrust; during distress Keep aloof; don't mix with foes
kural.explanation: Though (one's foe is) aware or not of one's misfortune one should act so as neither to join nor separate (from him)
kural.couplet: Whether you trust or not, in time of sore distress,Questions of diff'rence or agreement cease to press

kural.Translation: To those who know not, tell not your pain Nor your weakness to foes explain
kural.explanation: Relate not your suffering even to friends who are ignorant of it, nor refer to your weakness in the presence of your foes
kural.couplet: To those who know them not, complain not of your woes;Nor to your foeman's eyes infirmities disclose

kural.Translation: Know how and act and defend well The pride of enemies shall fall
kural.explanation: The joy of one's foes will be destroyed if one guards oneself by knowing the way (of acting) and securing assistance
kural.couplet: Know thou the way, then do thy part, thyself defend;Thus shall the pride of those that hate thee have an end

kural.Translation: Cut off thorn-trees when young they are; Grown hard, they cut your hands beware
kural.explanation: A thorny tree should be felled while young, (for) when it is grown it will destroy the hand of the feller
kural.couplet: Destroy the thorn, while tender point can work thee no offence;Matured by time, 'twill pierce the hand that plucks it thence

kural.Translation: To breathe on earth they are not fit Defying foes who don't defeat
kural.explanation: Those who do not destroy the pride of those who hate (them) will certainly not exist even to breathe
kural.couplet: But breathe upon them, and they surely die,Who fail to tame the pride of angry enemy

kural.Translation: Traitorous kinsmen will make you sad As water and shade do harm when bad
kural.explanation: Shade and water are not pleasant, (if) they cause disease; so are the qualities of (one's) relations not agreeable, (if) they cause pain
kural.couplet: Water and shade, if they unwholesome prove, will bring you painAnd qualities of friends who treacherous act, will be your bane

kural.Translation: You need not sword-like kinsmen fear Fear foes who feign as kinsmen dear
kural.explanation: Fear not foes (who say they would cut) like a sword; (but) fear the friendship of foes (who seemingly
kural.couplet: Dread not the foes that as drawn swords appear;Friendship of foes, who seem like kinsmen, fear

kural.Translation: The secret foe in days evil Will cut you, beware, like potters' steel
kural.explanation: Fear internal enmity and guard yourself; (if not) it will destroy (you) in an evil hour, as surely as the tool which cuts the potter's clay
kural.couplet: Of hidden hate beware, and guard thy life;In troublous time 'twill deeper wound than potter's knife

kural.Translation: The evil-minded foe within Foments trouble, spoils kinsmen!
kural.explanation: The secret enmity of a person whose mind in unreformed will lead to many evils causing disaffection among (one's) relations
kural.couplet: If secret enmities arise that minds pervert,Then even kin unkind will work thee grievous hurt

kural.Translation: A traitor among kinsmen will Bring life-endangering evil
kural.explanation: If there appears internal hatred in a (king's) family; it will lead to many a fatal crime
kural.couplet: Amid one's relatives if hidden hath arise,'Twill hurt inflict in deadly wise

kural.Translation: Discord in kings' circle entails Life-destroying deadly evils
kural.explanation: If hatred arises among (one's) own people, it will be hardly possible (for one) to escape death
kural.couplet: If discord finds a place midst those who dwelt at one before,'Tis ever hard to keep destruction from the door

kural.Translation: A house hiding hostiles in core Just seems on like the lid in jar
kural.explanation: Never indeed will a family subject to internal hatred unite (really) though it may present an apparent union like that of a casket and its lid
kural.couplet: As casket with its cover, though in one they live alway,No union to the house where hate concealed hath sway

kural.Translation: By secret spite the house wears out Like gold crumbling by file's contact
kural.explanation: A family subject to internal hatred will wear out and lose its strength like iron that has been filed away
kural.couplet: As gold with which the file contends is worn away,So strength of house declines where hate concealed hath sway

kural.Translation: Ruin lurks in enmity As slit in sesame though it be
kural.explanation: Although internal hatred be as small as the fragment of the sesamum (seed), still does destruction dwell in it
kural.couplet: Though slight as shred of 'seasame' seed it be,Destruction lurks in hidden enmity

kural.Translation: Dwell with traitors that hate in heart Is dwelling with snake in selfsame hut
kural.explanation: Living with those who do not agree (with one) is like dwelling with a cobra (in the same) hut
kural.couplet: Domestic life with those who don't agree,Is dwelling in a shed with snake for company

kural.Translation: Not to spite the mighty ones Safest safeguard to living brings
kural.explanation: Not to disregard the power of those who can carry out (their wishes) is more important than all the watchfulness of those who guard (themselves against evil)
kural.couplet: The chiefest care of those who guard themselves from ill,Is not to slight the powers of those who work their mighty will

kural.Translation: To walk unmindful of the great Shall great troubles ceaseless create
kural.explanation: To behave without respect for the great (rulers) will make them do (us) irremediable evils
kural.couplet: If men will lead their lives reckless of great men's will,Such life, through great men's powers, will bring perpetual ill

kural.Translation: Heed not and do, if ruin you want Offence against the mighty great
kural.explanation: If a person desires ruin, let him not listen to the righteous dictates of law, but commit crimes against those who are able to slay (other sovereigns)
kural.couplet: Who ruin covet let them shut their ears, and do despiteTo those who, where they list to ruin have the might

kural.Translation: The weak who insult men of might Death with their own hands invite
kural.explanation: The weak doing evil to the strong is like beckoning Yama to come (and destroy them)
kural.couplet: When powerless man 'gainst men of power will evil deeds essay,Tis beck'ning with the hand for Death to seize them for its prey

kural.Translation: Where can they go and thrive where Pursued by powerful monarch's ire?
kural.explanation: Those who have incurred the wrath of a cruel and mighty potentate will not prosper wherever they may go
kural.couplet: Who dare the fiery wrath of monarchs dread,Where'er they flee, are numbered with the dead

kural.Translation: One can escape in fire caught The great who offends escapes not
kural.explanation: Though burnt by a fire (from a forest), one may perhaps live; (but) never will he live who has shown disrespect to the great (devotees)
kural.couplet: Though in the conflagration caught, he may escape from thence:He 'scapes not who in life to great ones gives offence

kural.Translation: If holy mighty sages frown Stately gifts and stores who can own?
kural.explanation: If a king incurs the wrath of the righteous great, what will become of his government with its splendid auxiliaries and (all) its untold wealth ?
kural.couplet: Though every royal gift, and stores of wealth your life should crown,What are they, if the worthy men of mighty virtue frown

kural.Translation: When hill-like sages are held small The firm on earth lose home and all
kural.explanation: If (the) hill-like (devotees) resolve on destruction, those who seemed to be everlasting will be destroyed root and branch from the earth
kural.couplet: If they, whose virtues like a mountain rise, are light esteemed;They die from earth who, with their households, ever-during seemed

kural.Translation: Before the holy sage's rage Ev'n Indra's empire meets damage
kural.explanation: Kings even fall from high estate and perish in the flame
kural.couplet: When blazes forth the wrath of men of lofty fame,Kings even fall from high estate and perish in the flame

kural.Translation: Even mighty aided men shall quail If the enraged holy seers will
kural.explanation: Though in possession of numerous auxiliaries, they will perish who are-exposed to the wrath of the noble whose penance is boundless
kural.couplet: Though all-surpassing wealth of aid the boast,If men in glorious virtue great are wrath, they're lost

kural.Translation: Who dote on wives lose mighty gain That lust, dynamic men disdain
kural.explanation: Those who lust after their wives will not attain the excellence of virtue; and it is just this that is not desired by those who are bent on acquiring wealth
kural.couplet: Who give their soul to love of wife acquire not nobler gain;Who give their soul to strenuous deeds such meaner joys disdain

kural.Translation: Who dotes, unmanly, on his dame His wealth to him and all is shame
kural.explanation: The wealth of him who, regardless (of his manliness), devotes himself to his wife's feminine nature will cause great shame (to ali men) and to himself;
kural.couplet: Who gives himself to love of wife, careless of noble nameHis wealth will clothe him with o'erwhelming shame

kural.Translation: Who's servile to his wife always Shy he feels before the wise
kural.explanation: The frailty that stoops to a wife will always make (her husband) feel ashamed among the good
kural.couplet: Who to his wife submits, his strange, unmanly moodWill daily bring him shame among the good

kural.Translation: Fearing his wife salvationless The weaklings' action has no grace
kural.explanation: The undertaking of one, who fears his wife and is therefore destitute of (bliss), will never be applauded
kural.couplet: No glory crowns e'en manly actions wroughtBy him who dreads his wife, nor gives the other world a thought

kural.Translation: Who fears his wife fears always Good to do to the good and wise
kural.explanation: He that fears his wife will always be afraid of doing good deeds (even) to the good
kural.couplet: Who quakes before his wife will ever tremble too,Good deeds to men of good deserts to do

kural.Translation: Who fear douce arms of their wives Look petty even with god-like lives
kural.explanation: They that fear the bamboo-like shoulders of their wives will be destitute of manliness though they may flourish like the Gods
kural.couplet: Though, like the demi-gods, in bliss they dwell secure from harm,Those have no dignity who fear the housewife's slender arm

kural.Translation: Esteemed more is women bashful Than man servile unto her will
kural.explanation: Even shame faced womanhood is more to be esteemed than the shameless manhood that performs
kural.couplet: The dignity of modest womanhood excelsHis manliness, obedient to a woman's law who dwells

kural.Translation: By fair-browed wives who are governed Help no friends nor goodness tend
kural.explanation: Those who yield to the wishes of their wives will neither relieve the wants of (their) friends nor perform virtuous deeds
kural.couplet: Who to the will of her with beauteous brow their lives conform,Aid not their friends in need, nor acts of charity perform

kural.Translation: No virtue riches nor joy is seen In those who submit to women
kural.explanation: From those who obey the commands of their wives are to be expected neither deeds of virtue, nor those of wealth nor (even) those of pleasure
kural.couplet: No virtuous deed, no seemly wealth, no pleasure, restsWith them who live obedient to their wives' behests

kural.Translation: Thinkers strong and broad of heart By folly on fair sex do not dote
kural.explanation: The foolishness that results from devotion to a wife will never be found in those who possess a reflecting mind and a prosperity (flowing) therefrom
kural.couplet: Where pleasures of the mind, that dwell in realms of thought, abound,Folly, that springs from overweening woman's love, is never found

kural.Translation: For gold, not love their tongue cajoles Men are ruined by bangled belles
kural.explanation: The sweet words of elegant braceleted (prostitutes) who desire (a man) not from affection but from avarice, will cause sorrow
kural.couplet: Those that choice armlets wear who seek not thee with love,But seek thy wealth, their pleasant words will ruin prove

kural.Translation: Avoid ill-natured whores who feign Love only for their selfish gain
kural.explanation: One must ascertain the character of the ill-natured women who after ascertaining the wealth (of a man) speak (as if they were) good natured-ones, and avoid intercourse (with them)
kural.couplet: Who weigh the gain, and utter virtuous words with vicious heart,Weighing such women's worth, from their society depart

kural.Translation: The false embrace of whores is like That of a damned corpse in the dark
kural.explanation: The false embraces of wealth-loving women are like (hired men) embracing a strange corpse in a dark room
kural.couplet: As one in darkened room, some stranger corpse inarms,Is he who seeks delight in mercenary women's charms

kural.Translation: The wise who seek the wealth of grace Look not for harlots' low embrace
kural.explanation: The wise who seek the wealth of grace will not desire the base favours of those who regard wealth (and not pleasure) as (their) riches
kural.couplet: Their worthless charms, whose only weal is wealth of gain,From touch of these the wise, who seek the wealth of grace, abstain

kural.Translation: The lofty wise will never covet The open charms of a vile harlot
kural.explanation: Those whose knowledge is made excellent by their (natural) sense will not covet the trffling delights
kural.couplet: From contact with their worthless charms, whose charms to all are free,The men with sense of good and lofty wisdom blest will flee;

kural.Translation: Those who guard their worthy fame Shun the wanton's vaunting charm
kural.explanation: Those who would spread (the fame of) their own goodness will not desire the shoulders of those,who rejoice in their accomplishments and bestow their despicable favours (on all who pay)
kural.couplet: From touch of those who worthless charms, with wanton arts, display,The men who would their own true good maintain will turn away

kural.Translation: Hollow hearts alone desire The arms of whores with hearts elsewere
kural.explanation: Those who are destitute of a perfectly (reformed) mind will covet the shoulders of those who embrace (them) while their hearts covet other things
kural.couplet: Who cherish alien thoughts while folding in their feigned embrace,These none approach save those devoid of virtue's grace

kural.Translation: Senseless fools are lured away By arms of sirens who lead astray
kural.explanation: The wise say that to such as are destitute of discerning sense the embraces of faithless women are (as ruinous as those of) the celestail female
kural.couplet: As demoness who lures to ruin woman's treacherous loveTo men devoid of wisdom's searching power will prove

kural.Translation: The soft jewelled arms of whores are hell Into which the degraded fall
kural.explanation: The delicate shoulders of prostitutes with excellent jewels are a hell into which are plunged the ignorant base
kural.couplet: The wanton's tender arm, with gleaming jewels decked,Is hell, where sink degraded souls of men abject

kural.Translation: Double-minded whores, wine and dice Are lures of those whom fortune flies
kural.explanation: Treacherous women, liquor, and gambling are the associates of such as have forsaken by Fortune
kural.couplet: Women of double minds, strong drink, and dice; to these giv'n o'er,Are those on whom the light of Fortune shines no more

kural.Translation: Foes fear not who for toddy craze The addicts daily their glory lose
kural.explanation: Those who always thirst after drink will neither inspire fear (in others) nor retain the light (of their fame)
kural.couplet: Who love the palm's intoxicating juice, each day,No rev'rence they command, their glory fades away

kural.Translation: Drink not liquor; but let them drink Whom with esteem the wise won't think
kural.explanation: Let no liquor be drunk; if it is desired, let it be drunk by those who care not for esteem of the great
kural.couplet: Drink not inebriating draught Let him count well the costWho drinks, by drinking, all good men's esteem is lost

kural.Translation: The drunkard's joy pains ev'n mother's face How vile must it look for the wise?
kural.explanation: Intoxication is painful even in the presence of (one's) mother; what will it not then be in that of the wise ?
kural.couplet: The drunkard's joy is sorrow to his mother's eyes;What must it be in presence of the truly wise

kural.Translation: Good shame turns back from him ashamed Who is guilty of wine condemned
kural.explanation: The fair maid of modesty will turn her back on those who are guilty of the great and abominable crime of drunkenness
kural.couplet: Shame, goodly maid, will turn her back for aye on themWho sin the drunkard's grievous sin, that all condemn

kural.Translation: To pay and drink and lose the sense Is nothing but rank ignorance
kural.explanation: To give money and purchase unconsciousness is the result of one's ignorance of (one's own actions)
kural.couplet: With gift of goods who self-oblivion buys,Is ignorant of all that man should prize

kural.Translation: They take poison who take toddy And doze ev'n like a dead body
kural.explanation: They that sleep resemble the deed; (likewise) they that drink are no other than poison-eaters
kural.couplet: Sleepers are as the dead, no otherwise they seem;Who drink intoxicating draughts, they poison quaff, we deem

kural.Translation: The secret drunkards' senses off Make the prying public laugh
kural.explanation: Those who always intoxicate themselves by a private (indulgence in) drink; will have their secrets detected and laughed at by their fellow-townsmen
kural.couplet: Who turn aside to drink, and droop their heavy eye,Shall be their townsmen's jest, when they the fault espy

kural.Translation: Don't say I'm not a drunkard hard The hidden fraud is known abroad
kural.explanation: Let (the drunkard) give up saying "I have never drunk"; (for) the moment (he drinks) he will simply betray his former attempt to conceal
kural.couplet: No more in secret drink, and then deny thy hidden fraud;What in thy mind lies hid shall soon be known abroad

kural.Translation: Can torch search one in water sunk?  Can reason reach the raving drunk?
