kural.explanation: Reasoning with a drunkard is like going under water with a torch in search of a drowned man
kural.couplet: Like him who, lamp in hand, would seek one sunk beneath the waveIs he who strives to sober drunken man with reasonings grave

kural.Translation: The sober seeing the drunkard's plight On selves can't they feel same effect?
kural.explanation: When (a drunkard) who is sober sees one who is not, it looks as if he remembered not the evil effects of his (own) drink
kural.couplet: When one, in sober interval, a drunken man espies,Does he not think, 'Such is my folly in my revelries'

kural.Translation: Avoid gambling, albeit you win Gulping bait-hook what does fish gain?
kural.explanation: Though able to win, let not one desire gambling; (for) even what is won is like a fish swallowing the iron in fish-hook
kural.couplet: Seek not the gamester's play; though you should win,Your gain is as the baited hook the fish takes in

kural.Translation: Can gamblers in life good obtain Who lose a hundred one to gain?
kural.explanation: That they may good obtain, and see a prosperous day? Is there indeed a means of livelihood that can bestow happiness on gamblers who gain one and lose a hundred?
kural.couplet: Is there for gamblers, too, that gaining one a hundred lose, some wayThat they may good obtain, and see a prosperous day

kural.Translation: If kings indulge in casting dice All their fortune will flow to foes
kural.explanation: If the king is incessantly addicted to the rolling dice in the hope of gain, his wealth and the resources thereof will take their departure and fall into other's hands
kural.couplet: If prince unceasing speak of nought but play,Treasure and revenue will pass from him away

kural.Translation: Nothing will make you poor like game Which adds to woes and ruins fame
kural.explanation: There is nothing else that brings (us) poverty like gambling which causes many a misery and destroys (one's) reputation
kural.couplet: Gaming brings many woes, and ruins fair renown;Nothing to want brings men so surely down

kural.Translation: The game, game-hall and gambler's art Who sought with glee have come to nought
kural.explanation: Penniless are those who by reason of their attachment would never forsake gambling, the gamblingplace and the handling (of dice)
kural.couplet: The dice, and gaming-hall, and gamester's art, they eager sought,Thirsting for gain- the men in other days who came to nought

kural.Translation: Men swallowed by the ogress, dice Suffer grief and want by that vice
kural.explanation: Those who are swallowed by the goddess called "gambling" will never have their hunger satisfied, but suffer the pangs of hell in the next world
kural.couplet: Gambling's Misfortune's other name: o'er whom she casts her veil,They suffer grievous want, and sorrows sore bewail

kural.Translation: If men their time in game-den spend Ancestral wealth and virtues end
kural.explanation: To waste time at the place of gambling will destroy inherited wealth and goodness of character
kural.couplet: Ancestral wealth and noble fame to ruin haste,If men in gambler's halls their precious moments waste

kural.Translation: Game ruins wealth and spoils grace Leads to lies and wretched woes
kural.explanation: Gambling destroys property, teaches falsehood, puts an end to benevolence, and brings in misery (here and hereafter)
kural.couplet: Gambling wastes wealth, to falsehood bends the soul: it drives awayAll grace, and leaves the man to utter misery a prey

kural.Translation: Dress, wealth, food, fame, learning-these five In gambler's hand will never thrive
kural.explanation: The habit of gambling prevents the attainment of these five: clothing, wealth, food, fame and learning
kural.couplet: Clothes, wealth, food, praise, and learning, all departFrom him on gambler's gain who sets his heart

kural.Translation: Love for game grows with every loss As love for life with sorrows grows
kural.explanation: As the gambler loves (his vice) the more he loses by it, so does the soul love (the body) the more it suffers through it
kural.couplet: Howe'er he lose, the gambler's heart is ever in the play;E'en so the soul, despite its griefs, would live on earth alway

kural.Translation: Wind, bile and phlegm three cause disease So doctors deem it more or less
kural.explanation: If (food and work are either) excessive or deficient, the three things enumerated by (medical) writers, flatulence, biliousness, and phlegm, will cause (one) disease
kural.couplet: The learned books count three, with wind as first; of these,As any one prevail, or fail; 'twill cause disease

kural.Translation: After digestion one who feeds His body no medicine needs
kural.explanation: No medicine is necessary for him who eats after assuring (himself) that what he has (already) eaten has been digested
kural.couplet: No need of medicine to heal your body's pain,If, what you ate before digested well, you eat again

kural.Translation: Eat food to digestive measure Life in body lasts with pleasure
kural.explanation: If (one's food has been) digested let one eat with moderation; (for) that is the way to prolong the life of an embodied soul
kural.couplet: Who has a body gained may long the gift retain,If, food digested well, in measure due he eat again

kural.Translation: Know digestion; with keen appetite Eat what is suitable and right
kural.explanation: (First) assure yourself that your food has been digested and never fail to eat, when very hungry, whatever is not disagreeable (to you)
kural.couplet: Knowing the food digested well, when hunger prompteth thee,With constant care, the viands choose that well agree

kural.Translation: With fasting adjusted food right Cures ills of life and makes you bright
kural.explanation: There will be no disaster to one's life if one eats with moderation, food that is not disagreeable
kural.couplet: With self-denial take the well-selected meal;So shall thy frame no sudden sickness feel

kural.Translation: Who eats with clean stomach gets health With greedy glutton abides ill-health
kural.explanation: As pleasure dwells with him who eats moderately, so disease (dwells) with the glutton who eats voraciously
kural.couplet: On modest temperance as pleasures pure,So pain attends the greedy epicure

kural.Translation: who glut beyond the hunger's fire Suffer from untold diseases here
kural.explanation: He will be afflicted with numberless diseases, who eats immoderately, ignorant (of the rules of health)
kural.couplet: Who largely feeds, nor measure of the fire within maintains,That thoughtless man shall feel unmeasured pains

kural.Translation: Test disease, its cause and cure And apply remedy that is sure
kural.explanation: Let the physician enquire into the (nature of the) disease, its cause and its method of cure and treat it faithfully according to (medical rule)
kural.couplet: Disease, its cause, what may abate the ill:Let leech examine these, then use his skill

kural.Translation: Let the skilful doctor note The sickmen, sickness, season and treat
kural.explanation: The learned (physician) should ascertain the condition of his patient; the nature of his disease, and the season (of the year) and (then) proceed (with his treatment)
kural.couplet: The habitudes of patient and disease, the crises of the illThese must the learned leech think over well, then use his skill

kural.Translation: Patient, doctor, medicine and nurse Are four-fold codes of treating course
kural.explanation: Medical science consists of four parts, viz, patient, physician, medicine and compounder; and each of these (again) contains four sub-divisions
kural.couplet: For patient, leech, and remedies, and him who waits by patient's side,The art of medicine must fourfold code of laws provide

kural.Translation: Right-sense and bashfulness adorn By nature only the noble-born
kural.explanation: Consistency (of thought, word and deed) and fear (of sin) are conjointly natural only to the high-born
kural.couplet: Save in the scions of a noble house, you never findInstinctive sense of right and virtuous shame combined

kural.Translation: The noble-born lack not these three: Good conduct, truth and modesty
kural.explanation: The high-born will never deviate from these three; good manners, truthfulness and modesty
kural.couplet: In these three things the men of noble birth fail not:In virtuous deed and truthful word, and chastened thought

kural.Translation: Smile, gift, sweet words and courtesy These four mark true nobility
kural.explanation: A cheerful countenance, liberality, pleasant words, and an unreviling disposition, these four are said to be the proper qualities of the truly high-born
kural.couplet: The smile, the gift, the pleasant word, unfailing courtesyThese are the signs, they say, of true nobility

kural.Translation: Even for crores, the noble mood Cannot bend to degrading deed
kural.explanation: Though blessed with immense wealth, the noble will never do anything unbecoming
kural.couplet: Millions on millions piled would never winThe men of noble race to soul-degrading sin

kural.Translation: The means of gift may dwindle; yet Ancient homes guard their noble trait
kural.explanation: Though their means fall off, those born in ancient families, will not lose their character (for liberality)
kural.couplet: Though stores for charity should fail within, the ancient raceWill never lose its old ancestral grace

kural.Translation: Who guard their family prestige pure Stoop not to acts of cunning lure
kural.explanation: Those who seek to preserve the irreproachable honour of their families will not viciously do what is detrimental thereto
kural.couplet: Whose minds are set to live as fits their sire's unspotted fame,Stooping to low deceit, commit no deeds that gender shame

kural.Translation: The faults of nobly-born are seen Like on the sky the spots of moon
kural.explanation: As spots on her bright orb that walks sublime the evening sky
kural.couplet: The faults of men of noble race are seen by every eye,As spots on her bright orb that walks sublime the evening sky

kural.Translation: If manners of the good are rude People deem their pedigree crude
kural.explanation: If one of a good family betrays want of affection, his descent from it will be called in question
kural.couplet: If lack of love appear in those who bear some goodly name,'Twill make men doubt the ancestry they claim

kural.Translation: Soil's nature is seen in sprout The worth of birth from words flow out
kural.explanation: As the sprout indicates the nature of the soil, (so) the speech of the noble indicates (that of one's birth)
kural.couplet: Of soil the plants that spring thereout will show the worth:The words they speak declare the men of noble birth

kural.Translation: All gain good name by modesty Nobility by humility
kural.explanation: He who desires a good name must desire modesty; and he who desires (the continuance of) a family greatness must be submissive to all
kural.couplet: Who seek for good the grace of virtuous shame must know;Who seek for noble name to all must reverence show

kural.Translation: Though needed for your life in main, From mean degrading acts refrain
kural.explanation: Actions that would degrade (one's) family should not be done; though they may be so important that not doing them would end in death
kural.couplet: Though linked to splendours man no otherwise may gain,Reject each act that may thine honour's clearness stain

kural.Translation: Who seek honour and manly fame Don't do mean deeds even for name
kural.explanation: Those who desire (to maintain their) honour, will surely do nothing dishonourable, even for the sake of fame
kural.couplet: Who seek with glory to combine honour's untarnished fame,Do no inglorious deeds, though men accord them glory's name

kural.Translation: Be humble in prosperity In decline uphold dignity
kural.explanation: In great prosperity humility is becoming; dignity, in great adversity
kural.couplet: Bow down thy soul, with increase blest, in happy hour;Lift up thy heart, when stript of all by fortune's power

kural.Translation: Like hair fallen from head are those Who fall down from their high status
kural.explanation: They who have fallen from their (high) position are like the hair which has fallen from the head
kural.couplet: Like hairs from off the head that fall to earth,When fall'n from high estate are men of noble birth

kural.Translation: Even hill-like men will sink to nought With abrus-grain-like small default
kural.explanation: Even those who are exalted like a hill will be thought low, if they commit deeds that are debasing
kural.couplet: If meanness, slight as 'abrus' grain, by men be wrought,Though like a hill their high estate, they sink to nought

kural.Translation: Why fawn on men that scorn you here It yields no fame, heaven's bliss neither
kural.explanation: Why follow men who scorn, and at their bidding wait?
kural.couplet: It yields no praise, nor to the land of Gods throws wide the gate:Why follow men who scorn, and at their bidding wait

kural.Translation: Better it is to die forlorn Than live as slaves of those who scorn
kural.explanation: It is better for a man to be said of him that he died in his usual state than that he eked out his life by following those who disgraced him
kural.couplet: Better 'twere said, 'He's perished!' than to gainThe means to live, following in foeman's train

kural.Translation: Is nursing body nectar sweet Even when one's honour is lost?
kural.explanation: For the high-born to keep their body in life when their honour is gone will certainly not prove a remedy against death
kural.couplet: When high estate has lost its pride of honour meet,Is life, that nurses this poor flesh, as nectar sweet

kural.Translation: Honour lost, the noble expire Like a yak that loses its hair
kural.explanation: Those who give up (their) life when (their) honour is at stake are like the yark which kills itself at the loss of (even one of) its hairs
kural.couplet: Like the wild ox that, of its tuft bereft, will pine away,Are those who, of their honour shorn, will quit the light of day

kural.Translation: Their light the world adores and hails  Who will not live when honour fails
kural.explanation: The world will (always) praise and adore the fame of the honourable who would rather die than suffer indignity
kural.couplet: Who, when dishonour comes, refuse to live, their honoured memoryWill live in worship and applause of all the world for aye

kural.Translation: A heart of courage lives in light  Devoid of that one's life is night
kural.explanation: One's light is the abundance of one's courage; one's darkness is the desire to live destitute of such (a state of mind.)
kural.couplet: The light of life is mental energy; disgrace is hisWho says, 'I 'ill lead a happy life devoid of this.'

kural.Translation: All beings are the same in birth But work decides their varied worth
kural.explanation: All human beings agree as regards their birth but differ as regards their characteristics, because of the different qualities of their actions
kural.couplet: All men that live are one in circumstances of birth;Diversities of works give each his special worth

kural.Translation: Ignoble high not high they are The noble low not low they fare
kural.explanation: Though (raised) above, the base cannot become great; though (brought) low, the great cannot become base
kural.couplet: The men of lofty line, whose souls are mean, are never greatThe men of lowly birth, when high of soul, are not of low estate

kural.Translation: Greatness like woman's chastity Is guarded by self-varacity
kural.explanation: Exists while to itself is true
kural.couplet: Like single-hearted women, greatness too,Exists while to itself is true

kural.Translation: Great souls when their will is active Do mighty deeds rare to achieve
kural.explanation: (Though reduced) the great will be able to perform, in the proper way, deeds difficult (for others to do)
kural.couplet: The man endowed with greatness true,Rare deeds in perfect wise will do

kural.Translation: The petty-natured ones have not The mind to seek and befriend the great
kural.explanation: It is never in the nature of the base to seek the society of the great and partake of their nature
kural.couplet: 'As votaries of the truly great we will ourselves enroll,'Is thought that enters not the mind of men of little soul

kural.Translation: The base with power and opulence Wax with deeds of insolence
kural.explanation: Even nobility of birth, wealth and learning, if in (the possession of) the base, will (only) produce everincreasing pride
kural.couplet: Whene'er distinction lights on some unworthy head,Then deeds of haughty insolence are bred

kural.Translation: Greatness bends with modesty Meanness vaunts with vanity
kural.explanation: The great will always humble himself; but the mean will exalt himself in self-admiration
kural.couplet: Greatness humbly bends, but littleness alwaysSpreads out its plumes, and loads itself with praise

kural.Translation: Greatness is free from insolence Littleness swells with that offence
kural.explanation: Freedom from conceit is (the nature of true) greatness; (while) obstinacy therein is (that of) meanness
kural.couplet: Greatness is absence of conceit; meanness, we deem,Riding on car of vanity supreme

kural.Translation: Weakness of others greatness screens Smallness defects alone proclaims
kural.explanation: The great hide the faults of others; the base only divulge them
kural.couplet: Greatness will hide a neighbour's shame;Meanness his faults to all the world proclaim

kural.Translation: All goodness is duty to them  Who are dutiful and sublime
kural.explanation: It is said that those who are conscious of their duty and behave with a perfect goodness will regard as natural all that is good
kural.couplet: All goodly things are duties to the men, they sayWho set themselves to walk in virtue's perfect way

kural.Translation: Good in the great is character Than that there is nothing better
kural.explanation: The only delight of the perfect is that of their goodness; all other (sensual) delights are not to be included among any (true) delights
kural.couplet: The good of inward excellence they claim,The perfect men; all other good is only good in name

kural.Translation: Love, truth, regard, modesty, grace These five are virtue's resting place
kural.explanation: Affection, fear (of sin), benevolence, favour and truthfulness; these are the five pillars on which perfect goodness rests
kural.couplet: Love, modesty, beneficence, benignant grace,With truth, are pillars five of perfect virtue's resting-place

kural.Translation: Not to kill is penance pure Not to slander virtue sure
kural.explanation: Penance consists in the goodness that kills not , and perfection in the goodness that tells not others' faults
kural.couplet: The type of 'penitence' is virtuous good that nothing slays;To speak no ill of other men is perfect virtue's praise

kural.Translation: Humility is valour's strength A force that averts foes at length
kural.explanation: Stooping (to inferiors) is the strength of those who can accomplish (an undertaking); and that is the weapon with which the great avert their foes
kural.couplet: Submission is the might of men of mighty acts; the sageWith that same weapon stills his foeman's rage

kural.Translation: To bear repulse e'en from the mean Is the touch-stone of worthy men
kural.explanation: The touch-stone of perfection is to receive a defeat even at the hands of one's inferiors
kural.couplet: What is perfection's test? The equal mindTo bear repulse from even meaner men resigned

kural.Translation: Of perfection what is the gain If it returns not joy for pain?
kural.explanation: Of what avail is perfect goodness if it cannot do pleasing things even to those who have pained (it) ?
kural.couplet: What fruit doth your perfection yield you, say!Unless to men who work you ill good repay

kural.Translation: No shame there is in poverty To one strong in good quality
kural.explanation: Poverty is no disgrace to one who abounds in good qualities
kural.couplet: To soul with perfect virtue's strength endued,Brings no disgrace the lack of every earthly good

kural.Translation: Aeons may change but not the seer Who is a sea of virtue pure
kural.explanation: Those who are said to be the shore of the sea of perfection will never change, though ages may change
kural.couplet: Call them of perfect virtue's sea the shore,Who, though the fates should fail, fail not for evermore

kural.Translation: The world will not more bear its weight If from high virtue fall the great
kural.explanation: If there is a defect in the character of the perfect, (even) the great world cannot bear (its) burden
kural.couplet: The mighty earth its burthen to sustain must cease,If perfect virtue of the perfect men decrease

kural.Translation: To the polite free of access Easily comes courteousness
kural.explanation: If one is easy of access to all, it will be easy for one to obtain the virtue called goodness
kural.couplet: Who easy access give to every man, they say,Of kindly courtesy will learn with ease the way

kural.Translation: Humanity and noble birth Develop courtesy and moral worth
kural.explanation: Affectionateness and birth in a good family, these two constitute what is called a proper behaviour to all
kural.couplet: Benevolence and high born dignity,These two are beaten paths of courtesy

kural.Translation: Likeness in limbs is not likeness It's likeness in kind courteousness
kural.explanation: Resemblance of bodies is no resemblance of souls; true resemblance is the resemblance of qualities that attract
kural.couplet: Men are not one because their members seem alike to outward view;Similitude of kindred quality makes likeness true

kural.Translation: The world applauds those helpful men Whose actions are just and benign
kural.explanation: The world applauds the character of those whose usefulness results from their equity and charity
kural.couplet: Of men of fruitful life, who kindly benefits dispense,The world unites to praise the 'noble excellence.'

kural.Translation: The courteous don't even foes detest For contempt offends even in jest
kural.explanation: Reproach is painful to one even in sport; those (therefore) who know the nature of others exhibit (pleasing) qualities even when they are hated
kural.couplet: Contempt is evil though in sport They who man's nature know,E'en in their wrath, a courteous mind will show

kural.Translation: The world rests with the mannered best Or it crumbles and falls to dust
kural.explanation: The (way of the) world subsists by contact with the good; if not, it would bury itself in the earth and perish
kural.couplet: The world abides; for 'worthy' men its weight sustainWere it not so, 'twould fall to dust again

kural.Translation: The mannerless though sharp like file Are like wooden blocks indocile
kural.explanation: He who is destitute of (true) human qualities (only) resembles a tree, though he may possess the sharpness of a file
kural.couplet: Though sharp their wit as file, as blocks they must remain,Whose souls are void of 'courtesy humane'

kural.Translation: Discourtesy is mean indeed E'en to a base unfriendly breed
kural.explanation: It is wrong (for the wise) not to exhibit (good) qualities even towards those who bearing no friendship (for them) do only what is hateful
kural.couplet: Though men with all unfriendly acts and wrongs assail,'Tis uttermost disgrace in 'courtesy' to fail

kural.Translation: To those bereft of smiling light Even in day the earth is night
kural.explanation: To those who cannot rejoice, the wide world is buried darkness even in (broad) day light
kural.couplet: To him who knows not how to smile in kindly mirth,Darkness in daytime broods o'er all the vast and mighty earth

kural.Translation: The wealth heaped by the churlish base Is pure milk soured by impure vase
kural.explanation: The great wealth obtained by one who has no goodness will perish like pure milk spoilt by the
kural.couplet: Like sweet milk soured because in filthy vessel poured,Is ample wealth in churlish man's unopened coffers stored

kural.Translation: Dead is he with wealth in pile Unenjoyed, it is futile
kural.explanation: He who does not enjoy the immense riches he has heaped up in his house, is (to be reckoned as) dead, (for) there is nothing achieved (by him)
kural.couplet: Who fills his house with ample store, enjoying none,Is dead Nought with the useless heap is done

kural.Translation: The niggard miser thinks wealth is all He hoards, gives not is born devil
kural.explanation: He who knows that wealth yields every pleasure and yet is so blind as to lead miserly life will be born a demon
kural.couplet: Who giving nought, opines from wealth all blessing springs,Degraded birth that doting miser's folly brings

kural.Translation: A burden he is to earth indeed Who hoards without a worthy deed
kural.explanation: A burden to the earth are men bent on the acquisition of riches and not (true) fame
kural.couplet: Who lust to heap up wealth, but glory hold not dear,It burthens earth when on the stage of being they appear

kural.Translation: What legacy can he leave behind Who is for approach too unkind
kural.explanation: What will the miser who is not liked (by any one) regard as his own (in the world to come) ?
kural.couplet: Whom no one loves, when he shall pass away,What doth he look to leave behind, I pray

kural.Translation: What is the good of crores they hoard To give and enjoy whose heart is hard
kural.explanation: Those who neither give (to others) nor enjoy (their property) are (truly) destitute, though possessing immense riches
kural.couplet: Amid accumulated millions they are poor,Who nothing give and nought enjoy of all they store

kural.Translation: Great wealth unused for oneself nor To worthy men is but a slur
kural.explanation: He who enjoys not (his riches) nor relieves the wants of the worthy is a disease to his wealth
kural.couplet: Their ample wealth is misery to men of churlish heart,Who nought themselves enjoy, and nought to worthy men impart

kural.Translation: Who loaths to help have-nots, his gold Is like a spinster-belle grown old
kural.explanation: The wealth of him who never bestows anything on the destitute is like a woman of beauty growing old without a husband
kural.couplet: Like woman fair in lonelihood who aged grows,Is wealth of him on needy men who nought bestows

kural.Translation: The idle wealth of unsought men Is poison-fruit-tree amidst a town
kural.explanation: The wealth of him who is disliked (by all) is like the fruit-bearing of the etty tree in the midst of a town
kural.couplet: When he whom no man loves exults in great prosperity,'Tis as when fruits in midmost of the town some poisonous tree

kural.Translation: Others usurp the shining gold In loveless, stingy, vicious hold
kural.explanation: To heap up glittering wealth, their hoards shall others take
kural.couplet: Who love abandon, self-afflict, and virtue's way forsakeTo heap up glittering wealth, their hoards shall others take

kural.Translation: The brief want of the rich benign Is like rainclouds growing thin
kural.explanation: The short-lived poverty of those who are noble and rich is like the clouds becoming poor (for a while)
kural.couplet: 'Tis as when rain cloud in the heaven grows day,When generous wealthy man endures brief poverty

kural.Translation: To shrink from evil deed is shame The rest is blush of fair-faced dame
kural.explanation: True modesty is the fear of (evil) deeds; all other modesty is (simply) the bashfulness of virtuous maids
kural.couplet: To shrink abashed from evil deed is 'generous shame';Other is that of bright-browed one of virtuous fame

kural.Translation: Food, dress and such are one for all Modesty marks the higher soul
kural.explanation: Food, clothing and the like are common to all men but modesty is peculiar to the good
kural.couplet: Food, clothing, and other things alike all beings own;By sense of shame the excellence of men is known

kural.Translation: All lives have their lodge in flesh Perfection has its home in blush
kural.explanation: As the body is the abode of the spirit, so the excellence of modesty is the abode of perfection
kural.couplet: All spirits homes of flesh as habitation claim,And perfect virtue ever dwells with shame

kural.Translation: Shame is the jewel of dignity Shameless swagger is vanity
kural.explanation: Is not the modesty ornament of the noble ? Without it, their haughtiness would be a pain (to others)
kural.couplet: And is not shame an ornament to men of dignity?Without it step of stately pride is piteous thing to see

kural.Translation: In them resides the sense of shame Who blush for their and other's blame
kural.explanation: The world regards as the abode of modesty him who fear his own and other's guilt
kural.couplet: As home of virtuous shame by all the world the men are known,Who feel ashamed for others, guilt as for their own

kural.Translation: The great refuse the wonder-world Without modesty's hedge and shield
kural.explanation: The great make modesty their barrier (of defence) and not the wide world
kural.couplet: Unless the hedge of shame inviolate remain,For men of lofty soul the earth's vast realms no charms retain

kural.Translation: For shame their life the shame-sensed give Loss of shame they won't outlive
kural.explanation: The modest would rather lose their life for the sake of modesty than lose modesty for the sake of life
kural.couplet: The men of modest soul for shame would life an offering make,But ne'er abandon virtuous shame for life's dear sake

kural.Translation: Virtue is much ashamed of him Who shameless does what others shame
kural.explanation: Virtue is likely to forsake him who shamelessly does what others are ashamed of
kural.couplet: Though know'st no shame, while all around asha med must be:Virtue will shrink away ashamed of thee

kural.Translation: Lapse in manners injures the race Want of shame harms every good grace
kural.explanation: Want of manners injures one's family; but want of modesty injures one's character
kural.couplet: 'Twill race consume if right observance fail;'Twill every good consume if shamelessness prevail

kural.Translation: Movements of the shameless in heart Are string-led puppet show in fact
kural.explanation: The actions of those who are without modesty at heart are like those of puppet moved by a string
kural.couplet: 'Tis as with strings a wooden puppet apes life's functions, whenThose void of shame within hold intercourse with men

kural.Translation: No greatness is grander like Saying \"I shall work without slack\"
kural.explanation: There is no higher greatness than that of one saying I will not cease in my effort (to raise my family)
kural.couplet: Who says 'I'll do my work, nor slack my hand',His greatness, clothed with dignity supreme, shall stand

kural.Translation: These two exalt a noble home Ardent effort and ripe wisdom
kural.explanation: One's family is raised by untiring perseverance in both effort and wise contrivances
kural.couplet: The manly act and knowledge full, when these combineIn deed prolonged, then lengthens out the race's line

kural.Translation: When one resolves to raise his race Loin girt up God leads his ways
kural.explanation: The Deity will clothe itself and appear before him who resolves on raising his family
kural.couplet: 'I'll make my race renowned,' if man shall say,With vest succinct the goddess leads the way

kural.Translation: Who raise their races with ceaseless pain No need for plan; their ends will gain
kural.explanation: Those who are prompt in their efforts (to better their family) need no deliberation, such efforts will of themselves succeed
kural.couplet: Who labours for his race with unremitting pain,Without a thought spontaneously, his end will gain

kural.Translation: Who keeps his house without a blame People around, his kinship claim
kural.explanation: People will eagerly seek the friendship of the prosperous soul who has raised his family without foul means
kural.couplet: With blameless life who seeks to build his race's fame,The world shall circle him, and kindred claim

kural.Translation: Who raise their race which gave them birth Are deemed as men of manly worth
kural.explanation: A man's true manliness consists in making himself the head and benefactor of his family
kural.couplet: Of virtuous manliness the world accords the praiseTo him who gives his powers, the house from which he sprang to raise

kural.Translation: Like dauntless heroes in battle field The home-burden rests on the bold
kural.explanation: Amid his kindred so the burthen rests upon the strong
kural.couplet: The fearless hero bears the brunt amid the warrior throng;Amid his kindred so the burthen rests upon the strong

kural.Translation: No season have they who raise their race Sloth and pride will honour efface
kural.explanation: As a family suffers by (one's) indolence and false dignity there is to be so season (good or bad) to those who strive to raise their family
kural.couplet: Wait for no season, when you would your house uprear;'Twill perish, if you wait supine, or hold your honour dear

kural.Translation: Is not his frame a vase for woes Who from mishaps shields his house?
kural.explanation: Is it only to suffering that his body is exposed who undertakes to preserve his family from evil ?
kural.couplet: Is not his body vase that various sorrows fill,Who would his household screen from every ill

kural.Translation: A house will fall by a mishap With no good man to prop it up
kural.explanation: If there are none to prop up and maintain a family (in distress), it will fall at the stroke of the axe of misfortune
kural.couplet: When trouble the foundation saps the house must fall,If no strong hand be nigh to prop the tottering wall

kural.Translation: Farming though hard is foremost trade Men ply at will but ploughmen lead
kural.explanation: Agriculture, though laborious, is the most excellent (form of labour); for people, though they go about (in search of various employments), have at last to resort to the farmer
kural.couplet: Howe'er they roam, the world must follow still the plougher's team;Though toilsome, culture of the ground as noblest toil esteem

kural.Translation: Tillers are linch-pin of mankind Bearing the rest who cannot tend
kural.explanation: Agriculturists are (as it were) the linch-pin of the world for they support all other workers who cannot till the soil
kural.couplet: The ploughers are the linch-pin of the world; they bearThem up who other works perform, too weak its toils to share

kural.Translation: They live who live to plough and eat The rest behind them bow and eat
kural.explanation: They alone live who live by agriculture; all others lead a cringing, dependent life
kural.couplet: Who ploughing eat their food, they truly live:The rest to others bend subservient, eating what they give

kural.Translation: Who have the shade of cornful crest Under their umbra umbrellas rest
kural.explanation: Patriotic farmers desire to bring all other states under the control of their own king
kural.couplet: O'er many a land they 'll see their monarch reign,Whose fields are shaded by the waving grain

kural.Translation: Who till and eat, beg not; nought hide But give to those who are in need
kural.explanation: Those whose nature is to live by manual labour will never beg but give something to those who beg
kural.couplet: They nothing ask from others, but to askers give,Who raise with their own hands the food on which they live

kural.Translation: Should ploughmen sit folding their hands Desire-free monks too suffer wants
kural.explanation: If the farmer's hands are slackened, even the ascetic state will fail
kural.couplet: For those who 've left what all men love no place is found,When they with folded hands remain who till the ground

kural.Translation: Moulds dried to quarter-dust ensure Rich crops without handful manure
kural.explanation: If the land is dried so as to reduce one ounce of earth to a quarter, it will grow plentifully even without a handful of manure
kural.couplet: Reduce your soil to that dry state, When ounce is quarter-ounce's weight;Without one handful of manure, Abundant crops you thus secure

kural.Translation: Better manure than plough; then weed; Than irrigating, better guard
kural.explanation: Manuring is better than ploughing; after weeding, watching is better than watering (it)
kural.couplet: To cast manure is better than to plough;Weed well; to guard is more than watering now

kural.Translation: If landsmen sit sans moving about The field like wife will sulk and pout
kural.explanation: If the owner does not (personally) attend to his cultivation, his land will behave like an angry wife and yield him no pleasure
kural.couplet: When master from the field aloof hath stood;Then land will sulk, like wife in angry mood

kural.Translation: Fair good earth will laugh to see Idlers pleading poverty
kural.explanation: The maiden, Earth, will laugh at the sight of those who plead poverty and lead an idle life
kural.couplet: The earth, that kindly dame, will laugh to see,Men seated idle pleading poverty

kural.Translation: What gives more pain than scarcity? No pain pinches like poverty
kural.explanation: There is nothing that afflicts (one) like poverty
kural.couplet: You ask what sharper pain than poverty is known;Nothing pains more than poverty, save poverty alone

kural.Translation: The sinner Want is enemy dire Of joys of earth and heaven there
kural.explanation: When cruel poverty comes on, it deprives one of both the present and future (bliss)
kural.couplet: Malefactor matchless! poverty destroysThis world's and the next world's joys

kural.Translation: The craving itch of poverty Kills graceful words and ancestry
kural.explanation: Hankering poverty destroys at once the greatness of (one's) ancient descent and (the dignity of one's) speech
kural.couplet: Importunate desire, which poverty men name,Destroys both old descent and goodly fame

kural.Translation: Want makes even good familymen Utter words that are low and mean
kural.explanation: Even in those of high birth, poverty will produce the fault of uttering mean words
kural.couplet: From penury will spring, 'mid even those of noble race,Oblivion that gives birth to words that bring disgrace

kural.Translation: The pest of wanton poverty Brings a train of misery
kural.explanation: The misery of poverty brings in its train many (more) miseries
kural.couplet: From poverty, that grievous woe,Attendant sorrows plenteous grow

kural.Translation: The poor men's words are thrown away Though from heart good things they say
kural.explanation: The words of the poor are profitless, though they may be sound in thought and clear in expression
kural.couplet: Though deepest sense, well understood, the poor man's words convey,Their sense from memory of mankind will fade away

kural.Translation: Even the mother looks as stranger The poor devoid of character
kural.explanation: He that is reduced to absolute poverty will be regarded as a stranger even by his own mother
kural.couplet: From indigence devoid of virtue's grace,The mother e'en that bare, estranged, will turn her face

kural.Translation: The killing Want of yesterday Will it pester me even to-day?
kural.explanation: Is the poverty that almost killed me yesterday, to meet me today too ?
kural.couplet: And will it come today as yesterday,The grief of want that eats my soul away

kural.Translation: One may sleep in the midst of fire In want a wink of sleep is rare
kural.explanation: One may sleep in the midst of fire; but by no means in the midst of poverty
kural.couplet: Amid the flames sleep may men's eyelids close,In poverty the eye knows no repose

kural.Translation: Renounce their lives the poor must Or salt and gruel go to waste
kural.explanation: The destitute poor, who do not renounce their bodies, only consume their neighbour's salt and water
kural.couplet: Unless the destitute will utterly themselves deny,They cause their neighbour's salt and vinegar to die

kural.Translation: Demand from those who can supply Default is theirs when they deny
kural.explanation: If you meet with those that may be begged of, you may beg; (but) if they withhold (their gift) it is their blame and not yours
kural.couplet: When those you find from whom 'tis meet to ask,- for aid apply;Theirs is the sin, not yours, if they the gift deny

kural.Translation: Even demand becomes a joy When the things comes without annoy
kural.explanation: Even begging may be pleasant, if what is begged for is obtained without grief (to him that begs)
kural.couplet: Even to ask an alms may pleasure give,If what you ask without annoyance you receive

kural.Translation: Request has charm form open hearts Who know the duty on their part
kural.explanation: There is even a beauty in standing before and begging of those who are liberal in their gifts and understand their duty (to beggars)
kural.couplet: The men who nought deny, but know what's due, before their faceTo stand as suppliants affords especial grace

kural.Translation: Like giving even asking seems From those who hide not even in dreams
kural.explanation: To beg of such as never think of withholding (their charity) even in their dreams, is in fact the same as giving (it oneself);
kural.couplet: Like giving alms, may even asking pleasant seem,From men who of denial never even dream

kural.Translation: The needy demand for help because The world has men who don't refuse
kural.explanation: As there are in the world those that give without refusing, there are (also) those that prefer to beg by simply standing before them
kural.couplet: Because on earth the men exist, who never say them nay,Men bear to stand before their eyes for help to pray

kural.Translation: The pain of poverty shall die Before the free who don't deny
kural.explanation: All the evil of begging will be removed at the sight of those who are far from the evil of refusing
kural.couplet: It those you find from evil of 'denial' free,At once all plague of poverty will flee

kural.Translation: When givers without scorn impart A thrill of delight fills the heart
kural.explanation: Beggars rejoice exceedingly when they behold those who bestow (their alms) with kindness and courtesy
kural.couplet: If men are found who give and no harsh words of scorn employ,The minds of askers, through and through, will thrill with joy

kural.Translation: This grand cool world shall move to and fro Sans Askers like a puppet show
kural.explanation: If there were no beggars, (the actions done in) the cool wide world would only resemble the movement of a puppet
kural.couplet: If askers cease, the mighty earth, where cooling fountains flow,Will be a stage where wooden puppets come and go

kural.Translation: Where stands the glory of givers Without obligation seekers?
kural.explanation: What (praise) would there be to givers (of alms) if there were no beggars to ask for and reveive (them)
kural.couplet: What glory will there be to men of generous soul,When none are found to love the askers' role

kural.Translation: The needy should not scowl at \"No\" His need another's need must show * Saint valluvar talks of two kinds of Asking:() Asking help for public causes or enterprises () Begging when one is able to work and this is condemned
kural.explanation: He who begs ought not to be angry (at a refusal); for even the misery of (his own) poverty should be a sufficient reason (for so doing)
kural.couplet: Askers refused from wrath must stand aloof;The plague of poverty itself is ample proof

kural.Translation: Not to beg is billions worth E'en from eye-like friends who give with mirth
kural.explanation: Not to beg (at all) even from those excellent persons who cheerfully give without refusing, will do immense good
kural.couplet: Ten million-fold 'tis greater gain, asking no alms to live,Even from those, like eyes in worth, who nought concealing gladly give

kural.Translation: Let World-Maker loiter and rot If \"beg and live\" be human fate
kural.explanation: If the Creator of the world has decreed even begging as a means of livelihood, may he too go abegging and perish
kural.couplet: If he that shaped the world desires that men should begging go,Through life's long course, let him a wanderer be and perish so

kural.Translation: Nothing is hard like hard saying \"We end poverty by begging\"
kural.explanation: There is no greater folly than the boldness with which one seeks to remedy the evils of poverty by begging (rather than by working)
kural.couplet: Nothing is harder than the hardness that will say,'The plague of penury by asking alms we'll drive away.'

kural.Translation: All space is small before the great Who beg not e'en in want acute
kural.explanation: Even the whole world cannot sufficiently praise the dignity that would not beg even in the midst of destitution
kural.couplet: Who ne'er consent to beg in utmost need, their worthHas excellence of greatness that transcends the earth

kural.Translation: Though gruel thin, nothing is sweet Like the food earned by labour's sweat
kural.explanation: Even thin gruel is ambrosia to him who has obtained it by labour
kural.couplet: Nothing is sweeter than to taste the toil-won cheer,Though mess of pottage as tasteless as the water clear

kural.Translation: It may be water for the cow Begging tongue is mean anyhow
kural.explanation: There is nothing more disgraceful to one's tongue than to use it in begging water even for a cow
kural.couplet: E'en if a draught of water for a cow you ask,Nought's so distasteful to the tongue as beggar's task

kural.Translation: If beg they must I beg beggers Not to beg from shrinking misers
kural.explanation: I beseech all beggars and say, "If you need to beg, never beg of those who give unwillingly."
kural.couplet: One thing I beg of beggars all, 'If beg ye may,Of those who hide their wealth, beg not, I pray.'

kural.Translation: The hapless bark of beggary splits On the rock of refusing hits
kural.explanation: The unsafe raft of begging will split when it strikes on the rock of refusal
kural.couplet: The fragile bark of beggaryWrecked on denial's rock will lie

kural.Translation: The heart at thought of beggars melts; It dies at repulsing insults
kural.explanation: To think of (the evil of) begging is enough to melt one's heart; but to think of refusal is enough to break it
kural.couplet: The heart will melt away at thought of beggary,With thought of stern repulse 'twill perish utterly

kural.Translation: The word \"No\" kills the begger's life Where can the niggard's life be safe?
kural.explanation: Saying "No" to a beggar takes away his life. (but as that very word will kill the refuser) where then would the latter's life hide itself ?
kural.couplet: E'en as he asks, the shamefaced asker dies;Where shall his spirit hide who help denies

kural.Translation: The mean seem men only in form We have never seen such a sham
kural.explanation: The base resemble men perfectly (as regards form); and we have not seen such (exact) resemblance (among any other species)
kural.couplet: The base resemble men in outward form, I ween;But counterpart exact to them I've never seen

kural.Translation: The base seem richer than the good For no care enters their heart or head
kural.explanation: The low enjoy more felicity than those who know what is good; for the former are not troubled with anxiety (as to the good)
kural.couplet: Than those of grateful heart the base must luckier be,Their minds from every anxious thought are free

kural.Translation: The base are like gods; for they too As prompted by their desire do
kural.explanation: The base resemble the Gods; for the base act as they like
kural.couplet: The base are as the Gods; they tooDo ever what they list to do

kural.Translation: When the base meets a rake so vile Him he will exceed, exult and smile
kural.explanation: The base feels proud when he sees persons whose acts meaner than his own
kural.couplet: When base men those behold of conduct vile,They straight surpass them, and exulting smile

kural.Translation: Fear forms the conduct of the low Craving avails a bit below
kural.explanation: (The principle of) behaviour in the mean is chiefly fear; if not, hope of gain, to some extent
kural.couplet: Fear is the base man's virtue; if that fail,Intense desire some little may avail

kural.Translation: The base are like the beaten drum Since other's secrets they proclaim
kural.explanation: The base are like a drum that is beaten, for they unburden to others the secrets they have heard
kural.couplet: The base are like the beaten drum; for, when they hearThe sound the secret out in every neighbour's ear

kural.Translation: The base their damp hand will not shake But for fists clenched their jaws to break
kural.explanation: The mean will not (even) shake off (what sticks to) their hands (soon after a meal) to any but those who would break their jaws with their clenched fists
kural.couplet: From off their moistened hands no clinging grain they shake,Unless to those with clenched fist their jaws who break

kural.Translation: The good by soft words profits yield The cane-like base when crushed and killed
kural.explanation: The great bestow (their alms) as soon as they are informed; (but) the mean, like the sugar-cane, only when they are tortured to death
kural.couplet: The good to those will profit yield fair words who use;The base, like sugar-cane, will profit those who bruise

kural.Translation: Faults in others the mean will guess On seeing how they eat and dress
kural.explanation: The base will bring an evil (accusation) against others, as soon as he sees them (enjoying) good food
kural.couplet: If neighbours clothed and fed he see, the baseIs mighty man some hidden fault to trace

kural.Translation: The base hasten to sell themselves From doom to flit and nothing else
kural.explanation: The base will hasten to sell themselves as soon as a calamity has befallen them. For what else are they fitted ?
kural.couplet: For what is base man fit, if griefs assail?Himself to offer, there and then, for sale

kural.Translation: Is it an angel? A fair peacock Or jewelled belle? To my mind a shock!
kural.explanation: Is this jewelled female a celestial, a choice peahen, or a human being ? My mind is perplexed
kural.couplet: Goddess? or peafowl rare? She whose ears rich jewels wear,Is she a maid of human kind? All wildered is my mind

kural.Translation: The counter glances of this belle Are armied dart of the Love-Angel
kural.explanation: This female beauty returning my looks is like a celestial maiden coming with an army to contend against me
kural.couplet: She of the beaming eyes, To my rash look her glance replies,As if the matchless goddess' hand Led forth an armed band

kural.Translation: Not known before -I spy Demise In woman's guise with battling eyes
kural.explanation: I never knew before what is called Yama; I see it now; it is the eyes that carry on a great fight with (the help of) female qualities
kural.couplet: Death's form I formerly Knew not; but now 'tis plain to me;He comes in lovely maiden's guise, With soul-subduing eyes

kural.Translation: This artless dame has darting eyes That drink the life of men who gaze
kural.explanation: These eyes that seem to kill those who look at them are as it were in hostilities with this feminine simplicity
kural.couplet: In sweet simplicity, A woman's gracious form hath she;But yet those eyes, that drink my life, Are with the form at strife

kural.Translation: Is it death, eye or doe? All three In winsome woman's look I see
kural.explanation: Is it Yama, (a pair of) eyes or a hind ?- Are not all these three in the looks of this maid ?
kural.couplet: The light that on me gleams, Is it death's dart? or eye's bright beams?Or fawn's shy glance? All three appear In form of maiden here

kural.Translation: If cruel brows unbent, would screen Her eyes won't cause me trembling pain
kural.explanation: Her eyes will cause (me) no trembling sorrow, if they are properly hidden by her cruel arched eyebrows
kural.couplet: If cruel eye-brow's bow, Unbent, would veil those glances now;The shafts that wound this trembling heart Her eyes no more would dart

kural.Translation: Vest on the buxom breast of her Looks like rutting tusker's eye-cover
kural.explanation: The cloth that covers the firm bosom of this maiden is (like) that which covers the eyes of a rutting elephant
kural.couplet: As veil o'er angry eyes Of raging elephant that lies,The silken cincture's folds invest This maiden's panting breast

kural.Translation: Ah these fair brows shatter my might Feared by foemen yet to meet
kural.explanation: On her bright brow alone is destroyed even that power of mine that used to terrify the most fearless
kural.couplet: Ah woe is me my might, That awed my foemen in the fight,By lustre of that beaming brow Borne down, lies broken now

kural.Translation: Which jewel can add to her beauty With fawn-like looks and modesty?
kural.explanation: Of what use are other jewels to her who is adorned with modesty, and the meek looks of a hind ?
kural.couplet: Like tender fawn's her eye; Clothed on is she with modesty;What added beauty can be lent; By alien ornament

kural.Translation: To the drunk alone is wine delight Nothing delights like love at sight
kural.explanation: Unlike boiled honey which yields delight only when it is drunk, love gives pleasure even when looked at
kural.couplet: The palm-tree's fragrant wine, To those who taste yields joys divine;But love hath rare felicity For those that only see

kural.Translation: Her painted eyes, two glances dart One hurts; the other heals my heart
kural.explanation: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof
kural.couplet: A double witchery have glances of her liquid eye;One glance is glance that brings me pain; the other heals again

kural.Translation: Her furtive lightning glance is more Than enjoyment of sexual lore
kural.explanation: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace)
kural.couplet: The furtive glance, that gleams one instant bright,Is more than half of love's supreme delight

kural.Translation: She looked; looking bowed her head And love-plant was with water fed
kural.explanation: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love
kural.couplet: She looked, and looking drooped her head:On springing shoot of love 'its water shed

kural.Translation: I look; she droops to earth awhile I turn; she looks with gentle smile
kural.explanation: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently
kural.couplet: I look on her: her eyes are on the ground the while:I look away: she looks on me with timid smile

kural.Translation: No direct gaze; a side-long glance She darts at me and smiles askance
kural.explanation: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles
kural.couplet: She seemed to see me not; but yet the maidHer love, by smiling side-long glance, betrayed

kural.Translation: Their words at first seem an offence But quick we feel them friendly ones
kural.explanation: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood
kural.couplet: Though with their lips affection they disown,Yet, when they hate us not, 'tis quickly known

kural.Translation: Harsh little words; offended looks, Are feigned consenting love-lorn tricks
kural.explanation: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers
kural.couplet: The slighting words that anger feign, while eyes their love revealAre signs of those that love, but would their love conceal

kural.Translation: What a grace the slim maid has! As I look she slightly smiles
kural.explanation: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me
kural.couplet: I gaze, the tender maid relents the while;And, oh the matchless grace of that soft smile

kural.Translation: Between lovers we do discern A stranger's look of unconcern
kural.explanation: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers
kural.couplet: The look indifferent, that would its love disguise,Is only read aright by lovers' eyes

kural.Translation: The words of mouth are of no use When eye to eye agrees the gaze
kural.explanation: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers)
kural.couplet: When eye to answering eye reveals the tale of love,All words that lips can say must useless prove

kural.Translation: In this bangled beauty dwell The joys of sight sound touch taste smell
kural.explanation: The (simultaneous) enjoyment of the five senses of sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch can only be found with bright braceleted (women)
kural.couplet: All joys that senses five- sight, hearing, taste, smell, touch- can give,In this resplendent armlets-bearing damsel live

kural.Translation: The cure for ailment is somewhere For fair maid's ill she is the cure
kural.explanation: The remedy for a disease is always something different (from it); but for the disease caused by this jewelled maid, she is herself the cure
kural.couplet: Disease and medicine antagonists we surely see;This maid, to pain she gives, herself is remedy

kural.Translation: Is lotus-eyed lord's heaven so sweet As sleep in lover's arms so soft?
kural.explanation: Can the lotus-eyed Vishnu's heaven be indeed as sweet to those who delight to sleep in the delicate arms of their beloved ?
kural.couplet: Than rest in her soft arms to whom the soul is giv'n,Is any sweeter joy in his, the Lotus-eyed-one's heaven

kural.Translation: Away it burns and cools anear Wherefrom did she get this fire?
kural.explanation: From whence has she got this fire that burns when I withdraw and cools when I approach ?
kural.couplet: Withdraw, it burns; approach, it soothes the pain;Whence did the maid this wondrous fire obtain

kural.Translation: The arms of my flower-tressed maid Whatever I wish that that accord
kural.explanation: Each varied form of joy the soul can wish is found
kural.couplet: In her embrace, whose locks with flowery wreaths are bound,Each varied form of joy the soul can wish is found

kural.Translation: My simple maid has nectar arms Each embrace brings life-thrilling charms
kural.explanation: The shoulders of this fair one are made of ambrosia, for they revive me with pleasure every time I embrace them
kural.couplet: Ambrosia are the simple maiden's arms; when I attainTheir touch, my withered life puts forth its buds again

kural.Translation: Ah the embrace of this fair dame Is like sharing one's food at home
kural.explanation: The embraces of a gold-complexioned beautiful female are as pleasant as to dwell in one's own house and live by one's own (earnings) after distributing (a portion of it in charity)
kural.couplet: As when one eats from household store, with kindly graceSharing his meal: such is this golden maid's embrace

kural.Translation: Joy is the fast embrace that doth Not admit e'en air between both
kural.explanation: To ardent lovers sweet is the embrace that cannot be penetrated even by a breath of breeze
kural.couplet: Sweet is the strict embrace of those whom fond affection binds,Where no dissevering breath of discord entrance finds

kural.Translation: Sulking, feeling and clasping fast These three are sweets of lover's tryst
kural.explanation: Love quarrel, reconciliation and intercourse - these are the advantages reaped by those who marry for lust
kural.couplet: The jealous variance, the healing of the strife, reunion gained:These are the fruits from wedded love obtained

kural.Translation: As knowledge reveals past ignorance So is the belle as love gets close
kural.explanation: As (one's) ignorance is discovered the more one learns, so does repeated intercourse with a welladorned female (only create a desire for more)
kural.couplet: The more men learn, the more their lack of learning they detect;'Tis so when I approach the maid with gleaming jewels decked

kural.Translation: Soft blessed anicha flower, hail On whom I dote is softer still
kural.explanation: May you flourish, O Anicham! you have a delicate nature But my beloved is more delicate than you
kural.couplet: O flower of the sensitive plant! than theeMore tender's the maiden beloved by me

kural.Translation: You can't liken flowers by many eyed, To her bright eyes, O mind dismayed
kural.explanation: O my soul, fancying that flowers which are seen by many can resemble her eyes, you become confused at the sight of them
kural.couplet: You deemed, as you saw the flowers, her eyes were as flowers, my soul,That many may see; it was surely some folly that over you stole

kural.Translation: The bamboo-shouldered has pearl-like smiles Fragrant breath and lance-like eyes
kural.explanation: The complexion of this bamboo-shouldered one is that of a shoot; her teeth, are pearls; her breath,
kural.couplet: As tender shoot her frame; teeth, pearls; around her odours blend;Darts are the eyes of her whose shoulders like the bambu bend

kural.Translation: Lily droops down to ground and says I can't equal the jewelled-one's eyes
kural.explanation: If the blue lotus could see, it would stoop and look at the ground saying, "I can never resemble the eyes of this excellent jewelled one."
kural.couplet: The lotus, seeing her, with head demiss, the ground would eye,And say, 'With eyes of her, rich gems who wears, we cannot vie.'

kural.Translation: Anicha flower with stem she wears To her breaking waist sad-drum-blares!
kural.explanation: No merry drums will be beaten for the (tender) waist of her who has adorned herself with the anicham without having removed its stem
kural.couplet: The flowers of the sensitive plant as a girdle around her she placed;The stems she forgot to nip off; they 'll weigh down the delicate waist

kural.Translation: Stars are confused to know which is The moon and which is woman's face
kural.explanation: The stars have become confused in their places not being able to distinguish between the moon and the maid's countenance
kural.couplet: The stars perplexed are rushing wildly from their spheres;For like another moon this maiden's face appears

kural.Translation: Are there spots on the lady's face Just as in moon that changes phase?
kural.explanation: Could there be spots in the face of this maid like those in the bright full moon ?
kural.couplet: In moon, that waxing waning shines, as sports appear,Are any spots discerned in face of maiden here

kural.Translation: Like my lady's face if you shine All my love to you; hail O moon!
kural.explanation: If you can indeed shine like the face of women, flourish, O moon, for then would you be worth loving ?
kural.couplet: Farewell, O moon! If that thine orb could shineBright as her face, thou shouldst be love of mine

kural.Translation: Like the face of my flower-eyed one If you look, then shine alone O moon!
kural.explanation: O moon, if you wish to resemble the face of her whose eyes are like (these) flowers, do not appear so as to be seen by all
kural.couplet: If as her face, whose eyes are flowers, thou wouldst have charms for me,Shine for my eyes alone, O moon, shine not for all to see

kural.Translation: The soft flower and the swan's down are Like nettles to the feet of the fair
kural.explanation: The anicham and the feathers of the swan are to the feet of females, like the fruit of the (thorny) Nerunji
kural.couplet: The flower of the sensitive plant, and the down on the swan's white breast,As the thorn are harsh, by the delicate feet of this maiden pressed

kural.Translation: Like milk and honey the dew is sweet From her white teeth whose word is soft
kural.explanation: The water which oozes from the white teeth of this soft speeched damsel is like a mixture of milk and honey
kural.couplet: The dew on her white teeth, whose voice is soft and low,Is as when milk and honey mingled flow

kural.Translation: Love between me and this lady Is like bond between soul and body
kural.explanation: The love between me and this damsel is like the union of body and soul
kural.couplet: Between this maid and me the friendship kindIs as the bonds that soul and body bind

kural.Translation: Depart image in my pupil Giving room to my fair-browed belle!
kural.explanation: O you image in the pupil (of my eye)! depart; there is no room for (my) fair-browed beloved
kural.couplet: For her with beauteous brow, the maid I love, there place is none;To give her image room, O pupil of mine eye, begone

kural.Translation: Life with my jewel is existence Death it is her severance
kural.explanation: My fair-jewelled one resembles the living soul (when she is in union with me), the dying soul when she leaves me
kural.couplet: Life is she to my very soul when she draws nigh;Dissevered from the maid with jewels rare, I die

kural.Translation: Can I forget? I recall always The charms of her bright battling eyes
kural.explanation: If I had forgotten her who has bright battling eyes, I would have remembered (thee); but I never forget her (Thus says he to her maid)
kural.couplet: I might recall, if I could once forget; but from my heartHer charms fade not, whose eyes gleam like the warrior's dart

kural.Translation: So subtle is my lover's form Ever in my eyes winking, no harm
kural.explanation: My lover would not depart from mine eyes; even if I wink, he would not suffer (from pain); he is so ethereal
kural.couplet: My loved one's subtle form departs not from my eyes;I wink them not, lest I should pain him where he lies

kural.Translation: My lover in my eyes abides I paint them not lest he hides
kural.explanation: As my lover abides in my eyes, I will not even paint them, for he would (then) have to conceal himself
kural.couplet: My love doth ever in my eyes reside;I stain them not, fearing his form to hide

kural.Translation: My lover abides in my heart I fear hot food lest he feels hot
kural.explanation: As my lover is in my heart, I am afraid of eating (anything) hot, for I know it would pain him
kural.couplet: Within my heart my lover dwells; from food I turnThat smacks of heat, lest he should feel it burn

kural.Translation: My eyes wink not lest he should hide And him as cruel the townsmen chide
kural.explanation: I will not wink, knowing that if I did, my lover would hide himself; and for this reason, this town says, he is unloving
kural.couplet: I fear his form to hide, nor close my eyes:'Her love estranged is gone!' the village cries

kural.Translation: He abides happy in my heart But people mistake he is apart
kural.explanation: My lover dwells in my heart with perpetual delight; but the town says he is unloving and (therefore) dwells afar
kural.couplet: Rejoicing in my very soul he ever lies;'Her love estranged is gone far off!' the village cries

kural.Translation: Pangs of passion find no recourse Except riding *`palmyra horse' * Palmyra horse or 'Madal' is a torture expressive of the burning passion of the lover to the beloved The lover's body is laid on a rough pricking palmyra bed and he is carried along the street with songs of love pangs The parents of the lovers first reproach them and then consent to their marriage
kural.explanation: To those who after enjoyment of sexual pleasure suffer (for want of more), there is no help so efficient as the palmyra horse
kural.couplet: To those who 've proved love's joy, and now afflicted mourn,Except the helpful 'horse of palm', no other strength remains

kural.Translation: Pining body and mind lose shame And take to riding of the palm
kural.explanation: Having got rid of shame, the suffering body and soul save themselves on the palmyra horse
kural.couplet: My body and my soul, that can no more endure,Will lay reserve aside, and mount the 'horse of palm'

kural.Translation: Once I was modest and manly My love has now Madal only
kural.explanation: Modesty and manliness were once my own; now, my own is the palmyra horse that is ridden by the lustful
kural.couplet: I once retained reserve and seemly manliness;To-day I nought possess but lovers' 'horse of palm'

kural.Translation: Rushing flood of love sweeps away The raft of shame and firmness, aye!
kural.explanation: The raft of modesty and manliness, is, alas, carried-off by the strong current of lust
kural.couplet: Love's rushing tide will sweep away the raftOf seemly manliness and shame combined

kural.Translation: Palm-ride and pangs of eventide Are gifts of wreath-like bracelet maid
kural.explanation: She with the small garland-like bracelets has given me the palmyra horse and the sorrow that is endured at night
kural.couplet: The maid that slender armlets wears, like flowers entwined,Has brought me 'horse of palm,' and pangs of eventide

kural.Translation: Madal I ride at midnight for My eyes sleep not seeing this fair
kural.explanation: Mine eyes will not close in sleep on your mistress's account; even at midnight will I think of mounting the palmyra horse
kural.couplet: Of climbing 'horse of palm' in midnight hour, I think;My eyes know no repose for that same simple maid

kural.Translation: Her sea-like lust seeks not Madal! Serene is woman's self control
kural.explanation: There is nothing so noble as the womanly nature that would not ride the palmyra horse, though plunged a sea of lust
kural.couplet: There's nought of greater worth than woman's long-enduring soul,Who, vexed by love like ocean waves, climbs not the 'horse of palm'

kural.Translation: Lust betrays itself in haste Though women are highly soft and chaste
kural.explanation: Even the Lust (of women) transgresses its secrecy and appears in public, forgetting that they are too chaste and liberal (to be overcome by it)
kural.couplet: In virtue hard to move, yet very tender, too, are we;Love deems not so, would rend the veil, and court publicity

kural.Translation: My perplexed love roves public street Believing that none knows its secret
kural.explanation: And thus, in public ways, perturbed will rove
kural.couplet: 'There's no one knows my heart,' so says my love,And thus, in public ways, perturbed will rove

kural.Translation: Fools laugh at me before my eyes For they feel not my pangs and sighs
kural.explanation: Even strangers laugh (at us) so as to be seen by us, for they have not suffered
kural.couplet: Before my eyes the foolish make a mock of me,Because they ne'er endured the pangs I now must drie

kural.Translation: Rumour sustains my existence Good luck! many know not its sense
kural.explanation: My precious life is saved by the raise of rumour, and this, to my good luck no others are aware of
kural.couplet: By this same rumour's rise, my precious life stands fast;Good fortune grant the many know this not

kural.Translation: Rumour gives me the flower-like belle People know not what rare angel
kural.explanation: Not knowing the value of her whose eyes are like flowers this town has got up a rumour about me
kural.couplet: The village hath to us this rumour giv'n, that makes her mine;Unweeting all the rareness of the maid with flower-like eyne

kural.Translation: I profit by this public rumour Having not, I feel, I have her
kural.explanation: Will I not get a rumour that is known to the (whole) town ? For what I have not got is as if I had got it (already)
kural.couplet: The rumour spread within the town, is it not gain to me?It is as though that were obtained that may not be

kural.Translation: Rumour inflames the love I seek Or else it becomes bleak and weak
kural.explanation: Rumour increases the violence of my passion; without it it would grow weak and waste away
kural.couplet: The rumour rising makes my love to rise;My love would lose its power and languish otherwise

kural.Translation: Drink delights as liquor flows Love delights as rumour grows
kural.explanation: As drinking liquor is delightful (to one) whenever one is in mirth, so is lust delightful to me whenever it is the subject of rumour
kural.couplet: The more man drinks, the more he ever drunk would be;The more my love's revealed, the sweeter 'tis to me

kural.Translation: One lasting day we met alone Lasting rumours eclipse our moon
kural.explanation: It was but a single day that I looked on (my lover); but the rumour thereof has spread like the seizure of the moon by the serpent
kural.couplet: I saw him but one single day: rumour spreads soonAs darkness, when the dragon seizes on the moon

kural.Translation: Scandal manures; mother's refrain Waters the growth of this love-pain
kural.explanation: This malady (of lust) is manured by the talk of women and watered by the (harsh) words of my mother
kural.couplet: My anguish grows apace: the town's reportManures it; my mother's word doth water it

kural.Translation: To quench the lust by rumour free Is to quench fire by pouring ghee
kural.explanation: To say that one could extinguish passion by rumour is like extinguishing fire with ghee
kural.couplet: With butter-oil extinguish fire! 'Twill proveHarder by scandal to extinguish love

kural.Translation: Who said \"fear not\" flared up rumour Why then should I blush this clamour?
kural.explanation: When the departure of him who said "fear not" has put me to shame before others, why need I be ashamed of scandal
kural.couplet: When he who said 'Fear not!' hath left me blamed,While many shrink, can I from rumour hide ashamed

kural.Translation: Town raising this cry, I desire Consent is easy from my sire
kural.explanation: The rumour I desire is raised by the town (itself); and my lover would if desired consent (to my following him)
kural.couplet: If we desire, who loves will grant what we require;This town sends forth the rumour we desire

kural.Translation: Tell me if you but do not leave, Your quick return to those who live
kural.explanation: If it is not departure, tell me; but if it is your speedy return, tell it to those who would be alive then
kural.couplet: If you will say, 'I leave thee not,' then tell me so;Of quick return tell those that can survive this woe

kural.Translation: His sight itself was pleasing, near Embrace pains now by partings fear
kural.explanation: His very look was once pleasing; but (now) even intercourse is painful through fear of separation
kural.couplet: It once was perfect joy to look upon his face;But now the fear of parting saddens each embrace

kural.Translation: On whom shall I lay my trust hence While parting lurks in knowing ones?
kural.explanation: As even the lover who understands (everything) may at times depart, confidence is hardly possible
kural.couplet: To trust henceforth is hard, if ever he depart,E'en he, who knows his promise and my breaking heart

kural.Translation: He parts whose love told me -fear not Is my trust in him at default?
kural.explanation: If he who bestowed his love and said "fear not" should depart, will it be the fault of those who believed in (his) assuring words ?
kural.couplet: If he depart, who fondly said, 'Fear not,' what blame's incurredBy those who trusted to his reassuring word

kural.Translation: Stop his parting -my life to save Meeting is rare if he would leave
kural.explanation: If you would save (my life), delay the departure of my destined (husband); for if he departs, intercourse will become impossible
kural.couplet: If you would guard my life, from going him restrainWho fills my life! If he depart, hardly we meet again

kural.Translation: His hardness says, \"I leave you now\" Is there hope of his renewed love?
kural.explanation: Is hard, when he could stand, and of departure speak to me
kural.couplet: To cherish longing hope that he should ever gracious be,Is hard, when he could stand, and of departure speak to me

kural.Translation: Will not my gliding bangles' cry The parting of my lord betray?
kural.explanation: Do not the rings that begin to slide down my fingers forebode the separation of my lord ?
kural.couplet: The bracelet slipping from my wrist announced beforeDeparture of the Prince that rules the ocean shore

kural.Translation: Bitter is life in friendless place; Worse is parting love's embrace!
kural.explanation: Painful is it to live in a friendless town; but far more painful is it to part from one's lover
kural.couplet: 'Tis sad to sojourn in the town where no kind kinsmen dwell;'Tis sadder still to bid a friend beloved farewell

kural.Translation: Can fire that burns by touch burn like Parting of the hearts love-sick?
kural.explanation: Fire burns when touched; but, like the sickness of love, can it also burn when removed ?
kural.couplet: Fire burns the hands that touch; but smart of loveWill burn in hearts that far away remove

kural.Translation: Many survive pangs of parting Not I this sore so distressing
kural.explanation: As if there were many indeed that can consent to the impossible, kill their pain, endure separation and yet continue to live afterwards
kural.couplet: Sorrow's sadness meek sustaining, Driving sore distress away,Separation uncomplaining Many bear the livelong day

kural.Translation: It swells out like baled out spring How to bear this pain so writhing?
kural.explanation: I would hide this pain from others; but it (only) swells like a spring to those who drain it
kural.couplet: I would my pain conceal, but see! it surging swells,As streams to those that draw from ever-springing wells

kural.Translation: I can't conceal this nor complain For shame to him who caused this pain
kural.explanation: I cannot conceal this pain, nor can I relate it without shame to him who has caused it
kural.couplet: I cannot hide this pain of mine, yet shame restrainsWhen I would tell it out to him who caused my pains

kural.Translation: In life -poles of this wearied frame Are poised the weights of lust and shame
kural.explanation: (Both) lust and shame, with my soul for their shoulder pole balance themselves on a body that cannot bear them
kural.couplet: My soul, like porter's pole, within my wearied frame,Sustains a two-fold burthen poised, of love and shame

kural.Translation: My lust is a sea; I do not see A raft to go across safely
kural.explanation: There is indeed a flood of lust; but there is no raft of safety to cross it with
kural.couplet: A sea of love, 'tis true, I see stretched out before,But not the trusty bark that wafts to yonder shore

kural.Translation: What wilt they prove when they are foes Who in friendship bring me woes!
kural.explanation: What will they prove when angry tempests lower?
kural.couplet: Who work us woe in friendship's trustful hour,What will they prove when angry tempests lower

kural.Translation: The pleasure in love is oceanful But its pangs are more painful
kural.explanation: The pleasure of lust is (as great as) the sea; but the pain of lust is far greater
kural.couplet: A happy love 's sea of joy; but mightier sorrows rollFrom unpropitious love athwart the troubled soul

kural.Translation: Wild waves of love I swim shoreless Pining alone in midnight hush
kural.explanation: I have swam across the terrible flood of lust, but have not seen its shore; even at midnight I am alone; still I live
kural.couplet: I swim the cruel tide of love, and can no shore descry,In watches of the night, too, 'mid the waters, only I

kural.Translation: Night's mercy lulls all souls to sleep Keeping but me for companionship
kural.explanation: The night which graciously lulls to sleep all living creatures, has me alone for her companion
